title_en: Presidents Macron and Tshisekedi to Meet in Paris, February 24, 2026
excerpt_en: PARIS February 24, 2026 - French President Emmanuel Macron is scheduled to meet with Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi in Paris on Wednesday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts addressing the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC. The two leaders last met on January 23,
body_en:
PARIS February 24, 2026 - French President Emmanuel Macron is scheduled to meet with Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi in Paris on Wednesday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts addressing the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC.
The two leaders last met on January 23, 2026, at the Élysée Palace, during which discussions centered on the humanitarian situation in eastern DRC and bilateral cooperation between France and the DRC.
On February 14, France welcomed Tshisekedi’s commitment to implement a ceasefire proposed by Angola for all warring parties in the Great Lakes region. French authorities also stressed the importance of implementing the Washington Agreement of December 4, 2025, calling on all stakeholders to respect their obligations.
French diplomacy reaffirmed its dedication to ensuring that peace momentum generated by the Washington Agreement, the Doha Framework Agreement of November 15, 2025, and African Union initiatives translates into tangible improvements in the lives of civilians in eastern DRC.
France also highlighted its role in monitoring the humanitarian response, citing the visit of Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Acting Head of MONUSCO, to Goma from February 12-14, 2026. This visit prepared UN support for ceasefire verification and monitoring in line with UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025).
“The first flight to Goma airport represents a critical step toward resuming small-scale, daytime humanitarian flights. France calls on all parties to collaborate to ensure continued humanitarian access for the benefit of the population,” the French Foreign Ministry stated.

title: Seth Kikuni Rejects Dialogue Without Preconditions

title_en: Seth Kikuni Rejects Dialogue Without Preconditions
excerpt_en: KINSHASA February 26, 2026 - In exile since mid-January, opposition leader Seth Kikuni stressed that any national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo cannot be credible in a context of repression. Responding to Martin Fayulu, who had proposed topics for discussion, Kikun
body_en:
KINSHASA February 26, 2026 - In exile since mid-January, opposition leader Seth Kikuni stressed that any national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo cannot be credible in a context of repression. Responding to Martin Fayulu, who had proposed topics for discussion, Kikuni called for clear prerequisites, including a ceasefire and the cessation of all forms of political repression.
“The opposition will not engage in dialogue unless it is based on clear, credible, and verifiable preconditions,” wrote Kikuni on X, emphasizing that dialogue in a context of injustice, intimidation, and deprivation of fundamental rights risks legitimizing the status quo.
Among Kikuni’s preconditions for an inclusive dialogue are:
Release of political prisoners and prisoners of conscience
Lifting of politically motivated convictions
Restoration of civil and political rights, including the return of passports and freedom of movement for political actors
Annulment of politically motivated legal proceedings and lifting of arrest warrants
Reparations for damages suffered
Martin Fayulu, meanwhile, has called for a dialogue giving voice to all segments of society, including armed groups, outlining seven essential discussion points:
Preservation of DRC sovereignty and army/security reforms
Promotion of ethical governance, public finance reform, and anti-corruption measures
Strengthening justice, human rights, and equality before the law
Electoral reforms to ensure transparency for the 2028 elections
Peaceful coexistence among Congolese ethnic groups
Regional stability in the Great Lakes region
Review and analysis of past national dialogue resolutions since 1958 to develop a coherent governance doctrine
Kikuni and other opposition leaders insist that participation criteria must ensure tangible benefits for the Congolese people, rejecting any dialogue reduced to a mere political exercise.

title: DRC Nominates Juliana Lumumba for Secretary General of La Francophonie
excerpt: KINSHASA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has officially nominated Juliana Amato Lumumba, daughter of independence hero Patrice Emery Lumumba, as its candidate for Secretary General of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF). A political
title_en: DRC Nominates Juliana Lumumba for Secretary General of La Francophonie
excerpt_en: KINSHASA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has officially nominated Juliana Amato Lumumba, daughter of independence hero Patrice Emery Lumumba, as its candidate for Secretary General of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF). A political
body_en:
KINSHASA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has officially nominated Juliana Amato Lumumba, daughter of independence hero Patrice Emery Lumumba, as its candidate for Secretary General of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF).
A political science graduate from Paris and a prominent figure in Congolese public life, Lumumba brings over 30 years of experience in governance, cultural diplomacy, and international cooperation. She has held key positions in the Congolese government, including Deputy Minister and Minister of Culture (1997-2001), and has extensive entrepreneurial experience in consulting, communications, and international trade. From 2007 to 2015, she served as Secretary General of the Union of African Chambers of Commerce (UACCIAP), contributing to continental economic integration.
According to Crispin Mbadu, Minister Delegate responsible for Francophonie and the Congolese Diaspora, Lumumba’s candidacy reflects the DRC’s desire to promote a modern, inclusive, and people-centered Francophonie, highlighting her leadership, pan-African expertise, cultural diplomacy, commitment to women’s empowerment, and fluency in multiple languages, including French, Arabic, English, Lingala, and Swahili.
Her nomination comes amid a diplomatic contest with Rwanda, as current OIF Secretary General Louise Mushikiwabo seeks a third term. The DRC intends to submit Lumumba’s candidacy before June 2026.
The selection was reinforced by recent diplomatic engagement with France, including the February 2 visit of French Minister Delegate for Francophonie Éléonore Caroit to Kinshasa and the February 25 meeting in Paris between Presidents Emmanuel Macron and Félix Tshisekedi, emphasizing the DRC’s strategic role in the future of the Francophone space in Africa.
The DRC government stated that Lumumba’s vision, combined with her extensive public service and international experience, positions her as a candidate capable of strengthening solidarity, promoting diversity, and fostering development across Francophone countries.

title: President Tshisekedi Orders Review of Council of Ministers Decisions to Strengthen Government Action
excerpt: KINSHASA March 1, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has instructed Prime Minister Judith Suminwa to conduct a comprehensive review of all presidential instructions issued during Council of Ministers meetings, amid concerns over the non-implementation of key decisions. Since takin
title_en: President Tshisekedi Orders Review of Council of Ministers Decisions to Strengthen Government Action
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 1, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has instructed Prime Minister Judith Suminwa to conduct a comprehensive review of all presidential instructions issued during Council of Ministers meetings, amid concerns over the non-implementation of key decisions. Since takin
body_en:
KINSHASA March 1, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has instructed Prime Minister Judith Suminwa to conduct a comprehensive review of all presidential instructions issued during Council of Ministers meetings, amid concerns over the non-implementation of key decisions.
Since taking office, President Tshisekedi has designated Fridays for Council of Ministers sessions, during which presidential instructions are given, texts adopted, and government members present proposals for their sectors. However, several instructions have reportedly remained unimplemented or inadequately addressed, raising concerns over governmental accountability and efficiency.
At the 80th Council of Ministers meeting held at the African Union City complex, President Tshisekedi emphasized that the proper execution of these instructions is crucial for good governance, the credibility of public action, and state effectiveness. He stressed the need for results that are concrete, measurable, verifiable, and tangible for citizens, warning that failure to implement directives cannot be tolerated.
The comprehensive review, led by Prime Minister Suminwa with support from her office and the Presidency, will systematically assess individual and institutional performance, identify gaps, and propose corrective measures to ensure optimal government functioning aligned with national priorities.
The president cited specific examples, including the creation of 53 institutions during his first five-year term, noted by former Finance Minister Nicolas Kazadi, which require evaluation to determine whether they should be streamlined or restructured for efficiency.
This initiative is seen as a timely effort to reinforce discipline, accountability, and performance within the government, with the objective of delivering tangible improvements for the Congolese population and restoring confidence in public administration.

excerpt: ARUSHA March 2, 2026 - The East African Community (EAC) is set to hold its 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government on Saturday, March 7, 2026, in Arusha, Tanzania, under the theme “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens.” The summit a
title_en: EAC Heads of State to Meet Amid Ongoing Security Crisis in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: ARUSHA March 2, 2026 - The East African Community (EAC) is set to hold its 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government on Saturday, March 7, 2026, in Arusha, Tanzania, under the theme “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens.” The summit a
body_en:
ARUSHA March 2, 2026 - The East African Community (EAC) is set to hold its 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government on Saturday, March 7, 2026, in Arusha, Tanzania, under the theme “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens.” The summit aims to advance regional integration, review institutional reports, and launch key initiatives, including the EAC Customs Guarantee and the 7th Development Strategy (2026/27-2030/31).
The meeting will also address governance matters, including the appointment of a new Secretary-General, judges to the East African Court of Justice, renewal of Deputy Secretaries-General, appointments to the EAC Competition Authority, and ratification of draft laws from the East African Legislative Assembly.
However, the summit occurs amid persistent security tensions in eastern DRC, where clashes continue between the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) and AFC/M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda. Diplomatic strains between Kinshasa and Kigali remain high despite the Washington and Doha peace processes, complicating regional stabilization efforts.
Kinshasa also maintains a strained relationship with the EAC, perceiving insufficient engagement or balance from the regional bloc. This tension traces back to the 24th EAC Summit in November 2024, which President Félix Tshisekedi did not attend, and the ineffectiveness of the EAC Regional Force (EACRF), whose mandate expired in December 2023 without renewal. Frustrated by the inability of the EACRF to neutralize armed groups, the DRC has increasingly sought collaboration with SADC forces, following the withdrawal of its troops from Goma amid rebel advances.
Despite these challenges, the EAC remains a central actor in regional stability and integration. Observers are closely watching how the Kenyan presidency under President William Ruto will address the security crisis in eastern DRC and restore confidence in the Community’s role in regional peace and economic integration.

title: Senate Petition Targets Modeste Bahati Lukwebo Over Opposition to Constitutional Revision
excerpt: KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - Just a day after publicly opposing a proposed constitutional revision championed by President Félix Tshisekedi and the Sacred Union of the Nation, Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, Second Vice-President of the Senate and head of AFDC-A, has become the target of a f
title_en: Senate Petition Targets Modeste Bahati Lukwebo Over Opposition to Constitutional Revision
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - Just a day after publicly opposing a proposed constitutional revision championed by President Félix Tshisekedi and the Sacred Union of the Nation, Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, Second Vice-President of the Senate and head of AFDC-A, has become the target of a f
body_en:
KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - Just a day after publicly opposing a proposed constitutional revision championed by President Félix Tshisekedi and the Sacred Union of the Nation, Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, Second Vice-President of the Senate and head of AFDC-A, has become the target of a formal petition in the upper house of Parliament.
The initiative, led by Senator Dany Kabongo Bondanya, criticizes Bahati Lukwebo’s remarks as “completely inappropriate” and disrespectful to the President, particularly given his prominent role in both the Senate and the Sacred Union presidium. Kabongo emphasized that Bahati Lukwebo should have consulted the President, described as the “moral authority” of the Sacred Union, before expressing his personal opposition.
During a press conference on March 4, Bahati Lukwebo had dismissed the debate over changing the Constitution as false and politically motivated, arguing that the real issue lies in the failure to implement the existing law, not the law itself. He called for political actors to focus on practical governance for the benefit of the Congolese people rather than pursuing constitutional amendments.
The petition reflects growing tensions within the Sacred Union, with high-ranking figures such as Déo Bizibu, Secretary General of the UDPS, publicly criticizing Bahati Lukwebo’s stance as contrary to the coalition’s vision. Kabongo Bondanya promised a detailed statement outlining the grounds for possible removal from office ahead of the March parliamentary session.
This unfolding dispute underscores the heightened political sensitivity in the DRC surrounding potential constitutional reforms and the balancing of authority between the President and senior members of the ruling coalition.

KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - Just a day after publicly opposing a proposed constitutional revision championed by President Félix Tshisekedi and the Sacred Union of the Nation, Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, Second Vice-President of the Senate and head of AFDC-A, has become the target of a formal petition in the upper house of Parliament.
The initiative, led by Senator Dany Kabongo Bondanya, criticizes Bahati Lukwebo’s remarks as “completely inappropriate” and disrespectful to the President, particularly given his prominent role in both the Senate and the Sacred Union presidium. Kabongo emphasized that Bahati Lukwebo should have consulted the President, described as the “moral authority” of the Sacred Union, before expressing his personal opposition.
During a press conference on March 4, Bahati Lukwebo had dismissed the debate over changing the Constitution as false and politically motivated, arguing that the real issue lies in the failure to implement the existing law, not the law itself. He called for political actors to focus on practical governance for the benefit of the Congolese people rather than pursuing constitutional amendments.
The petition reflects growing tensions within the Sacred Union, with high-ranking figures such as Déo Bizibu, Secretary General of the UDPS, publicly criticizing Bahati Lukwebo’s stance as contrary to the coalition’s vision. Kabongo Bondanya promised a detailed statement outlining the grounds for possible removal from office ahead of the March parliamentary session.

title: 25th Summit Opens in Arusha Without DRC’s Tshisekedi or Rwanda’s Kagame
excerpt: ARUSHA, Tanzania March 7, 2026 - The 25th Ordinary Summit of the East African Community (EAC) opened today in Arusha under the theme, “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens,” despite notable absences, including DRC President Félix Tshisekedi and R
title_en: 25th Summit Opens in Arusha Without DRC’s Tshisekedi or Rwanda’s Kagame
excerpt_en: ARUSHA, Tanzania March 7, 2026 - The 25th Ordinary Summit of the East African Community (EAC) opened today in Arusha under the theme, “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens,” despite notable absences, including DRC President Félix Tshisekedi and R
body_en:
ARUSHA, Tanzania March 7, 2026 - The 25th Ordinary Summit of the East African Community (EAC) opened today in Arusha under the theme, “Deepening Integration to Improve the Living Conditions of EAC Citizens,” despite notable absences, including DRC President Félix Tshisekedi and Rwandan President Paul Kagame.
Ahead of the summit, the EAC Council of Ministers met from March 2 to 5 to review progress on previous decisions, prepare key agenda items, and formulate recommendations for the heads of state. The summit agenda includes reviewing the Council’s report covering November 30, 2024, to December 31, 2025, implementing the 24th Summit directive on sustainable financing of the EAC budget, assessing the integration status of partner states admitted between 2016 and 2024, appointing a new Secretary-General, judges to the East African Court of Justice, renewing Deputy Secretaries-General mandates, appointing commissioners to the EAC Competition Authority, and approving draft laws from the East African Legislative Assembly.
Several heads of state were present, including Yoweri Museveni (Uganda), Évariste Ndayishimiye (Burundi and current African Union Chairperson), and William Ruto (Kenya and current EAC Chairperson). South Sudan’s President Salva Kiir was represented by his foreign minister, Semaya Kumba, while Somalia’s Hassan Sheikh Mohamud was expected to arrive later.
Both Tshisekedi and Kagame delegated representatives-DRC’s Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni Isiloketshi and Rwanda’s Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva, respectively. Tshisekedi’s absence was due to attending the funeral of Reverend Jesse Jackson in the United States. The absence of the two leaders highlights ongoing tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali over accusations of support for armed groups, including Rwanda’s alleged backing of the AFC/M23 rebellion and the DRC’s criticism of Kigali for supporting these rebels.
The summit coincides with escalating security challenges in eastern DRC, where government forces continue to confront the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23. Diplomatic friction between the DRC and Rwanda persists despite efforts under the Washington and Doha frameworks. Observers note a broader sense of unease between Kinshasa and the EAC, fueled by perceptions that the DRC is distanced from regional decision-making and that the bloc is not fully engaged in resolving the eastern DRC security crisis.
The 25th Summit thus opens in a complex regional context, with integration, security, and diplomatic reconciliation as key tests for the EAC and its member states.

excerpt: CHICAGO, USA March 6, 2026 - Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi attended the funeral of civil rights icon Reverend Jesse Jackson in Chicago on Friday, paying tribute to the late activist whose lifelong commitment to racial equality and social justice left a profound mark global
title_en: Félix Tshisekedi Attends Funeral of Civil Rights Leader Reverend Jesse Jackson in Chicago
excerpt_en: CHICAGO, USA March 6, 2026 - Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi attended the funeral of civil rights icon Reverend Jesse Jackson in Chicago on Friday, paying tribute to the late activist whose lifelong commitment to racial equality and social justice left a profound mark global
body_en:
CHICAGO, USA March 6, 2026 - Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi attended the funeral of civil rights icon Reverend Jesse Jackson in Chicago on Friday, paying tribute to the late activist whose lifelong commitment to racial equality and social justice left a profound mark globally.
The DRC Presidency noted that Tshisekedi’s presence also honored Jackson’s historic ties to the Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly during its most challenging democratic transitions. Jackson’s work as US Special Envoy for Africa, including meetings with Étienne Tshisekedi, was highlighted as a pivotal moment in DRC-U.S. relations.
Jackson, who passed away on February 17, 2026, at age 84, was a central figure in the American Civil Rights Movement and collaborated closely with Reverend Martin Luther King Jr. His activism and global influence continue to resonate in Africa and beyond.
President Tshisekedi’s attendance at the ceremony underscores both personal respect and the DRC’s recognition of Jackson’s enduring legacy in supporting democratic values and human rights on the African continent.

title: Paul Kagame Denounces Selective Pressure, Calls for Equal Accountability of All Parties
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda March 6, 2026 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has rejected what he describes as selective international pressure on Rwanda over its alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), calling instead for equal scrutiny of all pa
title_en: Paul Kagame Denounces Selective Pressure, Calls for Equal Accountability of All Parties
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda March 6, 2026 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has rejected what he describes as selective international pressure on Rwanda over its alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), calling instead for equal scrutiny of all pa
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda March 6, 2026 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame has rejected what he describes as selective international pressure on Rwanda over its alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), calling instead for equal scrutiny of all parties to the conflict.
Speaking at a dinner with ambassadors, diplomats, and representatives of international organizations accredited to Kigali, Kagame emphasized that the crisis in eastern DRC is long-standing and rooted in structural issues, including the persistent threat posed by the Forces Démocratiques de Libération du Rwanda (FDLR). He criticized Kinshasa’s view that the FDLR is a residual force, arguing the group continues to pose a significant threat to Rwanda and spreads its ideology to other armed factions in the region.
Kagame highlighted what he sees as a double standard in international expectations: while the Washington Agreements call for a ceasefire and security measures by all parties, he asserts that only Rwanda faces punitive measures and sanctions. He cited military operations and troop buildups by DRC and allied forces in eastern and western DRC, arguing that these actions undermine the ceasefire and shift the burden unfairly onto Rwanda.
“As expected, responsibility has been placed exclusively on Rwanda. This selective pressure has only encouraged the Congolese government and affiliated elements to resume military operations. We are asking for the same rigor to be demanded from all parties,” Kagame said.
The Rwandan President’s remarks come amid U.S. sanctions and visa restrictions targeting Rwandan officials accused of supporting the M23 rebellion. The U.S. State Department insists that all parties, including the DRC, must honor the Washington Agreements, including the neutralization of the FDLR and withdrawal of Rwandan forces from Congolese territory.
Kagame stressed that Rwanda’s actions are driven by legitimate security concerns, defending the country’s right to protect its borders from the continued presence of armed groups and their genocidal ideology. “The choice is clear: tolerate the FDLR and its growing network of militias advancing toward our border, or defend ourselves and bear the consequences. Any other country in our position would do the same,” he concluded.
This statement underscores ongoing tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali, as diplomatic pressure intensifies amid continued clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, prolonging instability in the Great Lakes region.

title: DRC Signs $155 Million AfDB Loan to Boost Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park
excerpt: KINSHASA February 26, 2026 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has signed a $155 million loan agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) to strengthen connectivity for the Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park. The signing was carried out by Minister of F
title_en: DRC Signs $155 Million AfDB Loan to Boost Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park
excerpt_en: KINSHASA February 26, 2026 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has signed a $155 million loan agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) to strengthen connectivity for the Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park. The signing was carried out by Minister of F
body_en:
KINSHASA February 26, 2026 - The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has signed a $155 million loan agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) to strengthen connectivity for the Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park. The signing was carried out by Minister of Finance Doudou Fwamba Likunde Li-Botayi.
This project forms the third component of the DRC’s Agricultural Transformation Program, aligning with the vision of President Félix Tshisekedi to make agriculture a strategic lever for economic diversification and food security.
Minister Fwamba emphasized that connectivity is central to the success of existing investments in governance and value chain development. “It is essential for the sustainable development of our agricultural potential and the effective integration of producers into local and regional markets,” he said.
The project includes the improvement of the Lukalaba-Ngandajika and Nkuadi-Ngandajika-Park roads, aiming to:
Open up the region sustainably
Reduce transport costs
Facilitate trade
Create jobs, particularly for youth and women
The government underscored that infrastructure development is key to agricultural transformation, food security, and national cohesion, while praising the AfDB partnership as vital for achieving strategic priorities.
Officials noted that this agreement strengthens DRC’s financial credibility with international partners and opens new avenues for integrated and sustainable rural development.

title: Government Acknowledges Delays in Civil Servants’ Salaries, Promises Normalization Within a Month
excerpt: KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo government has acknowledged delays in salary payments for civil servants, citing strain on public finances, and pledged a return to regular payments within the month. At a meeting on March 5, the government, led by Prime M
title_en: Government Acknowledges Delays in Civil Servants’ Salaries, Promises Normalization Within a Month
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo government has acknowledged delays in salary payments for civil servants, citing strain on public finances, and pledged a return to regular payments within the month. At a meeting on March 5, the government, led by Prime M
body_en:
KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo government has acknowledged delays in salary payments for civil servants, citing strain on public finances, and pledged a return to regular payments within the month.
At a meeting on March 5, the government, led by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, and the Economic Situation Committee (CCE) reviewed public finances, monetary dynamics, market prices, and the potential effects of the Middle East crisis on the Congolese economy. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba confirmed that delayed salaries result from pressure on the treasury, compounded by security and humanitarian expenditures linked to the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.
“The delay is due to strain on the treasury,” Mukoko Samba explained. “A few months ago, the Government already emphasized the growing burden of the wage bill. We are taking measures to strengthen revenue collection and better control spending to restore timely salary payments.”
He reassured that steps to improve payroll management and public revenue collection, aligned with President Félix Tshisekedi’s directives, should normalize payments within the month.
The recurring delays have drawn attention from economists, such as Deputy Gode Mpoy, who noted that exchange rate fluctuations contribute to shortfalls when payrolls are calculated in USD but converted to Congolese francs. The government, however, rejects claims of liquidity problems, maintaining that sufficient resources are available.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has also flagged the growing public sector wage bill as a fiscal risk, particularly in education, health, and justice, where recent salary adjustments, recruitment, and administrative regularizations have strained the budget.
President Tshisekedi previously instructed a comprehensive payroll audit, with results expected within 30 days, aimed at ensuring sustainable public finances and regular, reliable salary payments for civil servants.
This move comes as the DRC faces increased expenditures related to security operations, including responses to the AFC/M23 rebellion in North and South Kivu, highlighting the delicate balance between fiscal management and social stability.

President Tshisekedi previously instructed a comprehensive payroll audit, with results expected within 30 days, aimed at ensuring sustainable public finances and regular, reliable salary payments for civil servants.
This move comes as the DRC faces increased expenditures related to security operations, including responses to the AFC/M23 rebellion in North and South Kivu, highlighting the delicate balance between fiscal management and social stability.

title: Kinshasa Holds 65.2% of Bank Deposits, Central Bank Reports
excerpt: KINSHASA February 28, 2026 - Bank deposits in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remain heavily concentrated in the capital, Kinshasa, accounting for 65.2% of total deposits, according to the latest economic outlook from the Central Bank of Congo (BCC). The report, covering e
title_en: Kinshasa Holds 65.2% of Bank Deposits, Central Bank Reports
excerpt_en: KINSHASA February 28, 2026 - Bank deposits in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remain heavily concentrated in the capital, Kinshasa, accounting for 65.2% of total deposits, according to the latest economic outlook from the Central Bank of Congo (BCC). The report, covering e
body_en:
KINSHASA February 28, 2026 - Bank deposits in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remain heavily concentrated in the capital, Kinshasa, accounting for 65.2% of total deposits, according to the latest economic outlook from the Central Bank of Congo (BCC).
The report, covering economic developments from February 13 to 20, 2026, shows that after Kinshasa, deposits are primarily held in Haut-Katanga (22.9%), Lualaba (4.0%), and North Kivu (2.7%). Total bank deposits reached $16.24 billion at the end of December 2025, marking a 3.4% increase from the previous month and a 10.2% year-on-year rise, largely driven by dollar-denominated deposits from households and private enterprises.
Households represent 35.8% of total deposits, while private businesses account for 31.8%. Sectorally, deposits come mostly from sectors outside public administration (39.2%), trade (21.7%), and extractive industries (14.5%).
Meanwhile, gross loans totaled $10.27 billion, up 2.5% month-on-month and 20.2% year-on-year, primarily due to increased lending to SMEs and the central government. Loans in foreign currency rose 2.5%, while local currency loans fell 1.7%.
The BCC notes that the formal financial system comprises 287 institutions, including 108 credit institutions, 137 financial companies, 39 insurance companies, two social security funds, and one guarantee fund. The banking sector includes 14 active banks with 445 service points (371 branches and 74 ATMs), representing 97% of financial sector assets.
The microfinance sector has 101 institutions, including 78 savings and credit cooperatives, 15 microfinance companies, and 8 microcredit enterprises, with 186 operating points representing roughly 3% of sector assets. Nearly 70% of microfinance institutions are concentrated in Kinshasa, North Kivu, and South Kivu.
The report underscores the continued dominance of Kinshasa in the country’s financial landscape, highlighting challenges for financial inclusion in other provinces.

title: Daniel Mukoko Highlights Local Industrialization and Value Chains
excerpt: KINSHASA March 2, 2026 - The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was i
title_en: Daniel Mukoko Highlights Local Industrialization and Value Chains
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 2, 2026 - The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was i
body_en:
KINSHASA March 2, 2026 - The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was initiated by the Embassy of Japan.
In his opening remarks, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba emphasized the importance of transforming the Democratic Republic of Congo’s economy through industrialization and local processing of raw materials. He highlighted the DRC’s critical mineral resources, exceptional hydroelectric potential through the Inga complex, and geostrategic position in Africa as key assets for industrial partnerships.
“We need to move from extraction to processing,” Mukoko Samba stated, underscoring government ambitions to develop value chains in batteries, advanced metallurgy, recycling, special economic zones, and high-value-added technology partnerships.
He also stressed the potential for Japanese companies to contribute their expertise in electronics, automotive, advanced materials, and clean technology to the DRC’s industrialization efforts. Beyond mining, he pointed to the country’s agricultural potential, advocating for mechanization, smart irrigation, agri-food processing, and technical training as areas for Japanese investment. “Investing in Congolese agriculture is investing in regional stability and the continent’s food security,” he said.
The Deputy Prime Minister reassured investors regarding ongoing structural reforms, including digitalization of public administration, mining governance improvements, modernization of public-private partnerships, and enhanced business security. He also recalled President Félix Tshisekedi’s commitment, made during a February 5 meeting in Washington, to an investor-friendly environment.
This inaugural forum builds on previous DRC-Japan economic dialogues held in Tokyo (April 2025) and Osaka (June 2025), reflecting a shared commitment to deepen trade, investment, and industrial cooperation between the two nations.

title: DRC Showcases Mining Strategy on Global Stage
excerpt: TORONTO March 3, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo presented its mining strategy at the annual Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada (PDAC 2026) convention, highlighting investment opportunities and sustainable development in the sector. Led by Minister of Mines Lo
title_en: DRC Showcases Mining Strategy on Global Stage
excerpt_en: TORONTO March 3, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo presented its mining strategy at the annual Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada (PDAC 2026) convention, highlighting investment opportunities and sustainable development in the sector. Led by Minister of Mines Lo
body_en:
TORONTO March 3, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo presented its mining strategy at the annual Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada (PDAC 2026) convention, highlighting investment opportunities and sustainable development in the sector.
Led by Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba, the DRC delegation emphasized reforms in governance, transparency, traceability, and local transformation through special economic zones. These initiatives reflect the vision of President Félix Tshisekedi and coordination by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka to position the DRC as a responsible, strategic player in the global mining industry.
Minister Watum Kabamba stressed: “It’s not enough to have critical minerals. We must create the conditions necessary for investment to transform this potential into tangible wealth. Our laws and administration are the investor’s best allies.” He underscored fiscal stability, streamlined administrative procedures, and a modernized regulatory framework as tools to attract responsible investors.
The delegation showcased the DRC’s mining potential through booths representing the Ministry of Mines and Lualaba Province, reinforcing the country’s international visibility and the modernization of its sector.
In addition, the minister participated in the 11th International Summit of Mining Ministers, focusing on aligning strategies between producing and consuming countries, securing supply chains, and financing energy-transition projects.
The DRC’s presence at PDAC 2026 aims to stimulate new investments in local exploration and processing, foster strategic partnerships with global developers and financiers, and strengthen its recognition as a critical player in global mineral security, while advancing the country’s economic transformation and contribution to the global energy transition.

title: UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce Launched to Boost Trade and Investment
excerpt: KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the United Kingdom (UK) launched the UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce, a platform aimed at strengthening trade, investment, and sustainable development between the two countries. The launch coincided with a ministerial
title_en: UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce Launched to Boost Trade and Investment
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the United Kingdom (UK) launched the UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce, a platform aimed at strengthening trade, investment, and sustainable development between the two countries. The launch coincided with a ministerial
body_en:
KINSHASA March 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the United Kingdom (UK) launched the UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce, a platform aimed at strengthening trade, investment, and sustainable development between the two countries. The launch coincided with a ministerial visit from the UK, highlighting the country’s commitment to long-term partnerships and high-quality investments in the DRC.
The Chamber of Commerce aims to bring Congolese and British businesses closer together, fostering partnerships that promote local value addition, skills transfer, and economic growth. Recent initiatives include a $25 million financing agreement to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and nearly £3 million to expand agricultural operations and strengthen climate resilience.
The DRC emphasized the importance of local processing of mineral resources to create quality jobs, develop technical skills, and ensure sustainable economic benefits for its population. Key requests made during the launch included establishing a direct London-Kinshasa air route and increasing the presence of British companies to support technology transfer and capacity building. The DRC also highlighted its access to global markets through trade agreements, including AGOA, UAE partnerships, EU Economic Partnership Agreements, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), and upcoming agreements with China and India.
The Chamber plans to formalize its operational structure, expand membership, launch targeted business forums, and create regular networking opportunities between Congolese and British companies. The UK-DRC Chamber of Commerce is expected to accelerate trade, attract investment, create jobs, develop skills, and reinforce governance standards amid the DRC’s ongoing economic transformation.

title: UN Proposes Initiatives to Strengthen Governance and Combat Illicit Flows
excerpt: Critical Minerals March 7, 2026 - At the UN Security Council meeting on Energy, Critical Minerals, and Security, the growing importance of critical minerals in the global economy was highlighted. Minerals such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel are now essential for digital technolog
title_en: UN Proposes Initiatives to Strengthen Governance and Combat Illicit Flows
excerpt_en: Critical Minerals March 7, 2026 - At the UN Security Council meeting on Energy, Critical Minerals, and Security, the growing importance of critical minerals in the global economy was highlighted. Minerals such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel are now essential for digital technolog
body_en:
Critical Minerals March 7, 2026 - At the UN Security Council meeting on Energy, Critical Minerals, and Security, the growing importance of critical minerals in the global economy was highlighted. Minerals such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel are now essential for digital technologies and the energy transition, with trade in raw and semi-processed minerals reaching $2.5 trillion in 2023. Demand is projected to triple by 2030 and quadruple by 2040, creating opportunities for job creation, economic diversification, and sustainable development.
The UN outlined three key priorities to ensure conflict-affected countries benefit responsibly from their natural resources. First, exploitation must lead to fair and equitable outcomes, strengthening national institutions, regulatory frameworks, and processing capacities, while mitigating negative impacts. Second, multilateral and regional action is needed to improve traceability, combat illicit flows, and build resilient supply chains. Third, mediation tools must be deployed to address conflicts related to natural resources, fostering cooperative relationships and enabling parties to share benefits equitably.
The session comes amid ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, where the AFC/M23 rebellion occupies areas in North and South Kivu. The Congolese government frames these attacks as part of an economic war aimed at plundering critical minerals, while providing military support to rebels. Rwanda denies involvement, citing the threat of the FDLR, a group with a genocidal ideology, and framing the situation as linked to Tutsi community security concerns.
Efforts to resolve tensions include the Washington Process, addressing relations between Kinshasa and Kigali, and the Doha Process, focused on the AFC/M23 crisis. Despite these initiatives, hostilities persist, endangering civilian populations and worsening humanitarian conditions amid declining international aid.
The UN emphasized that equitable and responsible management of critical minerals could lift millions out of poverty, promote peace, and support sustainable development, but only if governance, traceability, and diplomacy are effectively enforced.

excerpt_en: At the UN Security Council debate on energy and critical minerals, France highlighted the role of natural resources in fueling conflict and instability. Eastern DRC, largely controlled by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion, produces between 15 and 30% of global coltan, which is
body_en:
At the UN Security Council debate on energy and critical minerals, France highlighted the role of natural resources in fueling conflict and instability. Eastern DRC, largely controlled by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion, produces between 15 and 30% of global coltan, which is exploited to finance armed activities and expand territorial control.
This resource grabbing perpetuates violence, prolongs conflicts, and worsens the suffering of civilian populations. France condemned the predatory exploitation model, noting that such practices hinder economic and social development by depriving states of the resources of their own land. Comparisons were also made to Ukraine, where energy infrastructure attacks are used as a weapon of coercion.
The session occurred amid ongoing Rwandan aggression in eastern DRC, with AFC/M23 forces occupying large parts of North and South Kivu. The Congolese government considers these attacks as economic wars aimed at the plundering and illicit exploitation of minerals, while Kigali rejects these claims, citing FDLR threats and denying military support to M23.
Efforts to resolve tensions include the Washington Process, addressing Kinshasa-Kigali relations, and the Doha Process, focusing on the AFC/M23 crisis. Despite these initiatives, hostilities persist, endangering civilian populations and worsening humanitarian conditions, especially as international aid declines.

title: Deadly Landslides in Rubaya Highlight Unregulated Mining
excerpt: Rubaya Masisi , March 8, 2026 - The Support Group for Traceability and Transparency in Natural Resource Management (GATT-RN) expressed deep dismay following recent deadly landslides in the Rubaya mining town, Masisi territory, North Kivu. The organization denounced dangerous arti
title_en: Deadly Landslides in Rubaya Highlight Unregulated Mining
excerpt_en: Rubaya Masisi , March 8, 2026 - The Support Group for Traceability and Transparency in Natural Resource Management (GATT-RN) expressed deep dismay following recent deadly landslides in the Rubaya mining town, Masisi territory, North Kivu. The organization denounced dangerous arti
body_en:
Rubaya Masisi , March 8, 2026 - The Support Group for Traceability and Transparency in Natural Resource Management (GATT-RN) expressed deep dismay following recent deadly landslides in the Rubaya mining town, Masisi territory, North Kivu. The organization denounced dangerous artisanal mining practices and called on the government to take urgent action.
The Gakombe site landslide is the latest in a series of recurring tragedies, exacerbated by the rainy season and lack of safety standards. Several mining areas in Rubaya are under AFC/M23 rebel control, facilitating illegal and fraudulent mining. GATT-RN emphasized that Congolese miners risk their lives for minimal wages while some actors profit from strategic minerals, including nearly 15% of global coltan production.
This disaster follows another landslide in the same area less than a month prior, which claimed over 300 lives. GATT-RN stressed that these incidents reflect avoidable failures in mine management and safety.
The organization urged the government to formalize artisanal mining, impose strict safety and labor standards, and open an independent investigation to determine administrative, security, and economic responsibilities. It also called for strengthened mineral traceability, improved certification mechanisms, and a compensation system for families of victims.
Social and Health

body_en:
Rubaya, March 5, 2026 - Two days after a deadly landslide struck the Kasasa coltan mining site in the Rubaya mining area of Masisi territory, North Kivu, the exact death toll remains unclear as search operations continue under challenging conditions.
Local sources report that access to the site has been blocked by AFC/M23 rebels, who currently control this strategic mining area. This restriction prevents families and residents from obtaining information about loved ones who may still be buried under the rubble.
Sources also indicate that anyone attempting to publicly discuss the incident or provide details risks arrest, heightening anxiety and fear among the local population. Residents believe the rebels are deliberately trying to restrict the flow of information regarding the disaster.
Despite these obstacles, search efforts at the site continue, though conditions remain difficult and dangerous, leaving communities in deep uncertainty over the full extent of the tragedy.

excerpt: Kisangani, March 6, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, director general of the online news outlet KIS24.INFO, has been detained for three days at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani, Tshopo province, without contact with his family, colleagues, or lawyers. The edito

excerpt_en: Kisangani, March 6, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, director general of the online news outlet KIS24.INFO, has been detained for three days at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani, Tshopo province, without contact with his family, colleagues, or lawyers. The edito
body_en:
Kisangani, March 6, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, director general of the online news outlet KIS24.INFO, has been detained for three days at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani, Tshopo province, without contact with his family, colleagues, or lawyers.
The editorial team of KIS24.INFO reports that Sindani has spent his third night in detention without official information regarding the reasons for his arrest or his state of health. The media outlet described the situation as a serious attack on press freedom and the fundamental right to inform, guaranteed by the Constitution of the DRC, calling on journalists, media organizations, and civil society to mobilize.
The Tshopo branch of the National Union of Congolese Press (UNPC) denounced the journalist’s “abduction” in a press release. According to the UNPC, Sindani was arrested on Tuesday, March 3, 2026, around noon at the FIRVAO headquarters by agents claiming to be from the ANR. He was taken away in a vehicle without any official explanation and has not been informed of any charges or questioned formally.
The UNPC considers the detention a flagrant violation of fundamental rights, including the right to defense and due process. The organization demands immediate notification of allegations, access to legal counsel, respect for his legal rights, and calls for his immediate release if no legally substantiated charges are presented.
The UNPC further urges authorities to guarantee the safety and freedom of journalists working in Kisangani and across Tshopo province, emphasizing the importance of protecting press freedom in the region.

title: DRC Signs Memorandum to Institutionalize Gender Equality
excerpt: Kinshasa, March 8, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step toward gender equality with the signing of a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and institutionalizing parity. The ceremony followed a workshop organized on March 6 by the Ministry of
title_en: DRC Signs Memorandum to Institutionalize Gender Equality
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, March 8, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step toward gender equality with the signing of a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and institutionalizing parity. The ceremony followed a workshop organized on March 6 by the Ministry of
body_en:
Kinshasa, March 8, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step toward gender equality with the signing of a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and institutionalizing parity. The ceremony followed a workshop organized on March 6 by the Ministry of Gender, in collaboration with the Friedrich Ebert Foundation (FES), to validate the implementing decree of Law No. 15/013 of 2015 on women's rights and gender parity.
The initiative seeks to strengthen inclusive governance, promote networking among women, and enhance female leadership. The signing was attended by the Ambassador of Germany to the DRC, Ingo Herbert, and representatives of Congolese women’s associations.
Minister of Gender, Chantal Ombae, highlighted the significance of the agreement: “This paradigm shift means moving from symbolic representation to women’s decision-making participation; from political discourse to the structural implementation of parity. Together with civil society, we are building concrete mechanisms to strengthen governance and accelerate the achievement of SDG 5.”
She added that the partnership complements government efforts to build a more just and egalitarian society, amplifying the voices of women and children, “not as an option, but as a necessity for progress.”
During the ceremony, Minister Ombae also inaugurated the headquarters of the Friedrich Ebert Foundation, emphasizing its role as a space for dialogue, cooperation, and empowerment.
The Foundation’s representative, Constantin Grund, said: “By inaugurating this building on the eve of International Women's Day, we are sending a symbolic message: spaces for dialogue must be open to everyone, particularly women. We hope this will be a place for debates, inspiration, and partnerships that promote justice, equality, and democracy.”

title: Nearly 22,000 Congolese Return to Uvira from Burundi, Kinshasa Engages UNHCR
excerpt: Uvira, March 8, 2026 - Nearly 22,000 Congolese have spontaneously returned to the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uvira in South Kivu, coming from Bujumbura, Burundi, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs, Jacqu
title_en: Nearly 22,000 Congolese Return to Uvira from Burundi, Kinshasa Engages UNHCR
excerpt_en: Uvira, March 8, 2026 - Nearly 22,000 Congolese have spontaneously returned to the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uvira in South Kivu, coming from Bujumbura, Burundi, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs, Jacqu
body_en:
Uvira, March 8, 2026 - Nearly 22,000 Congolese have spontaneously returned to the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uvira in South Kivu, coming from Bujumbura, Burundi, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs, Jacquemain Shabani, reported during the 81st meeting of the Council of Ministers.
Shabani confirmed that the government has already contacted the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to ensure that the return of displaced persons and refugees complies with international regulations, through a planned tripartite framework.
The mass return follows violent clashes between the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion and government forces, which had previously led to the fall of Uvira and worsened the humanitarian situation in the region, affecting neighboring countries such as Burundi.
In response, the Congolese government, led by Minister of State for Social Affairs and Humanitarian Action Ève Bazaiba Masudi, conducted a humanitarian mission to Burundi and Tanzania, providing support to returning refugees, coordinating with host countries, and working with partners including the UNHCR.
The return coincides with the reopening of cross-border trade, symbolizing renewed state authority after months of closure due to security tensions linked to AFC/M23 activities. The government delegation presided over the reopening ceremony and continues to monitor measures aimed at restoring order and governance.
Uvira, a strategic city in South Kivu, had been under AFC/M23 control, strengthening the rebel presence in North and South Kivu. The city is considered a key security and economic stronghold, potentially facilitating advances toward the Greater Katanga region, the economic heartland of the DRC.
The developments follow the recent visit of European Commissioner for Crisis Preparedness and Management, Hadja Lahbib, who urged all parties in the Great Lakes region to respect international humanitarian law, reinforcing the message of humanitarian compliance and conflict resolution.

title: Measles and Mpox Cases Threaten Isangi Health Zone
excerpt: Isangi, Tshopo, March 2, 2026 - The Isangi health zone is facing a dual health threat as measles and Mpox cases are confirmed in the district, according to Dr. Charles Koy, chief medical officer. In the Yalosase health area, of 18 samples tested, five were positive for measles an
title_en: Measles and Mpox Cases Threaten Isangi Health Zone
excerpt_en: Isangi, Tshopo, March 2, 2026 - The Isangi health zone is facing a dual health threat as measles and Mpox cases are confirmed in the district, according to Dr. Charles Koy, chief medical officer. In the Yalosase health area, of 18 samples tested, five were positive for measles an
body_en:
Isangi, Tshopo, March 2, 2026 - The Isangi health zone is facing a dual health threat as measles and Mpox cases are confirmed in the district, according to Dr. Charles Koy, chief medical officer.
In the Yalosase health area, of 18 samples tested, five were positive for measles and one for rubella. Mpox cases were also reported. In the Weko health area, all seven samples tested positive for Mpox. As of February 28, at least 23 Mpox cases have been recorded, including two deaths.
A small-scale local response has been organized, but resources remain severely limited, Dr. Koy noted. “We have forwarded the report to our superiors, and today a partner came to investigate and confirm whether there is an outbreak of cases,” he said.
Health facilities in Isangi are inadequate, with some treatment centers destroyed by Congo River flooding. The health zone also lacks essential medications for providing free medical care.
“For now, our SOS is for partners to assist with the medical treatment of Mpox and measles cases,” Dr. Koy pleaded, urging urgent support from government and humanitarian partners.

title_en: DRC Inducts 2,500 New Magistrates to Strengthen Rule of Law
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo formally inducted 2,500 new magistrates into the national judiciary on Saturday, February 21, 2026, in a ceremony held at the Congress Hall of the People's Palace in Kinshasa. The event marked the conclusion of an int
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo formally inducted 2,500 new magistrates into the national judiciary on Saturday, February 21, 2026, in a ceremony held at the Congress Hall of the People's Palace in Kinshasa. The event marked the conclusion of an intensive three-month training program aimed at enhancing the efficiency, ethics, competence, and professional conduct of magistrates before their deployment across the country.
The Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Guillaume Ngefa, emphasized that this initiative represents a crucial step in strengthening the rule of law. “A magistrate is neither a tool of the powerful, nor a hostage to emotion, nor a prisoner of personal convictions. They are an impartial servant of the law, bound by strict neutrality and an equal distance from all parties,” he declared.
This graduating class completes the initial cohort of magistrates, already in office since 2023, all graduates of the national competitive examination held in October 2022 and dubbed the “Rule of Law” class.

These powers are delegated to you by the nation, within the limits set by the Constitution and the laws of the Republic.”
He stressed that integrity and probity are not merely personal virtues, but fundamental prerequisites for public trust in the justice system. Independence, he added, is not a privilege but an institutional guarantee that protects citizens against arbitrary power.
“You will face pressure, attempts at influence, and even threats, but these challenges cannot justify abandoning the principles upon which your oath is based. Fighting corruption, influence peddling, and unjustified delays is now both a professional obligation and a requirement for institutional performance,” Minister Ngefa stated.

The deployment of these 2,500 magistrates is expected to address pressing challenges in multiple jurisdictions, including in field operations. Minister Ngefa reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting the judiciary with the necessary material and organizational resources to ensure effective performance.
The DRC Constitution of February 18, 2006, guarantees the independence of the judiciary from the legislative and executive branches, reinforcing the separation of powers as a cornerstone of democracy. The High Council of the Judiciary, responsible for managing appointments, promotions, disciplinary measures, and advisory functions, ensures the proper implementation of these principles.
“The mandate is clear: build a justice system worthy of the nation, protective of fundamental rights, firm against violations, and responsive to the legitimate expectations of the people,” concluded Minister Ngefa.

body_en:
Kinshasa, February 27, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Matete High Court sentenced Josué Kaniki to death on Thursday, February 26, 2026, for the murder of his mother. In addition, he received three years of penal servitude for cannibalism, the offense of consuming human flesh. Under the rules governing concurrent sentencing, only the most severe penalty, the death sentence, was enforced.
The court also ordered the immediate arrest of Kaniki and mandated the payment of $50,000 USD in damages to the plaintiff for all harm suffered.
The verdict concludes a summary trial that has sparked outrage among the population of Kinshasa in recent days, highlighting the case’s shocking nature and the court’s firm stance on severe crimes.

body_en:
Kinshasa, March 6, 2026 - The Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Guillaume Ngefa, formally handed over 14 Twiraneho fighters to the Banyamulenge community in Kinshasa on Thursday, March 5, 2026. These fighters, affiliated with the AFC/M23, had voluntarily surrendered to the Congolese army during last December’s fighting for control of Uvira in South Kivu.
According to the Ministry of Justice, all necessary checks were conducted to determine whether the individuals were personally involved in any acts warranting criminal charges, in line with the principles of the rule of law. “No individual charges have been brought against them at this stage,” the Ministry reported.
The release, carried out in the presence of military justice officials and representatives of the Disarmament, Demobilization and Community Reintegration Program (P-DDR-CS), was welcomed by the Kinshasa Banyamulenge community, who praised the Head of State for his “relentless fight against tribal hate speech.”
The Ministry highlighted that the ceremony reflects President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi’s commitment to encouraging all Congolese involved in armed groups to abandon violence and reintegrate into civil life.
Twirwaneho, a self-defense militia formed in the late 2000s to protect the Banyamulenge community, is led by Michel Rukunda, alias Makanika. The group, allied with the M23 and AFC, has been accused of human rights violations, including child recruitment, and remains a significant actor in the ongoing Kivu conflicts.

title: Attempted Prison Escape Causes Major Damage at Bandundu

title_en: Attempted Prison Escape Causes Major Damage at Bandundu
excerpt_en: Bandundu, March 7, 2026 - Significant property damage was reported Friday evening at the Bandundu Central Prison following a thwarted escape attempt by inmates. The prison’s food store and kitchen were set on fire, while the doors and windows of the police station and several cel
body_en:
Bandundu, March 7, 2026 - Significant property damage was reported Friday evening at the Bandundu Central Prison following a thwarted escape attempt by inmates. The prison’s food store and kitchen were set on fire, while the doors and windows of the police station and several cell block doors were damaged.
Preliminary reports indicate one serious injury and several minor injuries, with warning shots fired by security forces to restore order. While some sources cite prolonged hunger as a possible trigger, provincial authorities suggest the unrest began as a minor incident between inmates that escalated.
Governor of Kwilu, Philippe Akamituna, described the situation: “The final straw was when a prisoner insulted the storekeeper and was punished. Ferre, a convicted hardened criminal, encouraged him and incited everyone to revolt. They burned fresh food and tried to break through the back to escape. They damaged the entrance gate and the window. There’s no famine; the prison had 60 sacks of cassava, but they ransacked and burned the food supplies.”
The incident comes days after civil society organizations in Kwilu condemned conditions at the Cinquantenaire Prison, noting that penitentiary subsidies had not been delivered for three quarters, leaving inmates in particularly difficult living conditions.

title: Clashes Between AFC/M23 Rebels and Wazalendo Spread Fear in Kavumu
excerpt: KAVUMU, South Kivu February 21, 2026 - Residents of Kavumu and surrounding localities in Kabare territory, eastern DRC, spent the day gripped by fear and uncertainty as armed clashes erupted between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. According to information gathered locally,
title_en: Clashes Between AFC/M23 Rebels and Wazalendo Spread Fear in Kavumu
excerpt_en: KAVUMU, South Kivu February 21, 2026 - Residents of Kavumu and surrounding localities in Kabare territory, eastern DRC, spent the day gripped by fear and uncertainty as armed clashes erupted between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. According to information gathered locally,
body_en:
KAVUMU, South Kivu February 21, 2026 - Residents of Kavumu and surrounding localities in Kabare territory, eastern DRC, spent the day gripped by fear and uncertainty as armed clashes erupted between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
According to information gathered locally, the exchange of gunfire began early in the morning before temporarily subsiding, only to resume later in the evening, heightening tensions across the area.
Witnesses reported that the violence broke out shortly after a Wazalendo combatant was evacuated from a health facility, an incident that appeared to trigger the confrontation between the two armed groups. Within hours, heavy gunfire could be heard across several localities, particularly along the Katana-Kavumu axis.
Residents described hearing continuous bursts of gunfire, creating panic among civilians who were forced to seek shelter in their homes throughout the day.
The situation escalated again at around 6:30 p.m., when renewed shooting was reported in Kavumu, signaling a fresh wave of confrontation. Shortly afterward, observers noted a reinforcement of Wazalendo fighters near the Kavumu commercial center, suggesting preparations for further engagement.
The security situation quickly affected daily life and movement in the area. Traffic along the Bukavu-Kavumu road, one of the region’s key routes, was severely disrupted as armed elements positioned weapons along the Katana-Kavumu section.
The presence of combatants and the intensity of the shooting forced many residents to remain indoors, while commercial activities and transport were largely paralyzed.
The latest clashes illustrate the fragile security environment in parts of South Kivu, where confrontations between AFC/M23 forces and local Wazalendo militias continue to threaten civilian safety and regional stability.

title: Fragile Calm Returns to Walikale After Two Days of Fighting Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt: WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - A tense and fragile calm returned Monday morning to Mounts Buhaya and Fungura, located near Katobi in the Banakindi area of Kisimba group, Walikale territory, after two days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
title_en: Fragile Calm Returns to Walikale After Two Days of Fighting Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - A tense and fragile calm returned Monday morning to Mounts Buhaya and Fungura, located near Katobi in the Banakindi area of Kisimba group, Walikale territory, after two days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - A tense and fragile calm returned Monday morning to Mounts Buhaya and Fungura, located near Katobi in the Banakindi area of Kisimba group, Walikale territory, after two days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
The fighting erupted despite a ceasefire initiative proposed by Angola, part of ongoing regional diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing the persistent insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Reports indicate that AFC/M23 combatants launched simultaneous offensives on Wazalendo positions established on the strategic hills of Buhaya and Fungura. These elevated positions dominate the village of Katobi and are considered a critical defensive line for the nearby town of Pinga, an area frequently targeted by armed incursions.
The confrontation led to fierce exchanges of gunfire as both sides attempted to secure control of the strategic high ground. After prolonged fighting, Wazalendo fighters claimed to have halted the rebel advance, forcing AFC/M23 elements to withdraw toward Mpety, described as one of their main operational strongholds in the zone.
The violence triggered panic among civilians in Katobi and surrounding villages. Fearing for their safety, many residents fled into nearby forests, abandoning their homes to escape the clashes.
Although relative calm was reported Monday morning, most displaced residents have not yet returned to their homes, citing fears of a renewed outbreak of fighting.
On the ground, the security situation remains volatile, with local communities living in uncertainty and fear amid a broader context of resurgent armed violence in Walikale territory, one of the areas repeatedly affected by conflict in North Kivu Province.

excerpt_en: UVIRA, South Kivu - February 23, 2026 - The Gatumba-Kavimvira border crossing between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi officially reopened on Monday, February 23, restoring the movement of travelers and traders after more than two months of closure linked to the AFC/M
body_en:
UVIRA, South Kivu - February 23, 2026 - The Gatumba-Kavimvira border crossing between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi officially reopened on Monday, February 23, restoring the movement of travelers and traders after more than two months of closure linked to the AFC/M23 conflict in eastern Congo.
The crossing connects the Congolese city of Uvira with Gatumba in Burundi, a strategic point for cross-border trade and daily travel between the two neighboring countries.
The border had been closed by Burundian authorities on December 10, 2025, shortly after AFC/M23 rebels seized control of Uvira, a development that heightened security concerns along the frontier.
Reopening Without Formal Ceremony
The resumption of activities at the border took place without an official ceremony, as authorities on both sides agreed to immediately allow the passage of travelers.
Migration officials confirmed that standard administrative procedures remain in place, requiring travelers to present valid visas and travel documents.
The border post will operate daily from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., according to migration authorities.
Relief Among Border Communities
The reopening sparked relief and renewed hope among residents and traders who depend on the crossing for their livelihoods and daily commerce.
For many small-scale traders, the closure had severely disrupted cross-border economic activities, particularly trade between Uvira and the Burundian capital, Bujumbura.
With the border now open again, traders and travelers began resuming their movements, signaling a gradual return to normal economic life in the region.
Strategic Border for Regional Trade
The Gatumba-Kavimvira crossing is one of the most important border points between the DRC and Burundi, facilitating the movement of goods, traders, and travelers every day.
Its reopening is expected to revive cross-border trade, which plays a crucial role in supporting local economies on both sides of the frontier.
Authorities hope that the reopening will contribute to easing tensions and restoring economic stability, although the security situation in eastern DRC remains fragile amid ongoing armed conflicts in the region.

title: Wazalendo Offensive Forces AFC/M23 Rebels Out of Three Villages Near Rubaya
excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted in Masisi territory after Wazalendo fighters launched an offensive against AFC/M23 rebel positions, resulting in the loss of three villages previously controlled by the rebels near the strategic mining town of Rubaya.
title_en: Wazalendo Offensive Forces AFC/M23 Rebels Out of Three Villages Near Rubaya
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted in Masisi territory after Wazalendo fighters launched an offensive against AFC/M23 rebel positions, resulting in the loss of three villages previously controlled by the rebels near the strategic mining town of Rubaya.
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted in Masisi territory after Wazalendo fighters launched an offensive against AFC/M23 rebel positions, resulting in the loss of three villages previously controlled by the rebels near the strategic mining town of Rubaya.
The fighting took place on Sunday, February 22, in the villages of Kasenyi, Chugi, and Kinigi, located in the Bahunde chiefdom. These localities are considered strategically important due to their proximity to Rubaya, an area widely known for its intensive mining activities and its significance in the military and economic dynamics of the region.
After intense exchanges of gunfire, Wazalendo fighters reportedly regained control of the three villages, which had previously served as key positions for AFC/M23 forces in this part of North Kivu. During the clashes, several rebel fighters were reportedly captured, while weapons and ammunition were seized by the Wazalendo.
In response to the loss of these positions, AFC/M23 elements reinforced their presence on the hill known as “Sita,” a strategic location overlooking the contested area. The reinforcements appear aimed at stopping the Wazalendo advance and potentially launching a counteroffensive to retake Chugi and Kinigi.
Amid the escalation, AFC/M23 representatives accused the government coalition of violating the ceasefire, while also reporting drone strikes in several areas of Masisi territory, further highlighting the fragile security environment in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
On Monday, February 23, a fragile calm prevailed along the front line, but the situation remains volatile. Residents in the surrounding villages continue to live in uncertainty and fear, as tensions remain high in Masisi territory, an area already deeply affected by months of armed conflict and insecurity.

title: AFC/M23 Reinforces Positions in Mpety and Mindjendje, Tensions Rise Around Pinga
excerpt: WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in Walikale territory as AFC/M23 rebels reinforced their positions on Sunday, February 22, in the villages of Mpety and Mindjendje, located in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group. Reports indicate t
title_en: AFC/M23 Reinforces Positions in Mpety and Mindjendje, Tensions Rise Around Pinga
excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in Walikale territory as AFC/M23 rebels reinforced their positions on Sunday, February 22, in the villages of Mpety and Mindjendje, located in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group. Reports indicate t
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu February 23, 2026 - The security situation remains tense in Walikale territory as AFC/M23 rebels reinforced their positions on Sunday, February 22, in the villages of Mpety and Mindjendje, located in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group.
Reports indicate that the reinforcements arrived from the Kitshanga-Kalembe axis, with several witnesses observing columns of heavily armed fighters moving through Kalembe before heading toward Mpety. The movements were also confirmed by security sources in Walikale, raising concerns about a possible military buildup in the area.
Although the exact objective of the deployment remains unclear, local observers believe the repositioning could signal preparations for new offensives against the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo fighters, particularly around the strategic town of Pinga.
The developments have heightened anxiety among local communities, which are already under pressure following recent clashes reported in several parts of Walikale territory.
Local traditional authorities in the Kisimba group have denounced what they describe as a violation of the current ceasefire, calling on FARDC forces and Wazalendo fighters to remain highly vigilant in the face of the evolving security situation.
Amid a regional context marked by persistent instability, civilians fear that the reinforcement of rebel positions could lead to a renewed escalation of violence, potentially triggering fresh waves of displacement and further worsening the humanitarian situation in this already fragile area of North Kivu.
