title: Catholic Church Says It Was First to Denounce Rwanda’s Support for AFC/M23
excerpt: KINSHASA February 24, 2026 - The Catholic Church in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reiterated that it was among the first institutions to denounce Rwanda’s alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion operating in eastern DRC, while also announcing a shift in its pastoral appr
title_en: Catholic Church Says It Was First to Denounce Rwanda’s Support for AFC/M23
excerpt_en: KINSHASA February 24, 2026 - The Catholic Church in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reiterated that it was among the first institutions to denounce Rwanda’s alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion operating in eastern DRC, while also announcing a shift in its pastoral appr
body_en:
KINSHASA February 24, 2026 - The Catholic Church in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reiterated that it was among the first institutions to denounce Rwanda’s alleged support for the AFC/M23 rebellion operating in eastern DRC, while also announcing a shift in its pastoral approach to address the ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region.
In a statement issued Monday, Bishop Donatien Nshole, Secretary General of the Congolese National Episcopal Conference (CENCO), said the Church had already raised concerns about Rwanda’s backing of AFC/M23 rebels in previous official declarations.
Nshole stressed that statements made in the past by Archbishop Fulgence Muteba of Lubumbashi and other members of CENCO had clearly referenced Rwanda’s involvement, rejecting claims that the Church had only recently taken such a position.
“The Catholic Church is not new to this position. If you review CENCO’s documents, you will see that the bishops, including Archbishop Fulgence Muteba, have mentioned Rwanda several times,” Nshole said, emphasizing that the Church had also conducted international advocacy on the issue.
He added that it would be misleading to suggest that this was the first time the Catholic Church had publicly denounced Rwanda’s alleged support for the armed group.
According to the prelate, the Church has recently adopted what he described as a “pastoral shift” after repeated condemnations of the conflict failed to produce the expected results. Instead of focusing solely on denunciations, the Church is now promoting a “social pact for living together” aimed at encouraging dialogue and reconciliation in the DRC and across the Great Lakes region.
“This does not mean that we have remained silent,” Nshole explained. “We are choosing a different approach in order to give national dialogue a chance. It is part of a broader national strategy.”
The remarks come amid ongoing insecurity in eastern DRC, where AFC/M23 fighters continue to clash with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo militias.
The issue has also revived debate following criticism directed at Archbishop Fulgence Muteba after he traveled to Goma last July to preside over a devotional mass honoring Blessed Floribert Bwana Chui. The visit drew scrutiny because it occurred in a region under the control of AFC/M23 forces.
Speaking during the closing of a CENCO standing committee meeting, Muteba noted that the socio-pastoral situation in the country remains deeply affected by recurring insecurity, particularly in eastern provinces where government forces and their allies continue to confront AFC/M23 fighters supported by Rwanda.
The renewed statements from the Catholic Church have sparked widespread public debate, with some observers questioning whether this marks a new phase in the Church’s engagement with the conflict, while Church officials insist that their position has remained consistent for years.

title: MONUSCO and ICGLR Deploy Joint Assessment Mission to Uvira to Support Ceasefire Monitoring
excerpt: UVIRA, South Kivu February 24, 2026 - The United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) have launched a joint exploratory and preliminary assessment mission in
title_en: MONUSCO and ICGLR Deploy Joint Assessment Mission to Uvira to Support Ceasefire Monitoring
excerpt_en: UVIRA, South Kivu February 24, 2026 - The United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) have launched a joint exploratory and preliminary assessment mission in
body_en:
UVIRA, South Kivu February 24, 2026 - The United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO) and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) have launched a joint exploratory and preliminary assessment mission in Uvira, South Kivu, as part of efforts to support the implementation and monitoring of the ceasefire in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The mission, scheduled to run from February 23 to 27, 2026, follows consultations with President Félix Tshisekedi, who currently serves as Chair of the ICGLR. According to a joint statement released Tuesday, the deployment represents a crucial preparatory step toward the future establishment of a joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism within the framework of the broader regional ceasefire architecture.
The primary objective of the mission is operational and technical, focusing on ensuring that future monitoring and verification mechanisms are credible, secure, and operationally feasible. Teams on the ground will assess accessibility, security conditions, logistical requirements, and operational needs necessary for the effective functioning of the monitoring system.
During the mission, the joint delegation will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the political, security, logistical, and socio-environmental environment in and around Uvira, with the goal of facilitating coherent planning for the future deployment of ceasefire monitoring structures.
Officials emphasized that effective monitoring of the ceasefire is essential to reducing violence and creating the conditions necessary for a lasting political solution in the region.
The acting head of MONUSCO, Vivian van de Perre, noted that the mission’s mandate in South Kivu differs from its operations in North Kivu and Ituri, explaining that MONUSCO’s role in the province is focused primarily on monitoring the ceasefire rather than conducting Protection of Civilians operations, in accordance with United Nations Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025).
She stressed that the current deployment represents an exploratory phase, and that the scope and configuration of any future operations will depend on agreed parameters, security guarantees, and operational requirements.
For his part, ICGLR Executive Secretary Dr. Mubita Luwabelwa highlighted the importance of regional cooperation, stating that the Great Lakes region possesses significant potential for peace and prosperity if states work together to address shared security challenges.
Both organizations underscored that credible ceasefire monitoring requires favorable operational conditions, including freedom of movement for monitoring teams and reliable security guarantees, which remain key aspects of the ongoing assessment.
Under UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025), MONUSCO is authorized to support the implementation of a permanent ceasefire in the Democratic Republic of Congo. This support includes assistance to the Ceasefire Monitoring and Verification Mechanism as well as the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), established following the signing of the Doha Global Peace Framework on November 15, 2025.
The deployment comes amid renewed diplomatic and peacekeeping efforts aimed at stabilizing eastern DRC. It also follows a recent field visit to the region by MONUSCO leadership, during which discussions were held with AFC/M23 representatives, as well as a visit to Kinshasa by United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix, who reaffirmed the UN’s commitment to implementing MONUSCO’s updated mandate and supporting peace efforts in the region.

The mission, scheduled to run from February 23 to 27, 2026, follows consultations with President Félix Tshisekedi, who currently serves as Chair of the ICGLR. According to a joint statement released Tuesday, the deployment represents a crucial preparatory step toward the future establishment of a joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism within the framework of the broader regional ceasefire architecture.

Teams on the ground will assess accessibility, security conditions, logistical requirements, and operational needs necessary for the effective functioning of the monitoring system.

body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 24, 2026 - The security situation remains highly tense in Masisi territory after the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone strikes against AFC/M23 rebel positions early Tuesday morning in Kishusha, a locality located near the strategic mining town of Rubaya.
The operation reportedly took place at around 4:00 a.m., when a military drone launched strikes on positions held by AFC/M23 fighters in the area, which has witnessed intense clashes in recent days.
Residents reported powerful explosions that could be heard as far as Rubaya, triggering panic among the local population. Several families, already living under the strain of ongoing insecurity, spent the early hours of the morning fearing a possible escalation of fighting in the area.
For now, no official casualty figures have been released. Information from the ground indicates that assessments are underway to determine the extent of human and material damage caused by the strikes.
The drone operation comes amid renewed clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and FARDC forces, supported by Wazalendo fighters, around Rubaya and in several other localities of Masisi territory, highlighting the continued volatility of the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

title_en: Willy Ngoma, AFC/M23 Military Spokesperson, Killed in Drone Strike Near Rubaya
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu - February 24, 2026 - Willy Ngoma, the military spokesperson for the AFC/M23 rebel group, was killed on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, during a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) near Rubaya, a strategic mining
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu - February 24, 2026 - Willy Ngoma, the military spokesperson for the AFC/M23 rebel group, was killed on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, during a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) near Rubaya, a strategic mining area in Masisi territory, eastern DRC.
Ngoma’s death, confirmed by multiple sources within the rebel movement, marks the loss of a high-ranking member of AFC/M23, following the earlier killing of Magloire Paluku, amid escalating hostilities in eastern DRC. The increase in fighting coincides with intensified FARDC airstrikes, ground offensives by Wazalendo allies, and Angola’s perceived failure to enforce the ceasefire, according to the United Nations.
Prior to Ngoma’s death, Bertrand Bisimwa, the second-in-command of AFC/M23, accused the Kinshasa government of violating the ceasefire since signing the Strategic Partnership Agreement with the United States. In statements on social media, Bisimwa condemned what he described as “assassinations and massacres of innocent civilians with impunity,” denouncing the government’s disregard for the peace process.
Willy Ngoma had previously been sanctioned by the United States in 2023 for his role in serious human rights abuses, including murders and sexual violence against civilians, committed under the banner of the AFC/M23 rebel movement.
His death underscores the intensifying conflict in North Kivu, reflecting the volatile security situation in eastern DRC and the continuing struggle between government forces, allied militias, and armed rebel groups in the region.

excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted on Tuesday morning, February 24, between AFC/M23 rebels and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, in Mahanga village, located in the Butsike area of the Nyamabo
title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Driven Out of Mahanga Village Amid Renewed Fighting
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted on Tuesday morning, February 24, between AFC/M23 rebels and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, in Mahanga village, located in the Butsike area of the Nyamabo
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted on Tuesday morning, February 24, between AFC/M23 rebels and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, in Mahanga village, located in the Butsike area of the Nyamaboko I group, Masisi territory.
Government forces reportedly advanced from Buhimba in neighboring Walikale territory, targeting rebel positions in Mahanga. After a brief but intense exchange of gunfire, AFC/M23 fighters were driven out of the village, retreating into the surrounding bush in this part of the Osso Banyungu chiefdom.
The offensive triggered population movements, with several families fleeing Mahanga to seek refuge in the nearby bush, fearing renewed clashes.
Local observers noted that the situation remains highly volatile, as the different armed factions continue to reposition themselves in this part of Masisi territory, an area regularly affected by conflict and instability.
These developments underscore the persistent fragility of security in rural North Kivu, where civilians continue to bear the brunt of ongoing armed rivalries.

body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu - February 25, 2026 - Violent clashes erupted on Wednesday, February 25, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militias in the villages of Lumbishi and Kashovu, located in the Katoy sector, southern Masisi territory, North Kivu province.
The fighting began early Wednesday as Wazalendo forces launched a counter-offensive aimed at retaking the two villages from rebel control. The exchanges of heavy and light weapon fire were reported across the area, triggering widespread panic among local residents.
The renewed confrontations have caused significant population displacement, with families fleeing the affected villages. Many sought shelter in the surrounding bush, while others moved toward the town of Ngungu in search of safety.
Masisi territory remains one of the most unstable regions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, frequently affected by clashes between local armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels. Observers note that the security situation remains fluid, with ongoing movements of both government-allied militias and rebel forces contributing to persistent civilian insecurity.

title_en: Intense Fighting in Kibanda as Government Forces Target AFC/M23 Positions
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Clashes intensified on Wednesday, February 25, in Kibanda village, located approximately two kilometers from Kasopo in the Nyamaboko 1 group of the Osso Banyungu sector, as government forces and local fighters from Buhimba launched an offens
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Clashes intensified on Wednesday, February 25, in Kibanda village, located approximately two kilometers from Kasopo in the Nyamaboko 1 group of the Osso Banyungu sector, as government forces and local fighters from Buhimba launched an offensive against AFC/M23 rebel positions that have controlled the area for several months.
The objective of the operation is reportedly to regain control of Kibanda and expel the rebels from this strategic locality. Heavy and light weapons fire has been reported since the morning, with explosions heard in nearby villages, including Kashebere in Walikale territory, spreading fear among civilians.
Residents described a volatile situation and expressed concern over a potential escalation of fighting throughout the day. The renewed hostilities in Kibanda coincide with a broader resurgence of clashes across Masisi territory, including the Osso Banyungu and Katoy sectors and the Bahunde chiefdom, reflecting an offensive strategy on multiple fronts in an area critical for mining operations and supply routes.
The persistent insecurity has prompted many families to abandon their homes, seeking safety in less exposed areas. The resulting population movements are aggravating an already fragile humanitarian situation in the region, highlighting the ongoing vulnerability of civilians amid repeated clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and government-allied forces.

title: AFC/M23 Denounces Kinshasa’s “General Offensive” Amid Escalating Fighting
excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement has accused the Kinshasa government of launching a “general offensive” across multiple frontlines following the death of its military spokesperson, Willy Ngoma, in a drone strike near Rubaya on Tuesday, February 24
title_en: AFC/M23 Denounces Kinshasa’s “General Offensive” Amid Escalating Fighting
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement has accused the Kinshasa government of launching a “general offensive” across multiple frontlines following the death of its military spokesperson, Willy Ngoma, in a drone strike near Rubaya on Tuesday, February 24
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement has accused the Kinshasa government of launching a “general offensive” across multiple frontlines following the death of its military spokesperson, Willy Ngoma, in a drone strike near Rubaya on Tuesday, February 24.
Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23 and deputy coordinator of AFC/M23, stated on Wednesday that the operation represents a coordinated military campaign, violating the ceasefire and reflecting a deliberate choice to prioritize military action over dialogue. He criticized the absence of any visible initiative to halt the government’s offensive, contrasting it with the swift international reactions observed when the rebels defend themselves.
Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson for AFC/M23, reported several attacks on Wednesday: at 9:00 a.m. in Rutigita (Minembwe), 10:30 a.m. in Kitazungura (Kalehe territory), and 12:00 p.m. in Rugezi and its surroundings (Minembwe). The attacks reportedly involved armed drones and heavy artillery, resulting in casualties and population displacements.
Ngoma’s death comes after Magloire Paluku was killed, amid intensifying hostilities in eastern DRC. The escalation follows challenges to the ceasefire proposed by Angola, airstrikes by FARDC, and ground offensives by Wazalendo forces, allies of the government, targeting AFC/M23 positions, a group reportedly supported by Rwanda according to the United Nations. Ngoma had been sanctioned by the United States in 2023 for the group’s role in murders and sexual violence against civilians.
On the ground, fighting has resumed with intensity in Kibanda, approximately two kilometers from Kasopo, in the Nyamaboko 1 group (Osso Banyungu sector). FARDC troops and Wazalendo fighters from Buhimba launched an offensive against rebel positions, with heavy and light weapons fire reported in and around Kibanda. Explosions were also heard in neighboring villages, notably Kashebere in Walikale territory. Residents described the situation as volatile, fearing further escalation. Since the beginning of the week, clashes have spread across Osso Banyungu, Katoy sectors, and the Bahunde chiefdom, reflecting a multi-front offensive in a strategic territory near mining areas and supply routes.
Renewed fighting also erupted in the villages of Lumbishi and Kashovu, where Wazalendo militias launched a counter-offensive early Wednesday to reclaim the localities. The clashes triggered further population displacements, with families fleeing the areas affected by the fighting.
The ongoing conflict has also disrupted communications in Masisi territory, including the mining town of Rubaya, which has been without telephone, internet, and mobile money services since Tuesday, February 24. The outage has directly affected economic activity and financial exchanges, forcing some residents to travel up to ten kilometers or climb hills to regain a signal. The interruption follows drone attacks by the FARDC, including the strike that killed Willy Ngoma, highlighting the broader humanitarian and operational impact of the military escalation.
These developments underscore the fragility of security in Masisi and surrounding areas, with residents bearing the brunt of the ongoing multi-front offensive and population displacements while armed clashes continue to escalate.

MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Clashes resumed early Wednesday afternoon, February 25, in the village of Kazinga, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group (Masisi territory), as AFC/M23 rebels launched a counter-offensive to try to recapture the town after being expelled earlier in the day by government forces and Wazalendo fighters.
Local sources report that the rebels simultaneously attacked multiple positions inside and around Kazinga, quickly intensifying the exchange of fire and plunging residents into renewed fear. The sounds of heavy and light weapons fire were reportedly heard for several kilometers.
Kazinga, situated in the Butsike area, has become a major theater of fighting in the southern part of Masisi territory, with front lines shifting rapidly and villages changing hands between government-allied forces and AFC/M23 rebels in recent days.
The AFC/M23 counter-offensive comes amid escalating clashes in neighboring localities, following the loss of other strategic rebel positions. Residents describe a fluid and chaotic situation, as fighting continued into the late afternoon, heightening fears of a further deterioration of security in this part of Masisi territory.

title: Zambian General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa Visits Goma as EJVM+ Head Amid Ongoing Clashes
excerpt: GOMA, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of Zambia, newly appointed head of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), arrived in Goma on Wednesday, February 25, marking his first visit since taking command. He is accompanied b
title_en: Zambian General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa Visits Goma as EJVM+ Head Amid Ongoing Clashes
excerpt_en: GOMA, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of Zambia, newly appointed head of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), arrived in Goma on Wednesday, February 25, marking his first visit since taking command. He is accompanied b
body_en:
GOMA, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Brigadier General Charles Simuyuni Nakeempa of Zambia, newly appointed head of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), arrived in Goma on Wednesday, February 25, marking his first visit since taking command. He is accompanied by a five-member delegation amid ongoing hostilities between government forces and AFC/M23 rebels across North Kivu and South Kivu.
According to MONUSCO, the delegation reaffirmed its support for ongoing peace efforts and indicated that the finalized 2026 action plan will be shared with the UN Mission to guide monitoring and verification operations. This initiative is part of MONUSCO’s mandate under UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025), which emphasizes support for peace and stability in eastern DRC, including the implementation of ceasefire monitoring mechanisms.
In parallel, MONUSCO and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) have deployed a joint exploratory and preliminary assessment mission to Uvira, South Kivu, running from February 23 to 27, 2026. The mission follows consultations with President Félix Tshisekedi, current Chair of the ICGLR, and serves as a prelude to the future deployment of the joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism.
The primary objective of this exploratory mission is operational, aiming to ensure that future monitoring and verification mechanisms are credible, secure, and operationally feasible. Teams will assess accessibility, security, logistics, and engagement needs to ensure the effective functioning of the mechanism. A thorough evaluation of political, security, logistical, and socio-environmental conditions around Uvira will guide coherent planning for future operations, with final deployment configurations dependent on agreed parameters and operational requirements.
The ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism, signed in Doha on October 14, 2025, resulted from the sixth round of talks between the Congolese government and AFC/M23, mediated by Qatar. Implementation on the ground has faced challenges due to the reduced operational capacity of the EJVM, and the new command under General Simuyuni Nakeempa is tasked with revitalizing the mechanism to ensure effective monitoring and credible peace processes.
This visit follows recent field trips by MONUSCO leadership to eastern DRC, including meetings with AFC/M23 authorities, and was reinforced by United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix, who reiterated the UN’s commitment to fully execute MONUSCO’s updated mandate.
The deployment of EJVM+ under new leadership is expected to strengthen ceasefire monitoring, facilitate conflict de-escalation, and support ongoing peace initiatives in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Fighting intensified on Wednesday, February 25, in the village of Kasenyi, located in the Kibabi group of Masisi territory, as AFC/M23 rebels launched a counter-offensive against the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) a
title_en: AFC/M23 Launches Counter-Offensive in Kasenyi to Halt Government Advance Toward Rubaya
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Fighting intensified on Wednesday, February 25, in the village of Kasenyi, located in the Kibabi group of Masisi territory, as AFC/M23 rebels launched a counter-offensive against the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) a
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 - Fighting intensified on Wednesday, February 25, in the village of Kasenyi, located in the Kibabi group of Masisi territory, as AFC/M23 rebels launched a counter-offensive against the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and their Wazalendo allies. The government forces had seized Kasenyi last Sunday following several hours of clashes.
Local sources report that rebels redeployed to Kasenyi with reinforcements in men and ammunition, aiming to retake the village and halt the advance of pro-government forces toward the mining town of Rubaya, a strategic rebel stronghold in the region. Kasenyi is a key crossing point on the road leading to Rubaya, making its control crucial for both sides.
Since midday, heavy and light weapons fire has been reported in and around Kasenyi, causing renewed panic among civilians. Several families have fled their homes, abandoning belongings and seeking safer areas, while the humanitarian situation in Masisi territory, already precarious, faces further strain.
In nearby Rubaya, tensions remain high following FARDC airstrikes that destroyed a rebel position in Kishusha, further exacerbating insecurity. Many residents have reportedly fled Rubaya over fears of reprisals or intensified fighting in the coming days.
The ongoing clashes in Kasenyi reflect the volatile security landscape in Masisi territory, where multi-front fighting between AFC/M23 rebels, government forces, and allied militias continues to displace civilians and disrupt humanitarian operations.

excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - The villages of Kasenyi and Luke in Masisi territory fell back under AFC/M23 rebel control on Thursday, February 26, following intense fighting with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo militias. The cou
title_en: AFC/M23 Retakes Kasenyi and Luke After Fierce Clashes
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - The villages of Kasenyi and Luke in Masisi territory fell back under AFC/M23 rebel control on Thursday, February 26, following intense fighting with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo militias. The cou
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - The villages of Kasenyi and Luke in Masisi territory fell back under AFC/M23 rebel control on Thursday, February 26, following intense fighting with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and Wazalendo militias.
The counter-offensive, launched on Wednesday, February 25, came just one day after the rebels had lost both villages. Fighting was concentrated around strategic positions in Kasenyi and Luke, causing panic among local residents.
Reinforcements from Rutshuru territory reportedly bolstered the rebels’ capabilities, facilitating the recapture of the two villages and altering the balance of power on the ground.
The security situation remains volatile, with front lines shifting unpredictably. Local authorities, civil society actors, and community leaders have expressed concerns over a potential escalation of violence in an area already weakened by months of persistent insecurity.
The civilian population, caught between the warring parties, continues to bear the brunt of the clashes. Displacement has been reported, with residents seeking safer areas, though official casualty figures are not yet available.
In a region marked by chronic instability, the recapture of Kasenyi and Luke by AFC/M23 threatens to further complicate stabilization efforts, exacerbating the security and humanitarian crisis in Masisi and greater North Kivu.

title: Second Day of Intense Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Kibanda
excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - Fighting continued for a second consecutive day on Thursday, February 26, in the village of Kibanda, near Kasopo in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory. The Wazalendo militia launched an offensive on Wednesday against AFC/M23 positi
title_en: Second Day of Intense Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Kibanda
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - Fighting continued for a second consecutive day on Thursday, February 26, in the village of Kibanda, near Kasopo in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory. The Wazalendo militia launched an offensive on Wednesday against AFC/M23 positi
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 26, 2026 - Fighting continued for a second consecutive day on Thursday, February 26, in the village of Kibanda, near Kasopo in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory. The Wazalendo militia launched an offensive on Wednesday against AFC/M23 positions, aiming to regain control of this strategic town, which has been under rebel occupation for several months.
Since Thursday morning, the sounds of heavy and light weapons fire have reverberated throughout Kibanda and surrounding villages, creating widespread fear among civilians. Residents, already suffering from persistent insecurity in Masisi territory, are attempting to flee to safer areas, while panic spreads to neighboring towns, halting socio-economic activities.
At this stage, no official casualty figures have been released. Sources report an extremely volatile situation, with ongoing fighting and reinforcements reported on both sides.
Masisi territory continues to be one of the epicenters of armed violence in North Kivu, where recurring clashes between local armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels are worsening the already critical humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

Since January 2026, more than 500 Mobondo militiamen have surrendered and been referred to the National Service for professional reintegration, a program designed to equip former combatants with vocational skills. The threat posed by the militia has now been reduced to approximately 10%, according to Ntambwe, who distinguished this internal intercommunal conflict-between the Teke and Yaka communities-from external aggression such as that of AFC/M23 in the east of the DRC.
The Mobondo phenomenon, which emerged in 2022, escalated from a land dispute into armed violence, causing murders, looting, and mass displacement. The militia, originally led by a farmer named Sadam, alias Faux Yaya, spread across Kwilu, Kwango, Mai-Ndombe provinces, and parts of Kinshasa, particularly Maluku, before disarmament operations began.
Ntambwe highlighted that the disarmament strategy focused on awareness-raising, voluntary surrender, and structured reintegration rather than forced integration into military programs. Former militiamen are assessed individually for eligibility in reintegration programs, ensuring that those involved in atrocities are subject to transitional justice measures.
“This does not mean everything will be forgotten,” Ntambwe said. “The transitional justice phase will follow, ensuring truth, reconciliation, and commitments to non-repetition.” He added that while the threat is not completely eliminated, it has been significantly diminished, with only isolated elements remaining in the bush.
On the question of political involvement, Ntambwe partially confirmed that former President Joseph Kabila and PPRD members may have played a role in the conflict, citing testimonies regarding land purchases and insufficient compensation that fueled tensions. Security services continue to investigate these claims, which will be made public once verified.
Despite the progress, Ntambwe emphasized that absolute security does not exist, and while the Mobondo threat has decreased, pockets of insecurity remain. He reiterated the ongoing role of the FARDC and the police (PNC) in pursuing remaining militants and preventing a resurgence of violence.
The humanitarian impact of the Mobondo militia has been severe, with numerous deaths, displaced populations, and significant material losses. The Minister noted that the current phase prioritizes calming the situation and preparing for reintegration, with detailed assessments of displacement and damage planned as pacification advances.
This initiative reflects a structured approach to local militia management, aiming to regulate conflict, reduce harm, and reintegrate combatants into society, contrasting sharply with external armed groups destabilizing other regions of the DRC.

title: UN Experts Condemn “Extreme” Violence by M23 Against Human Rights Defenders
excerpt: EASTERN DRC February 26, 2026 - United Nations experts have issued a strong warning over the escalating human rights violations perpetrated by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against human rights defenders in North and South Kivu provinces. The experts cited assassination at
title_en: UN Experts Condemn “Extreme” Violence by M23 Against Human Rights Defenders
excerpt_en: EASTERN DRC February 26, 2026 - United Nations experts have issued a strong warning over the escalating human rights violations perpetrated by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against human rights defenders in North and South Kivu provinces. The experts cited assassination at
body_en:
EASTERN DRC February 26, 2026 - United Nations experts have issued a strong warning over the escalating human rights violations perpetrated by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against human rights defenders in North and South Kivu provinces. The experts cited assassination attempts, repeated kidnappings, torture, sexual violence, and death threats targeting those who document abuses, support communities, or denounce violations.
In a statement released in Geneva during the 61st session of the UN Human Rights Council, the experts emphasized that human rights defenders in eastern DRC are facing unbearable risks, particularly women and members of the LGBT community, who are subjected to heightened threats of sexual violence and torture.
Between November 2025 and February 2026, multiple defenders were reportedly targeted. Two women advocating against forced civilian expulsions in Uvira were abducted and tortured, and their whereabouts remain unknown. Another woman defending LGBT rights suffered repeated abductions and severe torture. A human rights defender in Goma was forced into hiding after threats and attacks on his family, while another defender received death threats and was assaulted at home.
The experts stressed that even when violations are committed by non-state armed groups, the State has a legal obligation under international human rights law to protect all persons under its jurisdiction. They called on authorities to investigate abuses promptly, provide medical and psychosocial support, and ensure that human rights defenders can operate safely.
“Human rights defenders are not combatants. They are essential actors for justice, accountability, and peace. Silencing them through fear and brutality undermines prospects for lasting peace in eastern DRC,” the experts stated.
This warning follows a recent government report documenting 17,015 cases of human rights violations in Goma, North Kivu, and Bukavu, South Kivu, which was presented to Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka. The government has pledged to intensify international advocacy and ensure accountability for these abuses.
The UN experts’ statement highlights the urgent need for protection, accountability, and respect for the ceasefire, as ongoing attacks on human rights defenders threaten both the humanitarian situation and the peace process in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

excerpt: MASISI, North Kivu February 27, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out an airstrike Thursday evening, February 26, targeting an AFC/M23 rebel position in Nyabiondo, Masisi territory. Local sources reported that the strike occurred around 6
title_en: FARDC Conducts Airstrike on AFC/M23 Position in Nyabiondo
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 27, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out an airstrike Thursday evening, February 26, targeting an AFC/M23 rebel position in Nyabiondo, Masisi territory. Local sources reported that the strike occurred around 6
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 27, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out an airstrike Thursday evening, February 26, targeting an AFC/M23 rebel position in Nyabiondo, Masisi territory.
Local sources reported that the strike occurred around 6:00 p.m. in the Isiro neighborhood, with a drone dropping bombs on the rebel camp. The resulting explosion was heard across surrounding areas, causing panic among residents. Civilians reportedly rushed into their homes immediately afterward, leaving the streets empty.
No official casualty figures have been released, but witnesses noted the presence of military personnel and equipment at the targeted position, suggesting potentially significant losses for the rebels.
This strike is part of intensified military operations by the FARDC in Masisi, aimed at weakening the operational capacity of the AFC/M23, which maintains active positions across several parts of North Kivu. By the end of 2025, at least three other rebel positions in Nyabiondo had already been destroyed by airstrikes, reflecting the army's increasing use of aerial firepower in this strategic area.
The security situation in Masisi remains tense, with civilians continuing to bear the brunt of repeated clashes between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebels.

title: DRC Reaffirms Commitment to Human Rights, Rejects Allegations of Discrimination and Foreign Occupation
excerpt: GENEVA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland
title_en: DRC Reaffirms Commitment to Human Rights, Rejects Allegations of Discrimination and Foreign Occupation
excerpt_en: GENEVA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland
body_en:
GENEVA February 27, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland.
Minister of State and Foreign Affairs, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, addressed allegations that the DRC discriminates against Congolese of Tutsi origin, accusations often cited by the Rwandan government to justify interventions in eastern DRC. She emphasized that such claims do not reflect national policy and that transgressions by individuals are addressed under national law and international commitments.
“The alleged protection of a community cannot justify violations of international law or serve as a pretext for illegal occupation of DRC territory,” Minister Kayikwamba Wagner stated, stressing that the country relies on multilateral instruments rather than taking the law into its own hands.
The remarks also came amid controversy surrounding Major General Sylvain Ekenge, the FARDC spokesperson, who faced suspension after allegedly discriminatory comments toward Tutsi women. Lieutenant General Jules Banza, FARDC Chief of Staff, condemned the statements and reaffirmed the FARDC’s commitment to safeguard the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security of all Congolese without discrimination.
Minister Kayikwamba Wagner underscored that the DRC continues judicial investigations into hate speech and conflict-related offenses, cooperating with the Commission of Inquiry to hold accountable those responsible. She called for national unity, condemning exploitation of isolated remarks by external actors, including the AFC/M23 rebellion and Rwandan authorities, in the context of ongoing tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali regarding the Washington process commitments.
The DRC’s statement highlights its determination to protect all communities, uphold international law, and maintain national cohesion amid persistent regional security and political challenges.

title: AFC/M23 Recaptures Chugi, Katobo, and Kaniro Amid Growing Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: MASISI February 27, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebels regained control of the villages of Chugi, Katobo, and Kaniro in the Bahunde chiefdom of Masisi territory, North Kivu, on the evening of Thursday, February 26, following intense clashes with Wazalendo forces. These villages, strategic
title_en: AFC/M23 Recaptures Chugi, Katobo, and Kaniro Amid Growing Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: MASISI February 27, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebels regained control of the villages of Chugi, Katobo, and Kaniro in the Bahunde chiefdom of Masisi territory, North Kivu, on the evening of Thursday, February 26, following intense clashes with Wazalendo forces. These villages, strategic
body_en:
MASISI February 27, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebels regained control of the villages of Chugi, Katobo, and Kaniro in the Bahunde chiefdom of Masisi territory, North Kivu, on the evening of Thursday, February 26, following intense clashes with Wazalendo forces.
These villages, strategically located to control access to the mining town of Rubaya, had been seized by Wazalendo last Monday. After four days of occupation, the militia withdrew in the face of a reinforced counter-offensive by AFC/M23, according to local administrative and security sources.
The recapture underscores the intensifying violence in Masisi, which has been a focal point of recurrent clashes between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 over the past week. Reports indicate troop movements and reinforcements on both sides as each seeks to consolidate territorial control.
Residents reported heavy exchanges of fire and bombings, generating widespread fear among civilians. No official casualty or damage figures have been released.
Humanitarian concerns are mounting as repeated displacement is forcing families to abandon homes, crops, and livelihoods. If hostilities continue or spread, the population may face new waves of displacement toward Rubaya, Nyabiondo, or other safer areas, further worsening an already fragile socio-economic situation in the territory.

MASISI February 27, 2026 - Three civilians were seriously injured on Thursday evening, February 26, during an army drone strike targeting an AFC/M23 rebel position in the Isiro neighborhood of Nyabiondo, Masisi territory, North Kivu.
Local sources reported that the explosion sent shrapnel into nearby homes, injuring three residents from the same neighborhood, who were urgently evacuated to a medical facility for treatment.
No official figures have been released regarding casualties among the rebels. Access to the targeted site remains restricted, preventing independent verification of the damage.
The strike is part of resurgent military operations in Masisi, where clashes between government forces (FARDC) and AFC/M23 rebels have intensified in recent weeks. Nyabiondo continues to be a strategic focal point in the ongoing conflict.

title: AFC/M23 Confirms Death of Military Spokesperson Willy Ngoma
excerpt: NORTH KIVU February 28, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement officially announced on Saturday, February 28, the death of its military spokesperson, Colonel Willy Ngoma, who was killed on February 24 in a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
title_en: AFC/M23 Confirms Death of Military Spokesperson Willy Ngoma
excerpt_en: NORTH KIVU February 28, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement officially announced on Saturday, February 28, the death of its military spokesperson, Colonel Willy Ngoma, who was killed on February 24 in a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_en:
NORTH KIVU February 28, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel movement officially announced on Saturday, February 28, the death of its military spokesperson, Colonel Willy Ngoma, who was killed on February 24 in a drone strike attributed to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
In its statement, the movement accused the Kinshasa government of deliberately violating the ceasefire and launching a full-scale offensive in eastern DRC. The rebels said that the strike, and other recent military operations, have made both soldiers and civilians primary targets, even beyond active frontlines.
“These crimes will not go unnoticed or unpunished. Our duty is to guarantee the protection of our people and our soldiers throughout the liberated territory,” the AFC/M23 declared.
The announcement comes amid escalating fighting across North and South Kivu, following repeated FARDC airstrikes and ground offensives by the Wazalendo militia, allies of the government forces. The movement cited multiple localities affected by the conflict, including Kawele, Mweso, Rutigita, Kitazungura, Rugezi, Rubaya, Walikale, Masisi, Kalehe, Gasovu, Minembwe, Kinyumba, and Nyabyondo, among others.
This marks the second significant loss for the group after the death of Magloire Paluku, occurring in the context of slow progress on international peace initiatives under the Washington and Doha processes, supported by the African Union, but with limited impact on the ground. Despite the intensified military pressure, the AFC/M23 maintains control over large areas of North and South Kivu.

title: Mass Graves Found Following AFC/M23 Withdrawal, Specialized Teams Mobilized
excerpt: UVIRA March 1, 2026 - Two mass graves were discovered in Uvira, the provisional capital of South Kivu province, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city. The findings were reported by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Jacque
title_en: Mass Graves Found Following AFC/M23 Withdrawal, Specialized Teams Mobilized
excerpt_en: UVIRA March 1, 2026 - Two mass graves were discovered in Uvira, the provisional capital of South Kivu province, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city. The findings were reported by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Jacque
body_en:
UVIRA March 1, 2026 - Two mass graves were discovered in Uvira, the provisional capital of South Kivu province, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city. The findings were reported by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Jacquemain Shabani, after a mission to oversee the DRC-Burundi border.
According to the government, the graves were located in the Kavinvira and Kilomoni neighborhoods. Preliminary investigations by provincial authorities indicate a total of 151 civilians were buried, including 121 in Kavinvira and 30 in Kilomoni. These executions reportedly occurred around January 18, 2026, shortly before the forced withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from the city.
The South Kivu provincial government classified the killings as war crimes under Article 8 of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, and as potential crimes against humanity, citing the organized and systematic nature of the executions targeting civilians.
Specialized teams have been deployed to secure the sites, recover the bodies, and conduct further investigations, though no official exhumations have yet taken place. The identities of both victims and perpetrators remain unknown.
Uvira, a strategic city in South Kivu, had been under AFC/M23 control since December 2025. The withdrawal followed international pressure, notably from the United States, after violations of the Washington Agreement were reported. The city’s recapture is considered a key step in DRC’s efforts to reassert control over the region and prevent further rebel advances toward Greater Katanga, the country’s economic heartland.
The discovery underscores the severe humanitarian impact of the AFC/M23 rebellion and highlights the ongoing challenges in securing civilian safety in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Multiple Drone Attacks Target Kisangani Airport, No Casualties, March 1, 2026
excerpt: KISANGANI March 1, 2026 - Kisangani’s Bangboka International Airport in Tshopo province was targeted by a series of drone attacks on Sunday, March 1, but no casualties were reported. Local sources and provincial authorities told that the first drone was intercepted around 3:00 PM
title_en: Multiple Drone Attacks Target Kisangani Airport, No Casualties, March 1, 2026
excerpt_en: KISANGANI March 1, 2026 - Kisangani’s Bangboka International Airport in Tshopo province was targeted by a series of drone attacks on Sunday, March 1, but no casualties were reported. Local sources and provincial authorities told that the first drone was intercepted around 3:00 PM
body_en:
KISANGANI March 1, 2026 - Kisangani’s Bangboka International Airport in Tshopo province was targeted by a series of drone attacks on Sunday, March 1, but no casualties were reported.
Local sources and provincial authorities told that the first drone was intercepted around 3:00 PM local time. Three additional “kamikaze” drones were neutralized by airport security between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM. Shrapnel caused minor damage to infrastructure, including broken windows, but the control tower remained operational. Some nearby residents temporarily evacuated as a precaution.
The provincial government attributed the attacks to the AFC/M23 rebellion and Rwanda. The group had previously claimed responsibility for a drone attack on Bangboka Airport in late January.
According to the Congolese research institute Ebuteli, the army employs Turkish TAI Anka drones and Chinese CH-4 combat drones. The recent attacks were reportedly carried out using Turkish Baykar Yiha-III drones, with additional drones possibly supplied by Estonian Threod Systems.
This wave of drone incidents follows FARDC airstrikes in Masisi territory on February 24 that killed Willy Ngoma, AFC/M23 military spokesperson, and several other rebel members, underscoring the growing aerial dimension of the conflict in eastern DRC.
The airport remains operational, and authorities continue to monitor the security situation closely.

The confrontations began on Saturday, February 28, when government forces launched an offensive to regain control of Kibati. The town is considered strategic due to its location along roads connecting multiple key towns in the territory.
As clashes continue, insecurity remains high, and local populations face ongoing disruptions to daily life and mobility in this volatile region of North Kivu.

title: Buhimba Falls Back Under AFC/M23 Control, Triggering New Displacements
excerpt: WALIKALE March 2, 2026 - The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo
title_en: Buhimba Falls Back Under AFC/M23 Control, Triggering New Displacements
excerpt_en: WALIKALE March 2, 2026 - The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo
body_en:
WALIKALE March 2, 2026 - The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo fighters.
According to local sources, the rebels advanced from Kilongo in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory and launched an assault on government positions in Buhimba. Following several hours of fierce fighting, FARDC forces retreated to Ngenge, west of Buhimba, leaving the village in rebel hands.
The recapture has sparked a fresh wave of displacement. Residents from Ngenge and Kangati are fleeing for safety, with some taking refuge in the bush and others moving toward Kimua, according to the chief of Waloa Yungu.
This development intensifies the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the area, already strained by persistent insecurity. Local sources warn that the fighting could spread to surrounding villages, as clashes persist along the border between Walikale and Masisi territories.
The AFC/M23’s seizure of Buhimba comes amid a resurgence of hostilities in multiple strategic locations across eastern North Kivu, highlighting the volatility of the region.

title: FARDC Retakes Strategic Villages in Fizi and Mwenga
excerpt: FIZI/MWENGA March 2, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian army, have recaptured more than five villages in the Fizi and Mwenga territories of South Kivu following operations against the Twirw
title_en: FARDC Retakes Strategic Villages in Fizi and Mwenga
excerpt_en: FIZI/MWENGA March 2, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian army, have recaptured more than five villages in the Fizi and Mwenga territories of South Kivu following operations against the Twirw
body_en:
FIZI/MWENGA March 2, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian army, have recaptured more than five villages in the Fizi and Mwenga territories of South Kivu following operations against the Twirweneho militia, an ally of the AFC/M23 rebels.
Local sources report that clashes intensified since Sunday, March 1, culminating in the retaking of Mikenge, a town held by rebel forces since March 2025, along with other strategic villages including Kakenge, Bilalombili, Bidegu 1, Madegu, and parts of Kalinga.
According to Pacifique Kararuka, president of the New Congolese Civil Society in Kipupu, “It was on Sunday that the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo, recaptured Mikenge and other areas. The operations are being led from Kakobanya.”
The army reports that the counteroffensive resulted in significant rebel losses: several were killed, five captured, 17 surrendered, and 11 bodies were recovered, including a brigade commander of the AFC/M23 and a logistics officer of the Twirweneho militia with their escorts. Military equipment, including anti-drone lasers, was also recovered.
These operations have caused displacement, with some residents fleeing to Uvira for safety. Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, the army spokesperson, stressed that the counterattack aims to neutralize AFC/M23 influence in the area and restore government control over strategic towns and villages.
Fighting in this region remains ongoing, as clashes continue between the Twirweneho-Red Tabara-FNL coalition allied with AFC/M23 and FARDC forces supported by Wazalendo and Burundian troops.

excerpt_en: MASISI March 2, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebels have seized control of Katoy, the main town of the Katoy sector in southern Masisi, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo militia. According to local security sources, the offensive
body_en:
MASISI March 2, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebels have seized control of Katoy, the main town of the Katoy sector in southern Masisi, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo militia.
According to local security sources, the offensive began early Sunday morning when the rebels attacked FARDC positions. Heavy exchanges of fire continued throughout the day, and by early evening, the town had fallen entirely under rebel control, marking a significant setback for government forces in this strategic area of southern Masisi.
The capture of Katoy has triggered a wave of population displacement. Residents, primarily women and children, fled to the bush and neighboring villages, abandoning homes and belongings. Many spent the night outdoors, exposed to harsh conditions and without immediate humanitarian aid, local sources reported.
This development underscores the ongoing volatility in southern Masisi, where positions continue to shift between the AFC/M23 and government forces. The resurgence of fighting in the region has further deepened the humanitarian crisis, compounding insecurity and instability for civilians in North Kivu.

title: U.S. Imposes Sanctions on Rwandan Army and Four Nationals over DRC Involvement
excerpt: WASHINGTON, D.C. March 2, 2026 - The United States Treasury Department announced Monday that the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals have been sanctioned for their involvement in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
title_en: U.S. Imposes Sanctions on Rwandan Army and Four Nationals over DRC Involvement
excerpt_en: WASHINGTON, D.C. March 2, 2026 - The United States Treasury Department announced Monday that the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals have been sanctioned for their involvement in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
body_en:
WASHINGTON, D.C. March 2, 2026 - The United States Treasury Department announced Monday that the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals have been sanctioned for their involvement in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) added the RDF and individuals Stanislas Gashugi, Ruki Karusisi, Mubarakh Muganga (also known as "MK MUBARKH"), and Vincent Nyakarundi to its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list. Assets of the designated entities and individuals under U.S. jurisdiction are now frozen, and U.S. citizens and companies are prohibited from engaging in transactions with them.
At the same time, OFAC issued General Licence No. 1 under 31 CFR Part 547, authorizing, until April 1, 2026, transactions that are “normally incidental and necessary” to the phased cessation of dealings with the RDF or any entity in which it holds at least 50% ownership. Payments to blocked individuals must be directed to blocked accounts, and the licence does not authorize other prohibited transactions unless explicitly approved.
This move comes amid escalating tensions in eastern DRC, where the RDF has been accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel movement, contributing to ongoing clashes in North and South Kivu provinces. The sanctions reflect Washington’s effort to hold Rwandan actors accountable for their involvement in destabilizing operations in the DRC.

title: Rwanda Condemns U.S. Sanctions, Calls Them Unilateral and One-Sided
excerpt: KIGALI March 2, 2026 - The Rwandan government criticized the recent sanctions imposed by the United States on the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals, describing the measures as “unilateral” and unfairly targeting “only one party” involved in the peace process i
title_en: Rwanda Condemns U.S. Sanctions, Calls Them Unilateral and One-Sided
excerpt_en: KIGALI March 2, 2026 - The Rwandan government criticized the recent sanctions imposed by the United States on the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals, describing the measures as “unilateral” and unfairly targeting “only one party” involved in the peace process i
body_en:
KIGALI March 2, 2026 - The Rwandan government criticized the recent sanctions imposed by the United States on the Rwanda Defense Force (RDF) and four Rwandan nationals, describing the measures as “unilateral” and unfairly targeting “only one party” involved in the peace process in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
In an official statement, Kigali argued that the sanctions “distort the reality” of the security situation in eastern Congo and fail to account for alleged violations by the DRC government, including “constant and indiscriminate drone attacks” and ground offensives that have reportedly caused numerous civilian casualties.
The statement also highlights that the DRC’s coalition forces reportedly include foreign mercenaries, state-backed ethnic militias such as the Wazalendo, and the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), described by Kigali as a “genocidal militia” operating alongside the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC).
Rwanda asserts that under the Washington Accords, the DRC committed to ending support for the FDLR and allied militias in a verifiable and irreversible manner, but has yet to take any meaningful action. Kigali emphasizes that it remains fully committed to the disengagement of its own forces, in parallel with DRC’s compliance.
Finally, the Rwandan government reaffirmed its commitment to the full implementation of the Washington Agreements, including the regional economic integration framework, and called for a “balanced” approach from international partners through mechanisms such as the Joint Monitoring Committee.
This statement comes shortly after the U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned the RDF and four Rwandan individuals for their role in the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, citing Rwanda’s support for the AFC/M23 rebel movement.

excerpt_en: KISANGANI March 2, 2026 - The Congo River Alliance/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) has officially claimed responsibility for the drone attacks targeting Kisangani-Bangboka International Airport in Tshopo Province on Sunday, March 1. In a statement, the rebel movement described the op
body_en:
KISANGANI March 2, 2026 - The Congo River Alliance/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) has officially claimed responsibility for the drone attacks targeting Kisangani-Bangboka International Airport in Tshopo Province on Sunday, March 1.
In a statement, the rebel movement described the operation as a “targeted mission” to “neutralize and destroy drones” that, according to them, were being prepared to “massacre civilians and attack AFC/M23 positions” near Kisangani. The group emphasized that its actions are part of its “patriotic duty to protect innocent populations.”
Local sources and provincial authorities had reported that four drones were intercepted over the airport on Sunday. The first drone was thwarted around 3:00 PM local time, followed by three additional “kamikaze” drones between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM. Shrapnel from the drones damaged windows in some buildings, but there were no injuries or disruptions to the airport’s control tower.
The provincial government confirmed that all four drones were neutralized, noting that one crashed as a CAA aircraft announced its landing. Residents in nearby areas temporarily evacuated as a precaution.
The governor of Tshopo Province had previously attributed the attacks to the AFC/M23 and Rwanda. The rebels had also claimed responsibility for a previous drone strike on Bangboka Airport in late January. Local authorities had reported those incidents on January 31 and February 1 before the army declared the situation under control.

excerpt_en: WALIKALE March 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, successfully repelled an attack by AFC/M23 rebels on Fungura Hill, overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group, on Monday, March 2. According
body_en:
WALIKALE March 3, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, successfully repelled an attack by AFC/M23 rebels on Fungura Hill, overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group, on Monday, March 2.
According to local traditional sources, the rebels launched their offensive from Mpety, targeting positions held by government forces. Fungura Hill is considered a strategic security stronghold for Pinga, a central town in this part of Walikale territory. Its capture could have provided a corridor to neighboring towns.
Heavy and light weapons fire was reported over several hours, spreading fear among the civilian population. However, the FARDC and Wazalendo forces contained the attack and forced the rebels to retreat to their original positions after failing to break through.
This incident highlights the ongoing volatility in North Kivu, where repeated clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and loyalist forces, often with local allies, continue to destabilize areas including Walikale, Masisi, and Rutshuru. Residents remain on high alert, fearing further hostilities in the coming days.

body_en:
UPPEMBA NATIONAL PARK March 3, 2026 - An armed group attacked Upemba National Park in Haut-Katanga province on the night of Monday, March 2, to Tuesday, March 3, 2026. The assailants targeted Lusinga, the park headquarters, where several rangers and expatriates were staying, according to local sources.
The attack has been attributed to an unidentified Mai-Mai armed group. No casualties have been reported so far, and authorities are investigating the incident.
Established in 1939 during the colonial era, Upemba National Park spans approximately 1,773,000 hectares and is home to a rich diversity of wildlife, including zebras, roan antelopes, Cape elands, hartebeests, greater kudus, elephants, and buffalo.
Park officials and security forces are reportedly on high alert to prevent further incursions and ensure the safety of staff and visitors.

title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Retake Kazinga
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu March 3, 2026 - The village of Kazinga, in the Nyamaboko 1st group of Masisi territory, fell back under the control of AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday afternoon following fierce clashes with the FARDC and the Wazalendo local militia. This recapture comes roughly two
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu March 3, 2026 - The village of Kazinga, in the Nyamaboko 1st group of Masisi territory, fell back under the control of AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday afternoon following fierce clashes with the FARDC and the Wazalendo local militia.
This recapture comes roughly two weeks after government forces had taken the village. Local sources report that AFC/M23 fighters, mainly from the Ndete and Kasopo axes, launched an offensive early Tuesday morning. Exchanges of fire, including heavy weapons, continued throughout the morning.
Kazinga occupies a strategic location in the Osso Banyungu sector, serving as a corridor to Buhimba (Waloa Yungu group, Walikale territory) and the Katoy sector in southern Masisi. With this advance, the rebels are consolidating control over a triangle linking Buhimba, Katoy, and Kazinga, strengthening their capacity to project force into surrounding groups, including Waloa Yungu, Waloa Uroba, and Waloa Loanda in Walikale territory.
The recapture highlights the persistent fragility of security in this part of North Kivu, which has seen a succession of attacks, counter-offensives, and population displacements in recent weeks. Humanitarian concerns continue to mount as civilians face ongoing insecurity amid this renewed escalation of fighting.

body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu March 3, 2026 - After three days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and FARDC forces supported by the Wazalendo local militia, the town of Kibati in the Luberike area of Walikale territory remains under rebel control.
Local sources indicate that government forces, despite having recaptured much of the town during the fighting, ultimately withdrew to the villages of Miba and Mungazi, allowing AFC/M23 fighters to reclaim all lost positions.
The clashes have caused significant disruption to logistics and humanitarian aid, with traffic on the Mungazi-Kashebere road completely suspended. Travelers and transporters remain stranded on both sides, awaiting an improvement in security conditions.
This development comes amid a broader context of insecurity in Walikale, where repeated confrontations between government forces and AFC/M23 rebels continue to severely affect civilians. Fighting in Kibati initially broke out on Saturday, February 28, and has since escalated, reflecting the ongoing volatility in the region.

WALIKALE, North Kivu March 4, 2026 - The security situation in Walikale territory is deteriorating as AFC/M23 rebels consolidate control over Kibati, following three days of intense clashes with FARDC forces and the Wazalendo militia.
Local sources report that after government forces withdrew, rebels secured all positions in the town. On the evening of Tuesday, March 3, additional reinforcements of fighters and ammunition arrived from Masisi territory via the Kashebere axis. The deployment has heightened fears of expanded military operations in the area, with surrounding villages remaining tense. Civilians, already affected by recent fighting, live in fear of further escalation in the coming days.
This development underscores the persistent volatility in Walikale, where recurring clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and government forces continue to threaten security and disrupt daily life.

title_en: Precarious Lull as AFC/M23 Consolidates Positions in Buhimba-Kazinga-Katoy Triangle
excerpt_en: NORTH KIVU March 4, 2026 - A temporary calm was reported on Wednesday, March 4, 2026, in the Buhimba-Kazinga-Katoy triangle, spanning Masisi and Walikale territories in North Kivu, following several days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazale
body_en:
NORTH KIVU March 4, 2026 - A temporary calm was reported on Wednesday, March 4, 2026, in the Buhimba-Kazinga-Katoy triangle, spanning Masisi and Walikale territories in North Kivu, following several days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo forces.
Local sources indicate that fighting has been largely silent since Tuesday afternoon, after AFC/M23 recaptured Kazinga. This strategic area connects multiple localities in both Masisi and Walikale and has experienced significant population displacement due to recent hostilities.
Despite the lull, the situation remains highly volatile. Observers report that rebel reinforcements were seen moving from Nyabiondo and Kasopo towards Buhimba and Kazinga, and from Kasenyi towards Katoy. Security sources confirmed the movements but provided no details on the scale or objectives.
Analysts warn that these troop movements may signal the next phase of rebel offensives against government positions or attempts to seize additional surrounding localities, raising fears of a renewed escalation in fighting and a worsening humanitarian situation in this part of North Kivu.

title_en: James Swan Appointed Head of MONUSCO
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced the appointment of American diplomat James Swan as the new Special Representative for the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). He s
body_en:
KINSHASA March 5, 2026 - United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced the appointment of American diplomat James Swan as the new Special Representative for the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). He succeeds Bintou Keita of Guinea, whom Guterres thanked for her service to the mission.
James Swan is a seasoned diplomat with extensive experience in Africa, particularly in countries undergoing complex political and security transitions. He previously served as Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Somalia and headed the United Nations Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) from March 2025, having also held the role on an interim basis since May 2024. He led the United Nations Mission in Somalia (UNSOM) from 2019 to 2022.
Before joining the UN, Swan completed a 32-year career in the U.S. government, with several assignments related to the DRC, including as U.S. Ambassador to the DRC (2013-2016), Deputy Chief of Staff at the U.S. Embassy (2001-2004), and Desk Officer (1996-1998). He also served as U.S. Ambassador to Djibouti (2008-2011), Special Representative for Somalia (2011-2013), and Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs (2006-2008), with additional postings in Congo-Brazzaville, Somalia, Cameroon, Nicaragua, and Haiti.
Swan holds degrees from Georgetown University, Johns Hopkins University, and the National War College, and is fluent in French.

title: FARDC Seizes CRP/Zaire Coalition Ammunition Stockpile
excerpt: DJUGU March 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced the seizure of a significant ammunition stockpile belonging to the CRP/Zaire coalition, a rebel alliance led by Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province. Lieutenant Jules Ngongo, spokesperso
title_en: FARDC Seizes CRP/Zaire Coalition Ammunition Stockpile
excerpt_en: DJUGU March 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced the seizure of a significant ammunition stockpile belonging to the CRP/Zaire coalition, a rebel alliance led by Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province. Lieutenant Jules Ngongo, spokesperso
body_en:
DJUGU March 5, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced the seizure of a significant ammunition stockpile belonging to the CRP/Zaire coalition, a rebel alliance led by Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.
Lieutenant Jules Ngongo, spokesperson for the provincial government, said the stockpile included ammunition of all calibers, RPG-7 rockets, AK-47s, PKM machine guns, and Castor bombs, previously hidden at the coalition’s headquarters in Jingo, Mambisa chiefdom, Djugu territory. He described the operation as a “fatal blow” to the coalition’s logistical capabilities and credited local populations for their collaboration with the army.
“The Armed Forces will continue to search everywhere weapons and ammunition have been hidden. This is a major military achievement. Credit goes to the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces for deploying the necessary resources to progressively pacify Ituri, area by area,” Lieutenant Ngongo said.
The CRP/Zaire coalition has been responsible for escalating violence in Djugu territory since last year, targeting both FARDC positions and civilians, leading to mass displacements and numerous deaths. The FARDC said it intends to continue operations to fully restore security and state authority across the province, which remains under a state of siege since 2021.
Authorities maintain that military interventions have achieved some progress, though pacification efforts in Ituri are ongoing, and the humanitarian situation remains precarious, with a high number of displaced persons and civilian victims.

title_en: AFC/M23 Withdraws from Buabo and Ndete, Wazalendo Reoccupy Villages
excerpt_en: MASISI March 6, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have withdrawn without engaging in clashes from the villages of Buabo and Ndete in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory, North Kivu. Local sources reported the rebels’ absence early Thursday morning, March 5, after several days of occ
body_en:
MASISI March 6, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have withdrawn without engaging in clashes from the villages of Buabo and Ndete in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory, North Kivu.
Local sources reported the rebels’ absence early Thursday morning, March 5, after several days of occupation following previous fighting with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and their Wazalendo allies.
Following the withdrawal, the Wazalendo forces reoccupied Buabo and Ndete on the morning of Friday, March 6, according to security sources. The reasons behind the rebels’ departure remain unclear, though some observers suggest that military pressure and encirclement strategies by government forces may have influenced the decision.
The security situation in Masisi territory remains volatile, with continued troop movements and sporadic clashes reported in surrounding villages. These ongoing hostilities are causing further civilian displacement, aggravating the already fragile humanitarian conditions in the region.
