title: Congo Airways Faces Critical Challenges; President Tshisekedi Demands Realistic Recovery Plan
excerpt: March 22, 2026 - The national airline, Congo Airways SA, remains in a precarious state, posing legal, financial, and reputational risks for the state as a shareholder. Despite multiple government-led recovery efforts, the airline continues to struggle with operational inefficienc
title_en: Congo Airways Faces Critical Challenges; President Tshisekedi Demands Realistic Recovery Plan
excerpt_en: March 22, 2026 - The national airline, Congo Airways SA, remains in a precarious state, posing legal, financial, and reputational risks for the state as a shareholder. Despite multiple government-led recovery efforts, the airline continues to struggle with operational inefficienc
body_en:
March 22, 2026 - The national airline, Congo Airways SA, remains in a precarious state, posing legal, financial, and reputational risks for the state as a shareholder. Despite multiple government-led recovery efforts, the airline continues to struggle with operational inefficiencies, raising concerns over rising air travel costs in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
During the 83rd Council of Ministers meeting held on March 20 at the African Union City complex, President Félix Tshisekedi reviewed the findings of a joint investigation launched in December 2025. The mission, comprising the General Inspectorate of Finance (IGF), the High Council of the Portfolio, and the Civil Aviation Authority, assessed the company's administrative, financial, and operational management.
According to the report, Congo Airways continues to face serious operational problems, despite the emergency recovery plan initiated in 2023 and reinforced in 2024. The President stressed that, without rigorous planning and strengthened governance, these issues could undermine the airline’s fleet renewal process and jeopardize the strategic interests of the state.
“The situation is all the more concerning given that, in the absence of proper governance, it could compromise the renewal of the airline fleet recently acquired by the National Social Security Fund,” the meeting minutes note. President Tshisekedi also called for the state to meet its financial obligations, including outstanding taxes, to provide the company with the resources necessary for recovery.
The President instructed the Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Transport and Communications, the Minister of Finance, and the Minister of State Enterprises, under the supervision of the Prime Minister, to develop a realistic, rigorously structured financial recovery plan. This plan must include internal controls, regulatory compliance, audits, human resource management, and systematic reporting to the State.
“These measures must underpin a profound restructuring of managerial governance, restore management discipline, strengthen executive accountability, and improve transparency,” President Tshisekedi emphasized. He also highlighted the need for a model ensuring financial sustainability, operational efficiency, and long-term competitiveness, safeguarding the state’s strategic interests.
This is not the government’s first attempt to revive Congo Airways. In 2024, a five-year business plan was proposed, including the acquisition of three A320 aircraft and measures to maintain the airline’s Air Operator Certificate (AOC) and IATA accreditation. A moratorium granted by the International Air Transport Association prevented the loss of these credentials.
The President warned that domestic air travel demand continues to rise, while supply remains insufficient. The underutilization of international routes has led to lost revenue for the country, despite Congo’s portfolio of over 52 international air traffic rights, many of which currently benefit foreign airlines.
With these challenges, the government now faces a pivotal moment: crafting a realistic recovery plan that restores Congo Airways’ operational viability while protecting the state’s financial and strategic interests.

title: President Tshisekedi Demands “Urgent” Completion of Governance Framework for Inga III Project
excerpt: March 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has called for the rapid finalization of the governance framework for the Grand Inga hydropower project, emphasizing its strategic importance in transforming the Democratic Republic of Congo into a continental energy powerhouse. Speakin
title_en: President Tshisekedi Demands “Urgent” Completion of Governance Framework for Inga III Project
excerpt_en: March 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has called for the rapid finalization of the governance framework for the Grand Inga hydropower project, emphasizing its strategic importance in transforming the Democratic Republic of Congo into a continental energy powerhouse. Speakin
body_en:
March 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has called for the rapid finalization of the governance framework for the Grand Inga hydropower project, emphasizing its strategic importance in transforming the Democratic Republic of Congo into a continental energy powerhouse.
Speaking at the 83rd Council of Ministers meeting on March 20 at the African Union City in Kinshasa, the President underscored the project’s potential to generate 42,000 MW, describing it as a “sovereign lever for industrialization, ecological transition, and social dignity” for the Congolese people.
“The Grand Inga project embodies a historic choice: to sustainably electrify the country, support youth employment, drive green growth based on a responsible mining industry, and assert the DRC’s energy leadership in Africa,” he said.
President Tshisekedi highlighted the critical role of world-class partnerships in realizing this vision. He recalled the World Bank’s approval of a US$1 billion loan for the Inga III development program on June 3, 2025, of which US$250 million is already available. He stressed that, with the financing agreements now in force as of February 2, 2026, the project’s governance framework must be finalized urgently.
To this end, he instructed relevant ministries-including Industry, National Education, Mines, Environment, Higher Education, Employment, and Water Resources and Electricity-and the Kongo Central provincial government to complete the necessary memoranda of understanding with the Agency for the Development and Promotion of the Grand Inga Project (ADPI-RDC) within 60 days. Signed protocols must be forwarded to donors no later than April 3, 2026.
The President also urged the government to review and finalize the Inga bill, aiming for adoption at the March 27 Council of Ministers meeting and submission to Parliament by March 31, 2026. This legislation is considered a key prerequisite for unlocking World Bank support. A progress report on these directives is expected within five days.
President Tshisekedi framed the Inga III program as central to addressing the country’s energy deficit, noting that only 21% of Congolese households currently have access to electricity. The project is a cornerstone of the National Energy Pact and aligns with Africa-wide initiatives, such as Mission 300, aimed at expanding energy access. By 2030, the government aims to increase electricity coverage to 62% of the population, leveraging Inga III to accelerate institutional reforms, infrastructure development, and private sector engagement.
The Inga III development program, structured in multi-phase investments, will also target local communities, job creation, and infrastructure, laying the foundation for sustainable energy growth well beyond 2030, according to the World Bank.

title: 295 New Officers Join FARDC After Completing Training at Kananga Military Academy
excerpt: Kananga, Kasai-Central March 22, 2026 - A total of 295 newly trained officers were formally inducted into the ranks of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during a swearing-in ceremony at the Kananga Military Academy on Saturday, March 21. The event was a
title_en: 295 New Officers Join FARDC After Completing Training at Kananga Military Academy
excerpt_en: Kananga, Kasai-Central March 22, 2026 - A total of 295 newly trained officers were formally inducted into the ranks of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during a swearing-in ceremony at the Kananga Military Academy on Saturday, March 21. The event was a
body_en:
Kananga, Kasai-Central March 22, 2026 - A total of 295 newly trained officers were formally inducted into the ranks of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) during a swearing-in ceremony at the Kananga Military Academy on Saturday, March 21.
The event was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, the Chief of the General Staff, Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe, and several FARDC generals. The graduates represent the 37th ordinary session of the academy, which over three years trained nearly 400 cadets in applied and military sciences, as well as social and strategic military studies.
In his address, Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita highlighted the importance of preparing officers capable of effectively responding to current security challenges. He stressed that the graduates must embody the strength and authority of the State, maintain discipline, and uphold the laws of the Republic in defense of the Congolese people.
“Your choice to join the leadership of your institution requires constant adaptation to the evolving socio-professional environment, the nation’s ambitions, and the legitimate demands of defending the national territory,” the Minister said. “You must be the reassuring face of defense and security, particularly where authority is questioned or challenged.”
The ceremony included military honors, the swearing-in of officers, and the formal presentation of rank insignia, confirming the graduates as second lieutenants. A military parade and group photo concluded the event, much to the delight of families in attendance.
This induction strengthens the FARDC at a critical time, as the army faces continued aggression from Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 forces, which occupy significant parts of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. With these new officers, the FARDC aims to bolster its operational capacity and safeguard the territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: ARE Signs Strategic Partnership with ENA to Certify Managers and Staff
excerpt: Kinshasa March 20, 2026 - The Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE) of the Democratic Republic of Congo has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National School of Administration (ENA), establishing a strategic partnership to provide high-level certification training fo
title_en: ARE Signs Strategic Partnership with ENA to Certify Managers and Staff
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 20, 2026 - The Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE) of the Democratic Republic of Congo has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National School of Administration (ENA), establishing a strategic partnership to provide high-level certification training fo
body_en:
Kinshasa March 20, 2026 - The Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE) of the Democratic Republic of Congo has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National School of Administration (ENA), establishing a strategic partnership to provide high-level certification training for its managers and staff.
The agreement, formalized during a ceremony at ENA on Friday, March 20, aims to strengthen ARE’s capacity in project management, public procurement, financial modeling, environmental safeguards, and risk management. Staff will benefit from internationally recognized certifications, including PMP for directors and CAPM for managers, enhancing the Authority’s project-oriented structure.
In her remarks, ARE Director General Soraya Aziz-Moto emphasized the strategic significance of the partnership. “ENA has established itself as the absolute benchmark for training administrative elites in our country,” she said. “This collaboration demonstrates that our administration can reinvent itself from within, combining institutional heritage with modern management methods.”
She added that certification programs will equip ARE staff with universal project management skills, ensuring precision, efficiency, and accountability in license processing and audits. “By certifying our teams, we are not simply seeking qualifications, but guaranteeing surgical precision and record-breaking efficiency in processing each license application and audit,” she stated.
Soraya Aziz-Moto also highlighted the broader goal of transforming the public administration sector. “Become the faces of this new era where every regulated kilowatt is managed with certified expertise, for the greater good of our nation,” she urged.
Speaking at the ceremony, ENA Director General Tombola Muke praised ARE’s initiative and confirmed that the collaboration, which includes PMI and ISO certifications, will commence promptly. He emphasized that this training will provide ARE with the skilled human capital needed to enhance governance and align with international standards while supporting sustainable development in the DRC.

body_en:
Mitsamiouli, Comoros March 20, 2026 - Sixteen Congolese nationals were among the victims of a shipwreck off the coast of Mitsamiouli, Comoros, on March 18, local authorities reported.
The official list released by Comorian authorities confirms 18 deaths in total, including two Burundians, while a separate statement from the Civil Security Directorate General indicated that the boat, carrying migrants from the East African coast, had capsized at sea.
The provisional report notes 12 confirmed dead, 12 missing, and 30 survivors, who are currently receiving treatment at Mitsamiouli hospital.
Rescue operations are ongoing, with Comorian authorities cautioning about the dangers of irregular sea crossings.

title: HRW Documents Missing Opposition Members in CNC Detention Centers
excerpt: DRC March 11, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for
title_en: HRW Documents Missing Opposition Members in CNC Detention Centers
excerpt_en: DRC March 11, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for
body_en:
DRC March 11, 2026 - Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for the missing or, preferably, bring them before a judge.
According to HRW, the National Cyber Defense Council (CNC)-a body attached to the Presidency of the Republic-has been used since March 2025 to arrest and detain political opponents arbitrarily through Congolese security forces.
“Over the past year, Congolese security forces have secretly arrested and detained people on trumped-up charges in the heart of the capital,” said Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at HRW. “In most cases, the arrests appear to be politically motivated or involve individuals suspected of supporting armed groups in eastern DRC.”
HRW reached its conclusions after contacting 34 individuals, including nine former CNC detainees and 11 relatives. Accounts describe arrests conducted by uniformed Republican Guard and National Police officers, as well as plainclothes personnel, often at night. Several detainees reported being blindfolded during transport to or between CNC detention centers, without being shown any arrest warrants.
Detentions reportedly began at facilities within the Stade des Martyrs or CNC offices at the National Transport Office (ONATRA) in Kinshasa, before transferring detainees to other secret locations, including private rooms or hotels. Interrogations focused on alleged collusion with AFC/M23 rebels, rather than cyber-related offenses.
HRW also accuses the CNC of expanding its powers through arrests, interrogations, and secret detentions without judicial oversight.
Between December 2025 and January 2026, opposition members, including loyalists of former President Joseph Kabila, were arrested at night in their homes. Many went missing, while others were later found in CNC facilities before transfer to judicial authorities. Some high-profile figures, such as Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary and Aubin Minaku, both former leaders of the ruling PPRD party, were reportedly held in secret.
This report underscores growing concerns over political repression, arbitrary detention, and the lack of judicial oversight in Kinshasa, raising alarms about the treatment of opposition members amid the ongoing eastern DRC conflict.

title: Journalist Serge Sindani Released After Ten Days in Detention
excerpt: Kisangani March 13, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani. Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in th
title_en: Journalist Serge Sindani Released After Ten Days in Detention
excerpt_en: Kisangani March 13, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani. Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in th
body_en:
Kisangani March 13, 2026 - Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani.
Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in the city center by ANR agents and was held incommunicado until March 9, without access to his family or colleagues. The reasons for his arrest only became clear after his lawyer was granted access to him earlier this week.
According to his attorney, Christian Kambi, the journalist was suspected of maintaining contacts with individuals linked to the M23 rebellion. However, relatives of Sindani stated that the allegations were based on his past membership in a WhatsApp group known as “Génération Naanga,” described as inactive since the departure of Corneille Nangaa to join the rebellion.
Following his release, Sindani has begun preventive medical treatment, according to his entourage.
This incident follows a previous arrest a few months earlier, during which he was detained for three days after allegedly publishing a photo showing military equipment near Kisangani International Airport.
The case has once again raised concerns about press freedom and the conditions of detention in the country, particularly regarding access to legal representation and communication with relatives.

title: Three Kidnapped Teachers Freed After Ransom Payment
excerpt: Rutshuru March 14, 2026 - Three of the five teachers abducted earlier this week in Busanza, in Rutshuru Territory, have been released after a ransom payment, while two others remain in captivity, according to local education authorities. The victims were kidnapped on March 11 by
title_en: Three Kidnapped Teachers Freed After Ransom Payment
excerpt_en: Rutshuru March 14, 2026 - Three of the five teachers abducted earlier this week in Busanza, in Rutshuru Territory, have been released after a ransom payment, while two others remain in captivity, according to local education authorities. The victims were kidnapped on March 11 by
body_en:
Rutshuru March 14, 2026 - Three of the five teachers abducted earlier this week in Busanza, in Rutshuru Territory, have been released after a ransom payment, while two others remain in captivity, according to local education authorities.
The victims were kidnapped on March 11 by unidentified armed men in two separate incidents targeting teachers and school officials traveling along key roads in the area. According to Félix Gakiza, spokesperson for the local teachers’ union, approximately $1,000 was paid to secure the release of three of the hostages.
Those freed were part of a group of five education workers, including a school principal, a deputy headmaster, and several teachers from different primary schools in the Busanza area. The remaining two victims are still being held by their captors.
The first abduction occurred on the Kinyandonyi-Rugarama road in Mutego, where two school officials and their driver were intercepted while returning from Kiwanja. A second incident took place hours later on the Kitagoma-Kidandari road, where three other educators, including a school director, were kidnapped.
The teachers’ union strongly condemned the attacks, highlighting the growing insecurity targeting educators in conflict-affected zones. “Teachers are apolitical actors and deserve protection,” Gakiza stressed, calling on security forces to guarantee their safety as they continue working under increasingly difficult and dangerous conditions.
These incidents underscore the persistent security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where civilians, including education personnel, remain vulnerable to kidnappings and armed violence.

title: Two Wazalendo Commanders Arrested in Walikale for “Uncivil and Anti-Patriotic” Acts
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - The General Staff of the 34th Military Region announced the arrest of two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and acts of violence severely affecting civilians. The arrested leaders are Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COP
title_en: Two Wazalendo Commanders Arrested in Walikale for “Uncivil and Anti-Patriotic” Acts
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - The General Staff of the 34th Military Region announced the arrest of two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and acts of violence severely affecting civilians. The arrested leaders are Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COP
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - The General Staff of the 34th Military Region announced the arrest of two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and acts of violence severely affecting civilians.
The arrested leaders are Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COPACO (Coalition of Patriots in Congo) movement, and Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi. Military authorities cited their “uncivil and anti-patriotic behavior,” which contradicts the mission of the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP).
The commanders have been engaged in fratricidal clashes for nearly 17 months, with serious consequences for both their groups and the civilian population. Despite mediation efforts by traditional authorities and local leaders, confrontations continued.
The most recent clashes, between February 15-18, 2026, in the Tushunguti and Zirhalo areas of the Buhavu chiefdom in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, resulted in 14 civilian deaths, 7 serious injuries, 7 cases of sexual violence, and numerous instances of looting.
The army stated that these actions have strayed from the VDP’s original mission. Both commanders, described as repeat offenders, will now answer to competent authorities under the jurisdiction of the 34th Military Region.

title: Goma and Bukavu’s Judicial System Crumbles Amid Ongoing Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt: March 14, 2026 - The judicial infrastructure in Goma and Bukavu has been devastated by the ongoing war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, as the AFC/M23 rebellion, allegedly backed by Rwanda, clashes with government forces. A UN report covering 2025 reveals that the destruc
title_en: Goma and Bukavu’s Judicial System Crumbles Amid Ongoing Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt_en: March 14, 2026 - The judicial infrastructure in Goma and Bukavu has been devastated by the ongoing war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, as the AFC/M23 rebellion, allegedly backed by Rwanda, clashes with government forces. A UN report covering 2025 reveals that the destruc
body_en:
March 14, 2026 - The judicial infrastructure in Goma and Bukavu has been devastated by the ongoing war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, as the AFC/M23 rebellion, allegedly backed by Rwanda, clashes with government forces.
A UN report covering 2025 reveals that the destruction of courts and prisons led to the loss of nearly all case files, including 36 serious crime cases, 11 of which involved conflict-related sexual violence.
The report also highlights a rise in inter-ethnic tensions and hate speech, particularly against the Tutsi and Banyamulenge communities. Thirteen incidents were documented, six of which met international standards for hate speech, directly targeting Kinyarwanda-speaking populations.
Despite these challenges, the UN continued its humanitarian and rights programs. Through the “Digital Identification for All” initiative, a campaign promoting birth registration reached three million people in Kinshasa, registering 174,439 children and increasing the birth registration rate in Masina from 28% in 2023 to 68% in 2025.
The UN also organized 93 training and awareness sessions, reaching nearly 5,000 participants, including civil society representatives, human rights defenders, government officials, media professionals, and security personnel.
Human rights observers warn that abuses continue amid escalating violence in North Kivu and South Kivu, compounded by a shortage of humanitarian aid. Civilians remain at risk as hostilities persist, including reports of drone strikes. The government denies targeting civilians.

title_en: Opposition Figure Parole Kamizelo Sentenced, Plans Appeal
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 - Opposition leader Parole Kamizelo, also known as “Maîtrisable” (Controllable), has been sentenced to two years of penal servitude for insulting the Head of State. The ruling was issued by the Kinshasa/Ngaliema Magistrate's Court on March 9, 2026. Kamizel
body_en:
Kinshasa March 15, 2026 - Opposition leader Parole Kamizelo, also known as “Maîtrisable” (Controllable), has been sentenced to two years of penal servitude for insulting the Head of State. The ruling was issued by the Kinshasa/Ngaliema Magistrate's Court on March 9, 2026.
Kamizelo’s legal team immediately announced plans to appeal the decision. Attorney Eloi Mubilansama described the verdict as “fundamentally unjust,” citing violations of fair trial guarantees and human rights protections under both the constitution and international law.
Known for his assertive presence on political programs, Kamizelo has gained notoriety since mid-2025 for his outspoken criticism of the Kinshasa government. During his trial, prosecutors accused him of questioning the official marriage of President Félix Tshisekedi, including repeatedly requesting photographic proof on television.
The PPRD party, to which Kamizelo belongs, has also called for his release and that of other officials reportedly held incommunicado, labeling their detention as arbitrary.

title: DRC Launches Economic and Financial Criminal Court to Fight Corruption
excerpt: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 - The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, mar
title_en: DRC Launches Economic and Financial Criminal Court to Fight Corruption
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 - The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, mar
body_en:
Kinshasa March 15, 2026 - The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, marking a significant step in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s ongoing efforts to combat corruption, embezzlement, and other financial offenses.
Based in Kinshasa, the new court will include both a trial chamber and an appeals chamber, holding exclusive jurisdiction over cases involving public officials and serious financial misconduct. Its mandate covers corruption, bribery, embezzlement of public funds, counterfeiting, and forgery.
Officials note that the creation of this specialized court is the culmination of reforms initiated under former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba. The initiative aims to improve the speed, clarity, and efficiency of judicial proceedings while reinforcing public and international confidence in the rule of law.
The establishment of the Economic and Financial Criminal Court is seen as a critical step toward strengthening accountability in the DRC’s public sector and deterring economic crimes that have long hindered development.

title: Etienne Davignon to Stand Trial for Role in Patrice Lumumba’s Assassination
excerpt: March 17, 2026 - Belgian courts have approved that Etienne Davignon will stand trial over his alleged involvement in the kidnapping and transfer of Patrice Lumumba, which ultimately led to the assassination of the first Prime Minister of independent Congo on January 17, 1961. Dav
title_en: Etienne Davignon to Stand Trial for Role in Patrice Lumumba’s Assassination
excerpt_en: March 17, 2026 - Belgian courts have approved that Etienne Davignon will stand trial over his alleged involvement in the kidnapping and transfer of Patrice Lumumba, which ultimately led to the assassination of the first Prime Minister of independent Congo on January 17, 1961. Dav
body_en:
March 17, 2026 - Belgian courts have approved that Etienne Davignon will stand trial over his alleged involvement in the kidnapping and transfer of Patrice Lumumba, which ultimately led to the assassination of the first Prime Minister of independent Congo on January 17, 1961.
Davignon, the last surviving of the eleven Belgians targeted in a war crimes complaint filed in 2011 by Lumumba’s children, will face proceedings following a decade-long investigation.
Speaking during a briefing in Brussels, members of the Lumumba family emphasized that the lawsuit is not about reparations, but about establishing legal accountability for colonial-era crimes.
"The primary objective of this lawsuit is for justice to be served for Patrice Lumumba, and to acknowledge that what he suffered was a crime," said Blandine Lumumba, wife of François Lumumba. "The consequences of this act continue to affect the family, and this justice will help heal wounds for both the family and the country."
The Belgian federal prosecutor’s office accuses Davignon of unlawfully detaining and transferring a prisoner of war, depriving him of a fair trial, and subjecting him to humiliating and degrading treatment, though no intent to kill has been established. At the time, Davignon was a young diplomat intern stationed in Kinshasa and Brazzaville, and his position allegedly allowed him knowledge of the planned arrest and transfer.
Lumumba was overthrown, arrested, and transferred to Katanga, where he was executed alongside Maurice M’Polo and Joseph Okito, amid Cold War tensions, regional secessions, and foreign interference.
Six grandchildren of Lumumba are participating in the proceedings as civil parties, seeking a public acknowledgment of Belgian responsibility and a debate on what they call a disastrous colonial crime.
The defense argued the case should be dismissed due to the statute of limitations, citing the extended time since the events. Davignon, a prominent figure in Belgian political and industrial circles after the 1960s, now faces a legal reckoning fueled by decades of historical research, including the work of historian Ludo De Witte, who documented Belgian civilian and military involvement in Lumumba’s execution.

title: $1.9 Million Seized at N’djili Airport in High-Stakes Operation
excerpt: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have seized approximately $1.9 million at N’djili International Airport, in a move described by the Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Guillaume Ngefa, as “lawful and complete.” According to an of
title_en: $1.9 Million Seized at N’djili Airport in High-Stakes Operation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have seized approximately $1.9 million at N’djili International Airport, in a move described by the Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Guillaume Ngefa, as “lawful and complete.” According to an of
body_en:
Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have seized approximately $1.9 million at N’djili International Airport, in a move described by the Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Guillaume Ngefa, as “lawful and complete.”
According to an official directive sent to the Prosecutor General at the Court of Cassation, the interception was carried out amid suspicions that the funds were intended to be unlawfully manipulated or distributed, in clear violation of Congolese law.
The minister’s letter highlights that such actions could constitute serious offenses, including embezzlement of seized assets, corruption, obstruction of justice, and money laundering. Judicial authorities were instructed to seize the money immediately, place it under official seal in the presence of judicial police officers, and document the circumstances thoroughly, including the identification of all individuals involved.
Under the law on combating money laundering and terrorism financing, the funds are to be deposited with the Central Bank of Congo, and the reports transmitted to the National Financial Intelligence Unit (CENAREF). The Minister also demanded a full legal investigation to determine the origin of the funds, classify potential criminal actions, and hold responsible parties accountable.
“This is a highly sensitive matter for public order and the credibility of our institutions,” the minister stated, emphasizing that any attempt by officials to handle or dispose of the funds outside the legal framework will be prosecuted with the utmost rigor.
The authorities have committed to keeping the public informed of the progress of the case.

title: Former Energy Minister and Renowned Jurist Jeannot Matadi Nenga Ngamanda Dies at 76
excerpt: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo mourns the loss of Jeannot Matadi Nenga Ngamanda, former Minister of Energy and Water Resources, who passed away on March 22 at the age of 76. Born on September 14, 1949, in Kifumu, Ngamanda was a towering figure in both
title_en: Former Energy Minister and Renowned Jurist Jeannot Matadi Nenga Ngamanda Dies at 76
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo mourns the loss of Jeannot Matadi Nenga Ngamanda, former Minister of Energy and Water Resources, who passed away on March 22 at the age of 76. Born on September 14, 1949, in Kifumu, Ngamanda was a towering figure in both
body_en:
Kinshasa March 22, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo mourns the loss of Jeannot Matadi Nenga Ngamanda, former Minister of Energy and Water Resources, who passed away on March 22 at the age of 76.
Born on September 14, 1949, in Kifumu, Ngamanda was a towering figure in both the Congolese legal and political spheres. He earned a doctorate in law from the University of Paris X-Nanterre, a law degree from the National University of Zaire, and a diploma in human rights from Columbia University, New York. He also held a bachelor’s degree in philosophy and literature from Lovanium University in Kinshasa.
A practicing lawyer since 1975, Ngamanda appeared before the Court of Cassation and the Council of State throughout his career. He was a member of the Standing Commission for the Reform of Congolese Law and held leadership positions within the legal profession, including President of the Kinshasa Bar Association, President of the Young Lawyers Association of Zaire, and Vice-President of the International Association of Young Lawyers.
In politics, he served as Minister of Energy and Water Resources under the Matata II government, was a member of parliament, and held the position of Second Vice-President of the National Assembly during the transitional period.
Ngamanda was also a prolific author, publishing several influential works on law and governance, including Private Judicial Law (2006), The Right to a Fair Trial (2002), The Question of Judicial Power in the Democratic Republic of Congo (2001), and Zaire: An Improbable Democracy (1997).
His passing marks the end of a distinguished career dedicated to law, justice, and public service, leaving a lasting legacy in Congolese legal and political life.

title: ICRC Ready to Support Transfer of Over 5,000 Released FARDC Soldiers to Kinshasa
excerpt: Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The soldiers, members of the FAR
title_en: ICRC Ready to Support Transfer of Over 5,000 Released FARDC Soldiers to Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The soldiers, members of the FAR
body_en:
Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The soldiers, members of the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC), were handed over on March 2 at the Rumangabo military camp in Rutshuru Territory, according to a statement issued by the AFC/M23. The group indicated that the troops, captured on various frontlines, would be transferred to Kinshasa under ICRC supervision.
“The AFC/M23 informs the public that it has handed over more than 5,000 FARDC members to the ICRC. They will be repatriated to Kinshasa under its supervision,” the statement said.
Responding to the announcement, François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in Kinshasa, confirmed the organization’s position. “As a neutral intermediary, the ICRC stands ready to assist with such an operation, with the agreement of all parties,” he stated.
This large-scale prisoner transfer forms part of confidence-building measures agreed upon within the Doha mediation process, aimed at easing tensions between Kinshasa and the rebellion. The AFC/M23 says the release reflects its commitment to international humanitarian law and efforts to de-escalate the conflict.
The ICRC has previously played a similar role. In May 2025, it facilitated the transfer of more than 1,300 disarmed soldiers from Goma to Kinshasa.
However, despite this development, tensions remain high. The AFC/M23, often described as Rwandan-backed rebels, accuses the government of Kinshasa of refusing to release detained fighters, including individuals allegedly arrested “simply because of their appearance.”
The group further alleges ongoing ceasefire violations, claiming that government forces continue military operations targeting civilian populations and property, accusations that risk undermining fragile peace efforts in eastern DRC.
While the planned transfer could mark a significant step toward de-escalation, its success will depend on cooperation between all parties and sustained commitment to the broader peace process.

excerpt: Masisi March 10, 2026 - The strategic town of Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory, has returned to the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) following a military offensive conducted on Monday, March 9. According to lo

body_en:
Masisi March 10, 2026 - The strategic town of Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory, has returned to the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) following a military offensive conducted on Monday, March 9.
According to local sources, the town had been under AFC/M23 rebel occupation for nearly two weeks before being retaken by government forces, supported by the Wazalendo militia, in a coordinated operation aimed at reasserting state authority in the area.
The offensive triggered intense fighting, with both heavy and light weapons used throughout the day. By evening, however, the situation had stabilized, and a relative calm returned to the town.
The clashes forced many civilians to flee into surrounding bush areas, where they are now facing dire humanitarian conditions, including lack of shelter, food, and access to basic services.
The recapture of Kazinga follows recent rebel withdrawals from nearby localities, including Buabo and Ndete, signaling a possible shift in territorial dynamics in parts of North Kivu.
Regarded as a strategic position within the Osso Banyungu sector, Kazinga’s return to government control strengthens the military foothold of loyalist forces and reinforces their presence in this volatile region of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: FARDC Recaptures Mukole After Clashes with AFC/M23 Rebels
excerpt: Walikale March 10, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
title_en: FARDC Recaptures Mukole After Clashes with AFC/M23 Rebels
excerpt_en: Walikale March 10, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
body_en:
Walikale March 10, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
The clashes, which took place on Monday, March 9, were part of a targeted offensive by government-aligned forces to reclaim the area, which had been under rebel occupation for several days. The operation resulted in the recapture of Mukole, marking another shift in the evolving security dynamics in North Kivu.
Following the confrontation, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly withdrew toward Ihula, a locality situated along the border between Walikale and Rutshuru Territory.
The fighting left several casualties, including at least three reported deaths among the rebels, with injuries recorded on both sides.
The violence also triggered civilian displacement, as residents fled into nearby bush areas to escape the hostilities. As of Tuesday morning, a fragile calm had returned to Mukole, although many inhabitants remain in temporary refuge, uncertain about their safety.
The recapture of Mukole provides FARDC and allied forces with a key strategic advantage, enabling them to monitor surrounding areas, including Ihula and Kalonge in Walikale, as well as Kalembe in neighboring Masisi Territory-areas that remain under AFC/M23 control.

title: February Sees Record Surge in Airstrikes Against M23 Positions
excerpt: DRC March 11, 2026 - The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED. On February 24, a drone strike ki
title_en: February Sees Record Surge in Airstrikes Against M23 Positions
excerpt_en: DRC March 11, 2026 - The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED. On February 24, a drone strike ki
body_en:
DRC March 11, 2026 - The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED.
On February 24, a drone strike killed Willy Ngoma, M23’s military spokesperson, along with several senior leaders near Rubaya, a strategic coltan mining hub producing around 15% of global supply and generating roughly $800,000 per month for the rebels.
The FARDC has deployed CH-4 and TAI Anka drones, fighter jets, and attack helicopters, alongside Wazalendo militia ground offensives in Mwenga, Masisi, and Fizi. Private military actors, including Vectus, associated with Erik Prince, also support operations linked to mining revenue control.
Despite the air campaign, M23 launched counter-offensives in late February, forcing temporary withdrawals of FARDC units. The rebels also conducted suicide drone attacks on the Kisangani military command center, a hub for FARDC air operations.

Despite the air campaign, M23 launched counter-offensives in late February, forcing temporary withdrawals of FARDC units. The rebels also conducted suicide drone attacks on the Kisangani military command center, a hub for FARDC air operations.

title: Drone Strikes Hit Goma, International Reactions Pour In
excerpt: Goma DRC March 11, 2026 - The city of Goma, capital of North Kivu Province and currently under AFC/M23 rebel control, was struck by drone attacks early Wednesday morning. The strikes, attributed by the AFC/M23 rebellion to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FAR
title_en: Drone Strikes Hit Goma, International Reactions Pour In
excerpt_en: Goma DRC March 11, 2026 - The city of Goma, capital of North Kivu Province and currently under AFC/M23 rebel control, was struck by drone attacks early Wednesday morning. The strikes, attributed by the AFC/M23 rebellion to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FAR
body_en:
Goma DRC March 11, 2026 - The city of Goma, capital of North Kivu Province and currently under AFC/M23 rebel control, was struck by drone attacks early Wednesday morning. The strikes, attributed by the AFC/M23 rebellion to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), caused material damage and at least three deaths, including a French UNICEF aid worker, as well as two other civilians.
The Himbi neighborhood, near Lake Kivu, was particularly affected, with homes and civilian infrastructure damaged. The city has been controlled by the AFC/M23 since January 2025 and serves as the rebellion’s operational headquarters in North and South Kivu provinces.
Rebel Response
Bertrand Bisimwa, deputy coordinator of AFC/M23, condemned the strikes, accusing the Kinshasa government of violating the ceasefire and deploring the silence of international partners. He described the attacks as part of a campaign to “decapitate the revolution” and force an escalation of regional conflict.
Corneille Nangaa, political coordinator of AFC/M23, specified that the strikes were allegedly targeting the leadership of the rebellion and key political figures, including General Sultani Makenga, Bertrand Bisimwa, and Freddy Kaniki. He affirmed the rebellion’s commitment to protecting civilians in areas under its control and warned that any escalation would be the responsibility of Kinshasa.
International Reactions
Belgium :Maxime Patrick Robert Albert Prévot, Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, condemned the attacks as a violation of the ceasefire, emphasizing that such strikes against humanitarian workers are rising. “The drone attack in Goma claimed the lives of a humanitarian worker and civilians. The guns must fall silent. Let’s negotiate,” he said on X, offering condolences to the victims’ families.
European Union :  Commissioner Hadja Lahbib, responsible for Crisis Preparedness and Equality, called for respect for international humanitarian law and protection of humanitarian personnel. “All parties must respect their commitments. Humanitarian workers must never be targeted,” she warned.
France :President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the death of the French UNICEF aid worker and urged all parties to respect international humanitarian law. “These aid workers are committed to saving lives in a precarious and dangerous environment,” he said, offering condolences to the family, colleagues, and loved ones of the deceased.
United Nations : The UN mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) strongly condemned the escalation, describing the attacks as deeply concerning and reiterating that targeting UN personnel could constitute war crimes under the Rome Statute. Bruno Lemarquis, Acting Head of MONUSCO, called for a swift, independent investigation into the drone strikes and urged both parties to prioritize political dialogue to protect civilians.
International Contact Group (ICG) :  Earlier, on March 5, members of the ICG, including Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, the UK, and the USA, had expressed concern over ceasefire violations in eastern DRC, highlighting the use of drones in military operations that endanger civilians. They stressed that there is no military solution to the conflict and called for urgent negotiations.
Context
The strikes come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts, including the Washington and Doha processes, supported by the African Union. Despite these initiatives, tensions remain high between Kinshasa and Kigali, as well as between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23, limiting progress on the ground.
The attacks also reignite concern over humanitarian security, as the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) had recorded a decrease in incidents affecting aid workers in January 2026, but the Goma attack demonstrates that risks remain severe.

title: Three Wazalendo Fighters Killed in Clash with FARDC Soldier in Mungazi
excerpt: Walikale March 11, 2026 - Tensions erupted on Tuesday, March 10, in Mungazi, located in the Luberike area of Walikale Territory, following a deadly confrontation between a FARDC soldier and members of the Wazalendo militia. The clash left three Wazalendo fighters dead. The incide

excerpt_en: Walikale March 11, 2026 - Tensions erupted on Tuesday, March 10, in Mungazi, located in the Luberike area of Walikale Territory, following a deadly confrontation between a FARDC soldier and members of the Wazalendo militia. The clash left three Wazalendo fighters dead. The incide
body_en:
Walikale March 11, 2026 - Tensions erupted on Tuesday, March 10, in Mungazi, located in the Luberike area of Walikale Territory, following a deadly confrontation between a FARDC soldier and members of the Wazalendo militia. The clash left three Wazalendo fighters dead.
The incident reportedly stemmed from a misunderstanding between the soldier and the group of militia members, though the exact cause of the dispute remains unclear. During the altercation, the soldier opened fire, killing all three Wazalendo fighters instantly.
The situation was brought under control within hours, but the gunfire caused panic among the local population. The soldier involved was detained by military authorities and is currently under questioning.
The three victims were buried locally on Wednesday morning. This incident is part of a pattern of clashes in Mungazi, where previous confrontations between FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters in 2025 also resulted in deaths and injuries.

body_en:
Walikale March 11, 2026 - Heavy clashes erupted Wednesday morning, March 11, in Mikumbi, located in the Luberike area of Walikale Territory, between the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo militia, and AFC/M23 rebels.
The confrontation reportedly began around 9:00 a.m. after an attack by AFC/M23 forces on government positions. The exchange of fire has suspended traffic on the Mungazi-Kashebere road, a vital route in the region.
Fighting continued in the vicinity of Mikumbi until early afternoon. Local authorities and security sources warned civilians to remain vigilant and avoid the area while the situation develops.

title_en: Mining Sites Attacked by Unidentified Armed Men
excerpt_en: Mambasa March 12, 2026 - Several mining sites in the Mambasa territory of Ituri Province were targeted by unidentified armed men late Wednesday evening, March 12. The assaults caused panic among residents and miners, forcing many to abandon their homes. Some spent the night outdo
body_en:
Mambasa March 12, 2026 - Several mining sites in the Mambasa territory of Ituri Province were targeted by unidentified armed men late Wednesday evening, March 12. The assaults caused panic among residents and miners, forcing many to abandon their homes. Some spent the night outdoors, while others fled to Badengaido, the main town of the Bombo chiefdom.
According to local civil society sources, the attacks began around 8:00 p.m. in the Enjewa mining group, including the areas of Muchacha and Mavuvu, and continued into Thursday morning, creating a state of severe insecurity. Several houses were reportedly burned down, and many families were left displaced.
Jospin Paluku Mbowa, coordinator of the New Congolese Civil Society in Mambasa, said, “The residents and miners were taken by surprise. Many had to leave their homes, and several families spent the night outside. These assailants stormed various mining sites, causing widespread fear.”
Local authorities have not yet released an official assessment of the material damage or potential casualties.
The Mambasa territory, rich in mineral resources, remains vulnerable to armed incursions, putting the safety of civilians and mining operations at continual risk.

title: Fifteen Hostages Freed from ADF Captivity
excerpt: FARDC-UPDF Operations March 13, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) has announced the release of 15 hostages held by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The civilians were freed during joint military operatio
title_en: Fifteen Hostages Freed from ADF Captivity
excerpt_en: FARDC-UPDF Operations March 13, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) has announced the release of 15 hostages held by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The civilians were freed during joint military operatio
body_en:
FARDC-UPDF Operations March 13, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) has announced the release of 15 hostages held by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The civilians were freed during joint military operations conducted with the Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF), part of an ongoing campaign launched in 2021 to dismantle ADF networks in North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
The former hostages were officially handed over on March 12 in Beni for social reintegration, marking another step in efforts to restore community stability in conflict-affected areas.
“We welcome this act of bravery by our security forces, alongside our UPDF partners,” said Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson for Operation Sokola 1. “These individuals were kidnapped by the enemy and held in captivity for four to eight months. Their return is a moment of relief for their communities.”
The FARDC called on local populations to avoid stigmatizing the former hostages, emphasizing that they were victims of abduction. Civil society groups also welcomed their return, praising the military for its continued efforts to rescue civilians.
These 15 individuals join hundreds of previously freed hostages, released during successive operations that have led to the recapture of key ADF strongholds and the neutralization of several fighters and commanders.
Despite these successes, the ADF remains a persistent security threat in eastern DRC, with continued attacks against civilians highlighting the need for sustained military pressure and regional cooperation.

excerpt: Walikale March 13, 2026 - A group of AFC/M23 fighters who recently surrendered in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has arrived in Pinga, located in Walikale Territory, following their defection from rebel ranks. The fighters, initially reported to have laid down their arms in
title_en: Surrender of AFC/M23 Fighters Reported in Pinga
excerpt_en: Walikale March 13, 2026 - A group of AFC/M23 fighters who recently surrendered in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has arrived in Pinga, located in Walikale Territory, following their defection from rebel ranks. The fighters, initially reported to have laid down their arms in
body_en:
Walikale March 13, 2026 - A group of AFC/M23 fighters who recently surrendered in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has arrived in Pinga, located in Walikale Territory, following their defection from rebel ranks.
The fighters, initially reported to have laid down their arms in Chanjikiro, in the Kisimba group, were transferred to Pinga on March 10. Local and administrative authorities confirmed their presence and indicated that they are currently being held under supervision pending further decisions regarding their status and reintegration process.
According to information gathered on the ground, the former combatants cited intensified military pressure from the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo militia, as a key factor behind their surrender. They also pointed to harsh living conditions and internal suffering within the rebel movement.
This development comes amid escalating military operations and renewed clashes across Walikale, where government forces and their allies are seeking to reclaim rebel-held positions. The surrender is seen as a potential sign of strain within AFC/M23 ranks, as pressure continues to mount on multiple frontlines in North Kivu.

excerpt_en: Masisi March 14, 2026 - Intense fighting broke out early Saturday in Malemo, a village in the Bashali Mokoto area of Masisi Territory, pitting AFC/M23 rebels against Wazalendo fighters. According to local sources, the clashes began around 5:00 a.m. following an offensive launched
body_en:
Masisi March 14, 2026 - Intense fighting broke out early Saturday in Malemo, a village in the Bashali Mokoto area of Masisi Territory, pitting AFC/M23 rebels against Wazalendo fighters.
According to local sources, the clashes began around 5:00 a.m. following an offensive launched by Wazalendo forces on rebel-held positions along the Kalembe-Mpety axis. Since then, heavy and light weapons fire has been reported, with loud explosions echoing across the surrounding area.
The violence has triggered panic among civilians in nearby villages, many of whom have remained confined to their homes amid fears of further escalation.
These clashes come just 24 hours after similar fighting in Kashuga, located in the same Bashali Mokoto area, where Wazalendo forces also attacked AFC/M23 positions. The renewed offensives suggest mounting pressure on rebel strongholds in this part of Masisi.
As of midday Saturday, the situation remained highly volatile, with no confirmed casualty figures. Local sources in nearby Kalembe reported continued tension and uncertainty as fighting persisted.

title: Islamic State-Linked ADF Fighters Launch Deadly Attack on Muchacha Mining Site
excerpt: Mambasa, Ituri March 15, 2026 - A deadly attack struck the Muchacha and Mavuvu mining sites on the night of March 11-12, carried out by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters linked to the Islamic State. The assault targeted operations run by the Chinese company Kimia Mining, le
title_en: Islamic State-Linked ADF Fighters Launch Deadly Attack on Muchacha Mining Site
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri March 15, 2026 - A deadly attack struck the Muchacha and Mavuvu mining sites on the night of March 11-12, carried out by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters linked to the Islamic State. The assault targeted operations run by the Chinese company Kimia Mining, le
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri March 15, 2026 - A deadly attack struck the Muchacha and Mavuvu mining sites on the night of March 11-12, carried out by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters linked to the Islamic State. The assault targeted operations run by the Chinese company Kimia Mining, leaving equipment destroyed and multiple casualties in its wake.
Images released by the Islamic State show trucks, tractors, and camps set ablaze, highlighting the scale of the destruction. More than a dozen people were killed, and around 100 civilians were taken hostage during the attack. The ADF also ambushed a Congolese army unit that arrived to intervene, resulting in the death of an officer and several soldiers.
The fighters involved are believed to belong to the Batike and Bapaitumba groups, two factions that have operated in the Bapere sector of North Kivu for over a year. Following previous clashes in Budhudea, the ADF relocated to new positions in Botambisi, Mapendano, and Mabuo, maintaining control over gold mining sites where they collect taxes and coordinate attacks.
Officials note that the ADF’s movement toward Muchacha was part of a search for new hideouts, evading Congolese and Ugandan military operations supported by Wazalendo trackers. The fighters crossed the Lenda River, entering Ituri territory, where they executed the coordinated assault.
Since June 2024, Bapere has hosted multiple ADF factions, including the group led by Abwakasi, notorious for its brutal and lethal operations. Analysts warn that the Muchacha region is strategically significant, forming part of the Kivu-Kinshasa Green Corridor, a critical route supplying Kisangani and Kinshasa with essential agricultural products, raising concerns about the ongoing threat to the region.

title_en: Militiamen Surrender in Kwamouth, Dozens of Weapons Turned Over
excerpt_en: Kwamouth, Kwango - March 15, 2026 - A new surrender of militiamen was reported on March 12 in Kinsele, where sixteen weapons of war were handed over to the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo). The cache included one PKM, ten AK-47s, five 12-gauge shotguns, an
body_en:
Kwamouth, Kwango - March 15, 2026 - A new surrender of militiamen was reported on March 12 in Kinsele, where sixteen weapons of war were handed over to the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo). The cache included one PKM, ten AK-47s, five 12-gauge shotguns, and ammunition, marking another step in the ongoing disarmament and demobilization process in the region.
The handover ceremony was attended by a delegation from the Minister Delegate for Defense, Eliezer Ntambwe, highlighting the government’s continued efforts to reintegrate former combatants.
The Eleventh Military Region confirmed that several Mobondo fighters participated in the surrender. According to Captain Antony Mualushayi, spokesperson for the FARDC, the fighters and recovered weapons were transferred to Kinshasa to continue the formal demobilization process.
During a broader peacekeeping mission in Kwamouth territory, Minister Eliezer Ntambwe announced the earlier surrender of over 600 Mobondo militiamen, many of whom were sent to Kaniama Kasese to join the National Service. Some of the former fighters expressed interest in military training, though placement at Kaniama Kasese was declared mandatory.
This latest surrender reflects ongoing progress in efforts to stabilize the region and reintegrate armed groups into national structures.

title_en: Wazalendo Retake Malemo Village After Fierce Fighting Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - The village of Malemo, in the Bashali Mokoto group, was recaptured by the Wazalendo on Saturday, March 14, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels. Clashes began early in the morning and continued throughout the day along the Kalembe-M
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - The village of Malemo, in the Bashali Mokoto group, was recaptured by the Wazalendo on Saturday, March 14, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
Clashes began early in the morning and continued throughout the day along the Kalembe-Mpety axis, a strategic corridor linking Masisi to Walikale territory. By early evening, Wazalendo forces succeeded in dislodging the rebels from the village. Some AFC/M23 fighters retreated toward Kalembe, while others moved to Mindjendje and Mpety in Kisimba.
The recapture of Malemo is strategically significant, as it severs the link between Kalembe and Mpety, one of the main strongholds and logistical centers of the AFC/M23 in the Pinga region.
These clashes follow intense fighting reported 24 hours earlier in Kashuga, also in Bashali Mokoto, where the Wazalendo withdrew, leaving control to the AFC/M23 rebels.
The security situation remains highly volatile across several villages in Masisi and Walikale, with ongoing troop movements and clashes fueling civilian anxiety.

title: CNC-ALPC Urges Vigilance After Discovery of Explosive Devices in Walikale
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - Residents of Walikale are being urged to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of several unexploded devices and munitions in and around the town. The devices were found on March 14, 2026, by local residents and handed over to the
title_en: CNC-ALPC Urges Vigilance After Discovery of Explosive Devices in Walikale
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - Residents of Walikale are being urged to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of several unexploded devices and munitions in and around the town. The devices were found on March 14, 2026, by local residents and handed over to the
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - Residents of Walikale are being urged to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of several unexploded devices and munitions in and around the town.
The devices were found on March 14, 2026, by local residents and handed over to the CNC-ALPC (National Commission for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons). The discoveries have reignited security concerns, nearly ten months after the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels from Walikale town.
Officials reported the recovery of two 60mm mortar shells and a significant quantity of various munitions, thanks to the cooperation of the local population. One mortar shell was found in Mubanda, about four kilometers east of Walikale, by workers rehabilitating the Walikale-Kibua road, previously used by rebels. Another bomb was discovered on a residential property in Ndjingala, while additional munitions were recovered in the Nyalusukula neighborhood.
The head of the main CNC-ALPC post in Walikale, Clément Kubuya Ndoole, stressed the need for residents to avoid handling suspicious objects and to immediately alert authorities if explosives are found. He emphasized that community collaboration remains essential for long-term security and the gradual cleansing of Walikale from explosive remnants.
Since the start of its awareness campaign on unexploded ordnance, the CNC-ALPC has collected over 500 kilograms of munitions, which are awaiting destruction.

excerpt_en: Goma, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - At least thirteen Wazalendo fighters were killed and three captured during an overnight attack in the Mugunga neighborhood in western Goma, according to AFC/M23 officials. The Wazalendo militiamen, coming from Virunga National Park, reportedly en
body_en:
Goma, North Kivu March 16, 2026 - At least thirteen Wazalendo fighters were killed and three captured during an overnight attack in the Mugunga neighborhood in western Goma, according to AFC/M23 officials.
The Wazalendo militiamen, coming from Virunga National Park, reportedly entered the city with the aim of looting population property, especially food supplies. Clashes with AFC/M23 patrols triggered an exchange of heavy and light weapons fire, causing widespread fear among residents.
Residents reported a restless night, with a bomb explosion at the CCLK roundabout damaging shops and bars and causing a fire. Witnesses described the incident as terror-inducing, reflecting the growing security concerns in Goma and surrounding areas.
The attack comes amid ongoing tensions following recent drone strikes on the city, which killed three people, including a French UNICEF employee. AFC/M23 and the government have publicly blamed each other for the drone strikes, while the Paris anti-terrorism prosecutor's office has opened an investigation.
The security situation in Goma remains highly volatile, with residents and authorities on alert after the escalation of violence.

Walikale, North Kivu - March 16, 2026 - Cases of rape and looting were reported on March 13, 2026, along the Tuonane-Busurungi road in the Waloa Loanda group, Walikale territory.
According to local authorities, unidentified armed men intercepted civilians on the road. Several women were raped, while money and belongings were stolen. Administrative sources in the Wanianga sector confirmed the attacks.
Security services have launched investigations to identify the perpetrators and bring them before judicial authorities. Victims are receiving treatment at local health facilities.
The assaults occurred in March, a month dedicated to defending and promoting women’s rights, raising serious concerns about the persistent insecurity in rural areas of Walikale territory.

title: Several Civilians Killed and Village Burned in Major ADF Attack in Babesua
excerpt: Mambasa, Ituri March 17, 2026 - Islamist militants from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) carried out a deadly attack on the evening of March 16 in Babesua, a village 12 kilometers from Badengaido, in Ituri province. At least ten civilians were killed, and numerous homes and veh

excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri March 17, 2026 - Islamist militants from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) carried out a deadly attack on the evening of March 16 in Babesua, a village 12 kilometers from Badengaido, in Ituri province. At least ten civilians were killed, and numerous homes and veh
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri March 17, 2026 - Islamist militants from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) carried out a deadly attack on the evening of March 16 in Babesua, a village 12 kilometers from Badengaido, in Ituri province. At least ten civilians were killed, and numerous homes and vehicles were burned.
Journalists on the scene reported unbearable images of bodies lying on the ground and the village completely destroyed. The attack also targeted rangers of the Okapi Wildlife Reserve (RFO), some of whom sought refuge inside the forest.
The New Congolese Civil Society has called on authorities to resume joint FARDC-UPDF operations in the area, citing the vast territory of Mambasa (covering 54% of Ituri) and the limited presence of soldiers.
This attack comes days after another ADF assault on the Muchacha and Mavuvu mining sites on the night of March 11-12, which killed at least 17 people. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, releasing images showing burning trucks, tractors, and camps.
The Muchacha region connects to Badengaido, Niania, and the Okapi Wildlife Reserve, forming part of the Kivu-Kinshasa Green Corridor, a strategic route supplying Kisangani and Kinshasa with essential agricultural products.

Masisi, North Kivu March 17, 2026 - The village of Malemo, located between Kalembe and Mpety in the Pinga area, has once again fallen under the control of AFC/M23 rebels, following the withdrawal of Wazalendo forces.
The Wazalendo had retaken Malemo on March 14 after fierce clashes with the rebels, but their presence lasted only three days. On the morning of March 17, the Wazalendo voluntarily withdrew, allowing the AFC/M23 rebels to reoccupy the village without resistance.

The security situation around Pinga remains highly volatile, with frequent clashes and shifting positions between AFC/M23 rebels and government forces supported by Wazalendo, leaving the civilian population exposed to continued insecurity.

Uvira, South Kivu March 17, 2026 - Intense fighting erupted on the morning of March 17 between the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition and AFC/M23 rebels in the villages of Kabunango and Runingu, in the Ruzizi Plain. Both sides have reinforced positions, according to local sources.
The clashes, involving heavy and light weapons fire, have heightened fear among residents in this border region with Burundi. Additional fighting has been reported in Biriba, Kasambura, and Runingu, with the rebels describing the confrontation as a “widespread war” waged by government forces and their allies.
As a result, traffic on National Route 5, the main road connecting Bukavu and Uvira, has been disrupted, complicating movement and transport in the area.

title_en: Death Toll Rises to 19 in ADF Attack on Babesua Village
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri March 17, 2026 - The death toll from the ADF attack in Babesua village has risen to at least 19 civilians killed, following the assault on the evening of March 16. The village lies 12 kilometers from Badengaido, along the Kisangani road. A Red Cross team on the gro
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri March 17, 2026 - The death toll from the ADF attack in Babesua village has risen to at least 19 civilians killed, following the assault on the evening of March 16. The village lies 12 kilometers from Badengaido, along the Kisangani road.
A Red Cross team on the ground confirmed the updated toll, reporting extensive destruction, including burned houses and a truck. The scale of the violence mirrors recent ADF attacks on the Muchacha and Mavuvu mining sites, which left at least 17 dead days earlier.
Despite ongoing joint military operations by the Congolese and Ugandan armies, the ADF militants continue to advance and carry out attacks.
According to the United Nations Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO), ADF fighters were responsible for 465 attacks in 2025, resulting in 1,749 victims, including women and children. Summary executions accounted for nearly half of these incidents.
The renewed violence in Mambasa territory is spreading fear to neighboring areas such as Bafwasende, where reports indicate population displacement as residents flee ongoing attacks.

title_en: ADF Advance Toward Walese-Karo Raises Fears of Strategic Regrouping
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri March 19, 2026 - Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have intensified their movement along the Kisangani axis, advancing from Bapere (Lubero) into the Okapi Wildlife Reserve following the recent attack on a Chinese mining site in Muchacha. On the night of March
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri March 19, 2026 - Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have intensified their movement along the Kisangani axis, advancing from Bapere (Lubero) into the Okapi Wildlife Reserve following the recent attack on a Chinese mining site in Muchacha.
On the night of March 17, the group attacked the Babesua patrol post, leaving at least 19 civilians dead, according to local reports. The attack has heightened fears among local leaders that the ADF is attempting to push toward the Walese-Karo region, a known stronghold of Musa Baluku, along the Mambasa-Isiro axis via Nduye.
Recent FARDC-UPDF operations reportedly targeted ADF positions in Walese-Karo, prompting concerns that the fighters are seeking to regroup or extract their leader. Local communities fear the group could bypass Epulu and Mambasa to reinforce Baluku before retreating to the Bapere forests, whose terrain offers a strategic advantage.
Observers note that such movements reflect a recurring ADF survival strategy, involving mobility and reinforcement between factions. Similar operations were reported after June 2024, when fighters moved across Bandulu, Bilulu, and Midede to support units under pressure from joint military offensives.
The evolving situation underscores the fluid and adaptive nature of ADF operations, raising concerns over regional security and the risk of further attacks along key corridors in eastern DRC.

title_en: FARDC Repels Mai-Mai Incursion in Nkonga, Mitwaba Territory
excerpt_en: Mitwaba, Haut-Katanga March 20, 2026 - The FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) repelled a Mai-Mai Bakatanga incursion on March 19 in the village of Nkonga, about 35 kilometers from Mitwaba. Gunfire was reported between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., as armed assailants b
body_en:
Mitwaba, Haut-Katanga March 20, 2026 - The FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) repelled a Mai-Mai Bakatanga incursion on March 19 in the village of Nkonga, about 35 kilometers from Mitwaba.
Gunfire was reported between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., as armed assailants briefly entered the area before being pushed back by the army. Local authorities described the attack as sudden and sporadic, with the situation now under control.
Officials confirmed that the FARDC regained full control of the village after routing the attackers, while provincial authorities reported a return to calm.
The incident highlights the persistent insecurity in Mitwaba territory, where Mai-Mai Bakatanga militias continue to carry out recurrent attacks against state forces. Recent violence has also targeted Upemba National Park, where at least five rangers were killed in similar incursions.
Despite military reinforcements, the security situation remains fragile, with key routes around Mitwaba becoming increasingly dangerous due to the presence of armed groups.

excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu - March 22, 2026 - Violent clashes broke out early Sunday in the village of Kanune, in the Ikobo area, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. Hostilities began around 5:00 AM, when the Wazalendo launched an offensive on rebel positions. Since then, su
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu - March 22, 2026 - Violent clashes broke out early Sunday in the village of Kanune, in the Ikobo area, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
Hostilities began around 5:00 AM, when the Wazalendo launched an offensive on rebel positions. Since then, sustained heavy and light weapons fire has gripped the area, spreading fear among residents.
The civilian population remains confined indoors, fearing stray bullets and the intensity of the fighting. No official information has yet been released regarding casualties or damage.
The Ikobo area, under AFC/M23 control for nearly a year, has seen a volatile security situation, with recent reinforcements reported in nearby localities, particularly toward Kisimba. Analysts suggest these movements may have weakened some rebel positions, prompting the current Wazalendo attempt to retake the territory.
The situation remains fluid, raising serious concerns for the safety of civilians in a region already affected by prolonged conflict.
