title: Rwanda Earns Over Rwf15 Billion from Agricultural Exports in Five Days
excerpt: Kigali, 13 March 2026 - Rwanda generated more than Rwf15 billion from agricultural and livestock exports between 9 and 13 March 2026, according to the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB). During the five-day period, the country exported 8,300 tonnes of products,
title_en: Rwanda Earns Over Rwf15 Billion from Agricultural Exports in Five Days
excerpt_en: Kigali, 13 March 2026 - Rwanda generated more than Rwf15 billion from agricultural and livestock exports between 9 and 13 March 2026, according to the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB). During the five-day period, the country exported 8,300 tonnes of products,
body_en:
Kigali, 13 March 2026 - Rwanda generated more than Rwf15 billion from agricultural and livestock exports between 9 and 13 March 2026, according to the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB).
During the five-day period, the country exported 8,300 tonnes of products, including coffee, tea, fruits, vegetables, flowers, cereals, and livestock products.
Coffee remained the top export, with 571 tonnes generating over Rwf5.4 billion, followed by tea exports of 649 tonnes worth more than Rwf2.7 billion.
Other exports included vegetables (431 tonnes), fruits (221 tonnes), and flowers (30 tonnes), contributing hundreds of millions of francs in revenue.
Rwanda also exported over 6,200 tonnes of additional agricultural products, alongside 248 tonnes of animal products, further boosting earnings.
Key export destinations included the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, the United Arab Emirates, France, Germany, and several African markets.
The figures highlight the continued importance of agriculture as a driver of export revenue and economic growth for Rwanda.

title: Rwanda Reports Decline in Attempted Bank Frauds Despite Rising Cyber Threats
excerpt: Kigali, 19 March 2026 - Rwanda recorded around 3,000 attempted bank frauds in 2025, down from 5,000 cases the previous year, according to the Central Bank. Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye announced the figures during a press conference following discussions on monetary policy and f
title_en: Rwanda Reports Decline in Attempted Bank Frauds Despite Rising Cyber Threats
excerpt_en: Kigali, 19 March 2026 - Rwanda recorded around 3,000 attempted bank frauds in 2025, down from 5,000 cases the previous year, according to the Central Bank. Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye announced the figures during a press conference following discussions on monetary policy and f
body_en:
Kigali, 19 March 2026 - Rwanda recorded around 3,000 attempted bank frauds in 2025, down from 5,000 cases the previous year, according to the Central Bank.
Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye announced the figures during a press conference following discussions on monetary policy and financial stability, noting that while cyber-related threats persist, overall incidents have declined.
She confirmed that authorities are investigating a recent attempted fraud targeting Equity Bank Rwanda, adding that some of the affected funds have already been recovered.
Hakuziyaremye attributed many of the incidents to the growing use of digital financial services, which has introduced new vulnerabilities even as the sector modernizes.
“Cyber-related theft exists, but what matters is how we protect ourselves and respond when incidents occur,” she said, emphasizing the importance of prevention and accountability.
The Central Bank also indicated that mechanisms are in place to ensure that affected customers are reimbursed within a short period, with efforts underway to return funds within seven days in confirmed cases.
Rwanda’s financial sector includes 11 commercial banks, alongside microfinance institutions and SACCOs, all of which have strengthened cybersecurity measures in recent years.
Globally, cybercrime remains a growing challenge, with estimates suggesting that a cyberattack occurs every few seconds, underscoring the need for continued vigilance.

title: Rwanda Launches Cybersecurity Training Center Targeting One Million Learners by 2030
excerpt: Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A new cybersecurity training and consultancy center aimed at strengthening digital skills across Africa has been launched in Rwanda, with an ambitious target of training more than one million people by 2030. The initiative, known as International Cybersec
title_en: Rwanda Launches Cybersecurity Training Center Targeting One Million Learners by 2030
excerpt_en: Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A new cybersecurity training and consultancy center aimed at strengthening digital skills across Africa has been launched in Rwanda, with an ambitious target of training more than one million people by 2030. The initiative, known as International Cybersec
body_en:
Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A new cybersecurity training and consultancy center aimed at strengthening digital skills across Africa has been launched in Rwanda, with an ambitious target of training more than one million people by 2030.
The initiative, known as International Cybersecurity Community for Africa (ICCA), was officially unveiled on March 20 by a consortium of international students specializing in technology.
ICCA Chief Executive Officer Petero Niyodusenga said the idea was born while he and his colleagues were studying in the United States, where they began informally teaching cybersecurity to fellow students.
“We realized there was a strong need to expand this knowledge to Africa,” he said, noting the continent’s rapid digital transformation and the growing importance of cybersecurity in both public and private sectors.
He pointed to Rwanda’s national development strategies, including National Strategy for Transformation phases, which emphasize infrastructure development and increased integration of technology across government services, businesses, and daily life.
“As digital adoption grows, so does the need for skilled professionals to protect systems and data,” Niyodusenga added.
Rwanda has set a national target of equipping one million people-primarily youth-with coding and basic technology skills by 2029, alongside training an additional 500,000 individuals in advanced digital competencies.
An official from the Ministry of ICT and Innovation, Grace Niwemukiza, stressed that achieving these goals will require strong collaboration across sectors.
“The government cannot achieve this alone,” Niwemukiza said. “Partnerships between public institutions, private companies, and initiatives like ICCA are essential to meet our national ambitions.”
The center plans to offer training to a wide range of beneficiaries, including university students, IT professionals, entrepreneurs, and corporate staff seeking to strengthen their cybersecurity capabilities.
Students have welcomed the initiative as a practical complement to academic learning. Carnegie Mellon University Africa student Aklile Mamo said the program would provide hands-on experience often missing from classroom instruction.
“Learning in school is important, but applying that knowledge in real-world situations is critical,” he said.
ICCA also aims to expand its reach beyond Rwanda, with plans to operate across multiple African countries, including Gabon, Republic of the Congo, Kenya, and Ethiopia, as part of a broader effort to build cybersecurity capacity across the continent.

title: Rwandan Women in Mozambique Urged to Seize Opportunities at International Women’s Day Event
excerpt: Maputo, Mozambique March 8, 2026 - Rwandan women living in Mozambique have been encouraged to take full advantage of opportunities created by their home country, during celebrations marking International Women's Day in the capital, Maputo. The event, held at the Polana Serena Hot
title_en: Rwandan Women in Mozambique Urged to Seize Opportunities at International Women’s Day Event
excerpt_en: Maputo, Mozambique March 8, 2026 - Rwandan women living in Mozambique have been encouraged to take full advantage of opportunities created by their home country, during celebrations marking International Women's Day in the capital, Maputo. The event, held at the Polana Serena Hot
body_en:
Maputo, Mozambique March 8, 2026 - Rwandan women living in Mozambique have been encouraged to take full advantage of opportunities created by their home country, during celebrations marking International Women's Day in the capital, Maputo.
The event, held at the Polana Serena Hotel, brought together more than 120 participants, including government officials and members of the Rwandan diaspora. Among those in attendance were Ministerial Advisor Kenneth Viagem Marizane, Dr. Anabela Inguane representing the Maputo City Council, and Rwanda’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Donat Ndamage.
Speaking at the gathering, Sangwa Aline, Commissioner for Women’s Development within the Rwandan community in Mozambique, emphasized the importance of empowering women to fully utilize available opportunities.
“Let us seize the opportunities our country has given us, build our confidence, and strengthen our capabilities,” she said.
Ambassador Ndamage highlighted Rwanda’s progress in promoting gender equality, noting the significant representation of women in leadership positions.
“We must continue to build a society characterized by equality, justice, and sustainable development, where women and girls play a full role in governance and social life,” he stated.
He pointed out that women currently make up 63 percent of Rwanda’s lower house of parliament, alongside growing representation at district leadership levels, while acknowledging that further progress is still needed.
The ambassador also commended the leadership of Paul Kagame and Francisco Daniel Chapo for their commitment to advancing gender equality and inclusion, underscoring the strong ties between Rwanda and Mozambique.
Mozambican official Kenneth Viagem Marizane praised the contributions of Rwandan women in the country, describing them as hardworking and impactful members of society.
The event featured cultural performances, including traditional Rwandan music and dance, celebrating the achievements of women, followed by a social gathering among attendees.

title: Rwanda, United States Explore Expanded Healthcare Cooperation
excerpt: Kigali/Washington, March 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Sabin Nsanzimana, has held a series of high-level discussions in the United States aimed at strengthening collaboration between American and Rwandan healthcare institutions. During a visit to Ohio, the minister met
title_en: Rwanda, United States Explore Expanded Healthcare Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali/Washington, March 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Sabin Nsanzimana, has held a series of high-level discussions in the United States aimed at strengthening collaboration between American and Rwandan healthcare institutions. During a visit to Ohio, the minister met
body_en:
Kigali/Washington, March 12, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Sabin Nsanzimana, has held a series of high-level discussions in the United States aimed at strengthening collaboration between American and Rwandan healthcare institutions.
During a visit to Ohio, the minister met with Tomislav Mihaljevic, Chief Executive Officer of the Cleveland Clinic, to explore potential partnerships that could enhance healthcare delivery and medical expertise in Rwanda. The talks focused on how leading U.S. medical institutions could support Rwanda’s health system through knowledge exchange and institutional collaboration.
In a separate meeting, Nsanzimana held discussions with Marcello Fantoni, Director of International Relations at Kent State University. The two sides examined opportunities for academic cooperation, particularly in research and the expansion of study opportunities for Rwandan students in the United States.
The minister also met with Jeff Graham at the United States Department of State in Washington, DC, where discussions centered on global health security and bilateral cooperation. Key areas included the implementation of the Rwanda-U.S. Health Partnership Agreement.
The agreement, valued at $228 million, is designed to support Rwanda’s healthcare sector, with a significant portion allocated to combating HIV/AIDS, malaria, and other communicable diseases, as well as strengthening disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness.
Under the partnership, the United States is expected to contribute $158 million over the next five years, while Rwanda plans to increase its own health investment by up to $70 million to further improve national healthcare systems.

body_en:
Kigali, 19 March 2026 - The Ministry of Health (MINISANTE) announced plans to establish primary health centers in schools and crowded public spaces, including markets, to provide timely medical care to students and residents.
Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, emphasized that while some schools have medical facilities, they often lack trained personnel. The new initiative will help address injuries, infectious diseases, and mental health needs directly at schools and busy public areas.
Dr. Nsanzimana also highlighted Rwanda’s ongoing program to train nurses in secondary schools, projecting that by 2028, over 3,000 secondary-school-trained nurses will graduate. This initiative aims to strengthen healthcare delivery across clinics, schools, and local communities.
“Having a large number of trained nurses will ensure sufficient staff where they are most needed,” said Dr. Nsanzimana, noting that the program is part of a broader effort to quadruple Rwanda’s healthcare workforce.
The Ministry continues to receive requests from educational institutions to offer nursing programs, reflecting growing demand for skilled healthcare professionals in the country.

title: Rwandan Minister Warns Youth Against Drug Abuse, Links Responsibility to National Development
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
title_en: Rwandan Minister Warns Youth Against Drug Abuse, Links Responsibility to National Development
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
Speaking at Lycée de Kigali during the launch of the third phase of the Ndi Umunyarwanda program, the minister stressed that Rwanda’s youth-who make up the majority of the population-are central to the country’s future and must act responsibly.
“The country needs you, and if you are found to be addicted to drugs at a young age, you have betrayed it,” he said, emphasizing the link between individual choices and national progress.
Utumatwishima warned that risky behaviors, including drug use and poor health decisions, could permanently limit young people’s ability to contribute to society.
He also highlighted unity as a core value of the Ndi Umunyarwanda program, urging students to reject divisive groups and instead promote solidarity.
“The first value is unity. We must avoid anything that separates us and instead build groups that bring us together,” he said.
As part of this effort, he noted that school-based clubs-such as those under AERG-have been merged with unity and solidarity groups to foster cohesion among students.
The Director General of the Rwanda Basic Education Board, Nelson Mbarushimana, said the program complements formal civic education by instilling values such as integrity, truth-telling, and responsibility among students.
“We want students who stand for truth, who can denounce wrongdoing, and who are committed to building the country,” he said.
Students attending the event said the program has helped deepen their understanding of Rwanda’s history and their role in addressing misinformation, particularly on social media.
Irakoze Cyusa Prince Louis, a final-year student, said the discussions equip them to challenge narratives that distort the country’s past.
“We are encouraged to confront those who rewrite history. With the knowledge we gain, we are able to respond and defend the truth,” he said.
Another student, Mugisha Falhat, noted that the program also enables young people to engage their families and peers in conversations about unity and the dangers of divisive ideologies.
Officials say Ndi Umunyarwanda remains a key platform for promoting national unity, civic responsibility, and resilience among Rwanda’s youth.

excerpt_en: Kigali, 12 March 2026 - The Nyarugenge High Court has ruled that Barafinda Sekikubo Fred must remain in detention for 30 days, dismissing his appeal against the original detention order. The decision was read on 12 March 2026 in his absence. Barafinda, along with co-defendants Ma
body_en:
Kigali, 12 March 2026 - The Nyarugenge High Court has ruled that Barafinda Sekikubo Fred must remain in detention for 30 days, dismissing his appeal against the original detention order. The decision was read on 12 March 2026 in his absence.
Barafinda, along with co-defendants Mazimpaka Patrick, Nizeyimana Didier (Mucoma), Japhet Nkeramihigo, and Tumukunde, had challenged a prior ruling by the Kicukiro Primary Court, which ordered their detention on 3 March 2026.
The prosecution alleges that Barafinda, Mazimpaka, and Nkeramihigo conspired to create and broadcast YouTube interviews aimed at spreading rumors, inciting public dissent, and seeking protection from external donors who followed their content.
While Barafinda’s co-defendants were released on bail and prosecuted without detention on 9 March 2026, his own appeal for provisional release was argued by his brother in a closed-door hearing on the same day. The High Court ultimately rejected the appeal, confirming that Barafinda will remain in custody for the full 30-day period.

body_en:
Kigali, 13 March 2026 - The Kicukiro Primary Court has ordered 30 days of detention for Mike Habinshuti, a former advisor to Rwandan artist Bruce Melodie, as investigations continue into alleged cocaine trafficking.
Habinshuti was arrested on 18 February 2026 and is suspected of involvement in the purchase and distribution of illegal drugs.
According to preliminary findings, he is alleged to have bought cocaine worth 3,970,000 Rwandan francs between November and December 2025. Investigators claim the substances were sourced from a Nigerian supplier identified as James Ogbu and later distributed to various clients.
Habinshuti was previously known in the local entertainment industry for his association with Bruce Melodie, although the two are no longer working closely.
He had also been mentioned in sports management circles, notably within Rayon Sports, where he was appointed deputy director in November 2025 before the committee was later dissolved.
The case remains under investigation as authorities continue efforts to combat drug trafficking and related criminal activities.

title: Rwandan Minister Warns of Persistent Genocide Ideology, Accuses Habyarimana Family of Influence
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has warned that the ideology behind the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi remains present, cautioning against efforts to downplay or distort its legacy. Speaking at Lyc
title_en: Rwandan Minister Warns of Persistent Genocide Ideology, Accuses Habyarimana Family of Influence
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has warned that the ideology behind the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi remains present, cautioning against efforts to downplay or distort its legacy. Speaking at Lyc
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has warned that the ideology behind the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi remains present, cautioning against efforts to downplay or distort its legacy.
Speaking at Lycée de Kigali during the launch of the third phase of the Ndi Umunyarwanda program in schools, the minister said the spread of genocide ideology continues to be fueled in part by narratives linked to the family of former President Juvénal Habyarimana.
The Ndi Umunyarwanda program-implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Education Rwanda, the Ministry of Youth and Arts Development, the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement, and the Unity Club Intwararumuri-aims to strengthen historical awareness among students and counter misinformation about Rwanda’s past.
Utumatwishima said that, more than three decades after the genocide, its underlying ideology persists in subtle forms, including within families.
“You will often hear people attempting to absolve their relatives or conceal the truth about what happened, which contributes to the continued spread of this ideology,” he said.
He specifically cited members of the Habyarimana family, including Agathe Kanziga, accusing them of promoting narratives that deny or minimize the former president’s role in events leading up to the genocide.
“They claim innocence and attempt to mislead public opinion, even expressing ambitions to return and lead the country, while refusing to acknowledge historical responsibility,” he added.
The minister further alleged that such narratives are not limited to rhetoric, warning of potential links between individuals associated with the former regime and the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda, an armed group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and composed in part of individuals linked to the 1994 genocide.
“This is not something to take lightly. It goes beyond words and can translate into actions that threaten national security,” he said.
The remarks come amid heightened concerns expressed by President Paul Kagame, who recently criticized what he described as the continued presence and reception of individuals linked to the former regime in Kinshasa.
“The son of the former president and others continue to visit Kinshasa to expand collaboration with the FDLR, and they are being welcomed,” Kagame said during a meeting with diplomats on March 6.
Rwandan authorities say initiatives such as Ndi Umunyarwanda remain critical in educating younger generations and preventing the resurgence of divisive ideologies.

title: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Classroom Construction to Ease Overcrowding in Kamonyi
excerpt: Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development. The Rwanda National P
title_en: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Classroom Construction to Ease Overcrowding in Kamonyi
excerpt_en: Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development. The Rwanda National P
body_en:
Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 - Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development.
The Rwanda National Police and the Rwanda Defence Forces jointly laid the foundation stone for a 498 million Rwandan franc project at Kigese Technical Secondary School (TSS), located in Rugarika Sector. The project предусматривает the construction of 10 classrooms, along with a laboratory, administrative offices, sanitation facilities, and a dedicated space for girls.
Local officials say the expansion is expected to significantly reduce overcrowding at Kigese TSS and neighboring GS Masaka, where students have long faced congested and aging learning environments.
The Governor of the Southern Province, Alice Kayitesi, welcomed the initiative, describing it as a timely intervention to improve education conditions in the region.
“This school was overcrowded and had many old classrooms. These new facilities will address that challenge, and we are committed to supporting their completion,” she said.
Rwanda’s Minister of Defence, Juvenal Marizamunda, emphasized that the project reflects a broader strategy linking national security with socio-economic development.
“Security and development go hand in hand. Without security, there is no development, and it is difficult to sustain security in a country that does not address the welfare of its citizens,” he stated.
The construction effort is part of nationwide outreach activities launched by security institutions to strengthen ties with communities and contribute to social welfare programs.
Residents have also expressed optimism. A local parent, Uwimpayidufazizi, said the additional classrooms would create a better learning environment for children.
“This initiative will help our children study in better conditions and improve their chances of success,” she noted.
The development comes amid broader concerns over school infrastructure in Rwanda. In early 2025, the Ministry of Education Rwanda estimated that more than 26,000 additional classrooms are needed nationwide to adequately address overcrowding and improve learning conditions.

title: Rwandan Banking Executives Complete Advanced Leadership Training in Luxembourg

title_en: Rwandan Banking Executives Complete Advanced Leadership Training in Luxembourg
excerpt_en: Luxembourg March 9, 2026 - A group of 21 senior banking executives from Rwanda have graduated from a year-long leadership program designed to strengthen strategic capacity in the country’s financial sector. The initiative, known as the Advanced Banking Leadership Program (ABLP),
body_en:
Luxembourg March 9, 2026 - A group of 21 senior banking executives from Rwanda have graduated from a year-long leadership program designed to strengthen strategic capacity in the country’s financial sector.
The initiative, known as the Advanced Banking Leadership Program (ABLP), was delivered by the House of Training-ATTF in partnership with the Rwanda Bankers’ Association. The final phase of the program took place in Luxembourg, where participants were awarded certificates upon completion.
The ABLP is aimed at preparing high-potential banking professionals for senior leadership roles through specialized coursework, international case studies, and simulation-based training. It focuses on key areas shaping the modern financial industry, including financial technology, innovation, governance, and sustainable finance.
Participants represented several of Rwanda’s leading financial institutions, including BK, BRD, BPR Rwanda, Ecobank, NCBA, Bank of Africa, I&M Bank, Access Bank, and Equity Bank.
During the program’s final phase, participants engaged in the B@NKSIM simulation exercise, a computer-based platform that allows executives to model real-world banking scenarios. The exercise enables participants to make strategic decisions on financial management, risk, regulatory compliance, and operational performance.
Rwanda’s Ambassador to Luxembourg, Aurore Mimosa Munyangaju, congratulated the graduates, highlighting their role in advancing Rwanda’s banking sector.
She also expressed appreciation to the Government of Luxembourg, particularly the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Union, Defence, Development Cooperation and International Trade, for its support.
The program underscores growing cooperation between Rwanda and Luxembourg in financial sector development, as well as ongoing collaboration between the Rwanda Bankers’ Association and the House of Training-ATTF to build expertise and leadership capacity within Rwanda’s banking industry.

title: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Nationwide Welfare Projects Worth Rwf2.5 Billion
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda March 10, 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces and the Rwanda National Police have launched a nationwide campaign of social welfare and development projects valued at more than Rwf2.5 billion, marking the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation. The three-month initiat
title_en: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Nationwide Welfare Projects Worth Rwf2.5 Billion
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda March 10, 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces and the Rwanda National Police have launched a nationwide campaign of social welfare and development projects valued at more than Rwf2.5 billion, marking the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation. The three-month initiat
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda March 10, 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces and the Rwanda National Police have launched a nationwide campaign of social welfare and development projects valued at more than Rwf2.5 billion, marking the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation.
The three-month initiative, unveiled across multiple provinces, will focus on improving living conditions through interventions in healthcare, education, environmental protection, infrastructure, livestock distribution, and housing for vulnerable families.
In Kigali, the program was officially launched by Deputy Commissioner General Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, who emphasized that security institutions must go beyond maintaining order to actively contribute to citizens’ well-being.
The Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, praised the role of security forces in supporting key sectors such as education. Authorities announced that, in the capital alone, classrooms, sanitation facilities, and an Early Childhood Development (ECD) center in Ndera Sector will be constructed at a cost exceeding Rwf350 million.
Housing and Infrastructure Projects Across Provinces
In the Western Province, Police Commissioner Felix Namuhoranye, Governor Jean Bosco Ntibitura, and military officials launched the construction of 30 houses for vulnerable families in Nyabihu District.
“Protecting the country goes hand in hand with improving the welfare of its people,” Namuhoranye said, highlighting the practical impact of the initiative.
In the Southern Province, Defence Minister Juvenal Marizamunda and Governor Alice Kayitesi presided over the launch of new classroom construction at Kigese Technical Secondary School in Kamonyi District.
Marizamunda noted that the program strengthens cooperation between citizens, local authorities, and security institutions, stressing that sustainable security depends on development and public participation.
Healthcare and Connectivity in the North
In Northern Province, health-focused activities were launched at Byumba Teaching Hospital by State Minister Yvan Butera and senior military health officials. Services provided include surgery, pediatrics, dermatology, dentistry, and other specialized care, delivered jointly by military and civilian medical teams.
Meanwhile, authorities also launched the reconstruction of the Ryabazira bridge, a key link connecting communities in Musanze and Gakenke districts. Officials say the project will restore mobility, boost trade, and facilitate access to schools and markets.
Livelihood Support and Environmental Efforts in the East
In Eastern Province, the Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Agriculture, Solange Uwituze, distributed livestock-including cows and goats-to 32 vulnerable families in Kayonza District to support income generation and food security.
Chief of Defence Staff Mubarakh Muganga joined residents in Gatsibo District for environmental activities, including tree planting, urging sustained community participation.
“These initiatives have expanded from short-term efforts to long-term programs aimed at providing practical solutions,” he said.

title: Goma Residents Protest Drone Strike, Call on AFC/M23 to “Liberate” DR Congo
excerpt: Goma, March 12, 2026 - Residents of Goma took to the streets on Thursday to protest a recent drone strike attributed to the army of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, condemning the attack and calling on the AFC/M23 coalition to expand its control across the country. The demon
title_en: Goma Residents Protest Drone Strike, Call on AFC/M23 to “Liberate” DR Congo
excerpt_en: Goma, March 12, 2026 - Residents of Goma took to the streets on Thursday to protest a recent drone strike attributed to the army of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, condemning the attack and calling on the AFC/M23 coalition to expand its control across the country. The demon
body_en:
Goma, March 12, 2026 - Residents of Goma took to the streets on Thursday to protest a recent drone strike attributed to the army of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, condemning the attack and calling on the AFC/M23 coalition to expand its control across the country.
The demonstration followed a drone strike carried out on March 11 in the Himbi neighborhood, where at least three civilians were killed, including Karine Buisset, a French national working for the UNICEF. Local residents reported that drones targeted residential areas, sparking outrage among the population.
Responding to a call from civil society groups, demonstrators gathered in large numbers, halting daily activities to denounce what they described as indiscriminate attacks on civilian areas in North and South Kivu. Protesters also expressed condolences to the families of those killed.
The AFC/M23 coalition condemned the strike, accusing the Congolese government of violating the ceasefire agreement reached in Doha, Qatar, and criticized the international community for what it described as silence in the face of escalating violence.
Some demonstrators accused President Félix Tshisekedi of pursuing military actions at the expense of civilian lives, alleging that ongoing operations reflect a determination to maintain power despite the human cost.
According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, protesters called on the group to “remove Félix Tshisekedi from the entire country,” arguing that areas under government control have become centers of insecurity and violence.
Goma has been under the control of AFC/M23 since January 2025. The latest strike marks the first reported drone attack in the city in more than a year, heightening tensions in a region already affected by prolonged conflict.

title: 74 Burundians Voluntarily Return Home from Rwanda
excerpt: Bugesera, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Seventy-four Burundians, mostly men, who had sought refuge in Rwanda over the years, have voluntarily returned to their homeland, expressing gratitude for the peaceful environment they experienced during their stay. The group, comprising 30 women
title_en: 74 Burundians Voluntarily Return Home from Rwanda
excerpt_en: Bugesera, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Seventy-four Burundians, mostly men, who had sought refuge in Rwanda over the years, have voluntarily returned to their homeland, expressing gratitude for the peaceful environment they experienced during their stay. The group, comprising 30 women
body_en:
Bugesera, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Seventy-four Burundians, mostly men, who had sought refuge in Rwanda over the years, have voluntarily returned to their homeland, expressing gratitude for the peaceful environment they experienced during their stay.
The group, comprising 30 women and 44 men from 47 families, crossed the Rwanda-Burundi border at Nemba in Bugesera District. Sixty-two had been living in Mahama Camp in Kirehe District, while the remaining 12 resided in Kigali City.
The returnees were formally handed over to Burundian authorities, with representatives from the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs (MINEMA) and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) accompanying them.
Jérémie Havugiyaremye, who spent 25 years in Rwanda, shared his experience: “Life in the camp was not easy, but I had no problems in Rwanda. My family in the camp is not ready to return yet, but I miss my country and want to start a new life there.” Havugiyaremye added that the decision to return was influenced by friends who had found their homeland safe.
Similarly, Oda Mariya, who had fled the 2015 unrest in Burundi and lived in Mahama Camp for 11 years, said, “I came back because peace has returned and our comrades encouraged us. I wanted to reunite with my family and live well.”
Karagire Gonzague, Director of Refugee Programs at MINEMA, noted that since 2020, over 31,000 Burundians have returned home voluntarily, with strong cooperation from Burundian authorities. “In 2022, Burundian representatives visited Mahama Camp and Kigali to encourage refugees to return. Last year, online discussions were also held to explain the benefits of repatriation,” he said.
These 74 returnees add to 115 others who returned in November 2025. MINEMA reports that over 50,000 Burundian refugees still remain in Rwanda, living in camps and urban areas.

title: 205 Rwandans Return Home from DRC
excerpt: Rubavu, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Rwanda welcomed 205 of its citizens who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), as they voluntarily returned home on Thursday, 12 March 2026. The returnees crossed the Rwanda-DRC border in Rubavu District, where they were receive
title_en: 205 Rwandans Return Home from DRC
excerpt_en: Rubavu, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Rwanda welcomed 205 of its citizens who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), as they voluntarily returned home on Thursday, 12 March 2026. The returnees crossed the Rwanda-DRC border in Rubavu District, where they were receive
body_en:
Rubavu, Rwanda, 12 March 2026 - Rwanda welcomed 205 of its citizens who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), as they voluntarily returned home on Thursday, 12 March 2026.
The returnees crossed the Rwanda-DRC border in Rubavu District, where they were received by District Commissioner Ishimwe Pacifique, responsible for social welfare.
The majority of those returning were women and children born in the DRC. Many said they decided to come back after encouragement from colleagues who had returned earlier, aiming to rebuild their lives and pursue development.
Several of the returnees had been held hostage by FDLR fighters operating in the forests of eastern DRC. Since the AFC/M23 coalition gained control over parts of the region, security conditions have improved, allowing Rwandans to return safely with support from the UN Refugee Agency.
The initiative reflects ongoing efforts to assist citizens stranded abroad and facilitate their reintegration into Rwandan society.

The returnees crossed the Rwanda-DRC border in Rubavu District, where they were received by District Commissioner Ishimwe Pacifique, responsible for social welfare.
The majority of those returning were women and children born in the DRC. Many said they decided to come back after encouragement from colleagues who had returned earlier, aiming to rebuild their lives and pursue development.

The initiative reflects ongoing efforts to assist citizens stranded abroad and facilitate their reintegration into Rwandan society.

excerpt_en: Montego Bay, Jamaica, 13 March 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) has concluded a 60-day humanitarian mission in Montego Bay, leaving a lasting impact on communities devastated by Cyclone Melissa. Deployed in collaboration with the Jamaican Defence Force (JDF), a contingent of
body_en:
Montego Bay, Jamaica, 13 March 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) has concluded a 60-day humanitarian mission in Montego Bay, leaving a lasting impact on communities devastated by Cyclone Melissa.
Deployed in collaboration with the Jamaican Defence Force (JDF), a contingent of 100 Rwandan soldiers worked to repair and rebuild damaged infrastructure in St James Province, following a disaster that claimed 45 lives and caused destruction equivalent to 45% of Jamaica’s GDP.
Many residents, encountering Rwanda for the first time, expressed deep gratitude for the support. “You came all the way from Africa to help us. I thank you from the bottom of my heart,” said one local resident. Another added, “I didn’t know how I would rebuild, but what you have done is incredible. God bless you.”
The Chief of the Jamaican Armed Forces, Vice Admiral Antonette Wemyss-Gorman, praised the RDF soldiers for their professionalism and discipline. “They are dedicated, efficient, and true professionals. In just two months, they have achieved a great deal and built strong ties with the community,” she said, noting the absence of any misconduct during their deployment.
She also emphasized the importance of strengthening bilateral relations between Rwanda and Jamaica, highlighting that the support provided would not be forgotten.
Colonel Moses Kayigamba, head of the RDF contingent, said Rwanda’s commitment to humanitarian action is rooted in its own history. “We take any suffering as our own,” he stated, referencing the country’s past and its determination to assist others in times of need.
The mission followed the devastating cyclone that struck Jamaica on October 28, 2025, with winds reaching 298 km/h, severely impacting St Elizabeth and Black River regions. According to humanitarian data, the disaster damaged 450 schools and over 120,000 homes, affecting 626,000 people, with hundreds left homeless.
The RDF’s intervention has been widely seen as a symbol of solidarity and international cooperation, reinforcing Rwanda’s growing role in global humanitarian and peace support operations.

title: Wazalendo Expels MP Willy Mishiki After Goma Attack Admission
excerpt: Goma, 14 March 2026 - The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma. Mishiki, who represented Walika
title_en: Wazalendo Expels MP Willy Mishiki After Goma Attack Admission
excerpt_en: Goma, 14 March 2026 - The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma. Mishiki, who represented Walika
body_en:
Goma, 14 March 2026 - The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma.
Mishiki, who represented Walikale territory in the DRC Parliament and served as President of the Council of Experts within the coalition, made the remarks during an interview with TV5 Monde on 11 March 2026.
In the interview, he stated that Wazalendo forces were fighting in Virunga National Park and had advanced to Nyiragongo, just a few kilometers from Goma, with the objective of retaking the city. He also acknowledged responsibility for the drone attack carried out in Goma in the early hours of 11 March, which killed three civilians, including French national Karine Buisset, an employee of UNICEF.
“We are fighting to retake Goma… that is the reason for this attack,” Mishiki said.
Following the statement, the CNVDP-WAZ leadership announced on 13 March that Mishiki had acted without consultation and had escalated tensions through his remarks. As a result, he was removed from his position and stripped of membership, with Katulanya Jacques appointed as his replacement.
Reacting to the development, Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, said that dismissing Mishiki does not negate his admission. “You cannot erase a confession, especially when it is supported by evidence,” he stated.
Meanwhile, the French government has announced an investigation into the attack that killed one of its nationals.
The AFC/M23 coalition has also weighed in, alleging that the attack was carried out by DRC government forces, claiming it targeted political and military figures including Joseph Kabila, Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki, and Gen. Maj. Sultani Makenga.
The incident underscores the complex and contested narratives surrounding the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, particularly in and around Goma, where multiple armed groups and political actors remain active.

title: Equity Bank Rwanda Reassures Clients After Attempted Fraud Incident
excerpt: Kigali, 15 March 2026 - Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026. In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly iden
title_en: Equity Bank Rwanda Reassures Clients After Attempted Fraud Incident
excerpt_en: Kigali, 15 March 2026 - Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026. In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly iden
body_en:
Kigali, 15 March 2026 - Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026.
In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly identified unusual transactions, triggering immediate security protocols to contain the situation.
“Our systems continuously monitor irregular money transfers, and appropriate security measures were promptly activated,” the statement said.
The bank confirmed that swift intervention enabled the recovery of most of the targeted funds within 24 hours, while investigations continue in collaboration with relevant authorities, including the Central Bank of Rwanda and security agencies.
Equity Bank emphasized that no customer funds were lost, adding that all banking operations remain normal. “Customer accounts are fully protected, and services continue without disruption,” the bank stated.
Ongoing Investigation and Security Measures
The institution reiterated its zero-tolerance policy on financial crime, highlighting ongoing efforts to strengthen cybersecurity systems, enhance transaction monitoring, and reinforce internal controls.
Customers and stakeholders have also been encouraged to report any suspicious activities through the bank’s confidential whistleblowing channels, as part of broader efforts to maintain transparency and accountability.
Rising Cybersecurity Concerns
The incident comes amid growing concerns over cybercrime targeting financial institutions globally, prompting banks to invest heavily in advanced security technologies and closer cooperation with regulators.
Equity Bank Rwanda reaffirmed its commitment to protecting client assets and maintaining high standards of financial security as investigations into the attempted fraud continue.

title: FARDC and Wazalendo Block Key Bukavu-Uvira Road in South Kivu
excerpt: South Kivu, 16 March 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), in coordination with Wazalendo armed groups, have closed the RN5 road linking Bukavu and Uvira, disrupting transport and trade in the region. The RN5 corridor, a vital route for movement of
title_en: FARDC and Wazalendo Block Key Bukavu-Uvira Road in South Kivu
excerpt_en: South Kivu, 16 March 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), in coordination with Wazalendo armed groups, have closed the RN5 road linking Bukavu and Uvira, disrupting transport and trade in the region. The RN5 corridor, a vital route for movement of
body_en:
South Kivu, 16 March 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), in coordination with Wazalendo armed groups, have closed the RN5 road linking Bukavu and Uvira, disrupting transport and trade in the region.
The RN5 corridor, a vital route for movement of people and goods, connects communities in the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira territory. The closure has left traders and travelers stranded, raising concerns over the economic and humanitarian impact.
On the morning of 15 March 2026, traders traveling from Runingu to Sange were turned back by security forces. Reports indicate that passengers heading from Bukavu toward Uvira and the Ruzizi Valley were blocked and forced to gather at Sange, awaiting further instructions.
After hours of uncertainty, authorities informed residents that no vehicles, motorcycles, or pedestrians would be allowed to access Uvira from areas under the control of the AFC/M23 coalition.
Security Justification, Public Frustration
Officials say the decision was taken to maintain security in zones under government and allied control. However, many residents have expressed confusion and frustration, arguing that authorities should instead strengthen protection measures while allowing economic activities to continue.
The RN5 road had briefly resumed operations between December 2025 and January 2026, during a period when AFC/M23 forces controlled parts of the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira. Since their withdrawal in mid-January, traffic has significantly declined, with travelers forced to navigate areas controlled by opposing factions.
The latest closure highlights the ongoing instability in eastern DRC, where shifting control between armed groups continues to disrupt daily life, trade, and mobility for local populations.

title: Rwanda Defence Forces Return from Jamaica Mission
excerpt: Kigali, 16 March 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) team of engineers has returned to Kigali after completing a mission in Jamaica to assist with repairs of infrastructure and houses damaged by Cyclone Melissa. The team arrived at Kigali International Airport on Monday mornin
title_en: Rwanda Defence Forces Return from Jamaica Mission
excerpt_en: Kigali, 16 March 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) team of engineers has returned to Kigali after completing a mission in Jamaica to assist with repairs of infrastructure and houses damaged by Cyclone Melissa. The team arrived at Kigali International Airport on Monday mornin
body_en:
Kigali, 16 March 2026 - The Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) team of engineers has returned to Kigali after completing a mission in Jamaica to assist with repairs of infrastructure and houses damaged by Cyclone Melissa.
The team arrived at Kigali International Airport on Monday morning, concluding a 60-day mission that began on 14 January 2026.
Welcoming them, the Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Maj Alex Kagame, praised the soldiers for their dedication, professionalism, and teamwork. “The RDF culture and values were very clear. We have not heard anything negative from them during their time in Jamaica. Please give them a round of applause,” he said.
During the mission, RDF personnel focused on repairing infrastructure and homes in Montego Bay, Province of St James, earning appreciation from local residents.
The Chief of Defence Staff of Jamaica, Vice Admiral Antonette Wemyss-Gorman, commended the RDF for their work. “They are sincere, professional, and have done a lot in a short time. They spent time with the community and have not caused any issues. We are very proud of these peacekeepers,” she said.
Vice Admiral Wemyss-Gorman emphasized that the collaboration would continue to strengthen the relationship between Rwanda and Jamaica. “The people you helped will not forget the RDF under President Kagame’s leadership. We will continue working to preserve this good relationship,” she added.

title_en: Rwandan Security Forces Support Education in Mozambique
excerpt_en: Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, 16 March 2026 - Rwandan Security Forces deployed in Cabo Delgado Province have donated school supplies to students at Buji Primary School, in collaboration with local authorities, as part of ongoing efforts to support communities affected by conflict. Th
body_en:
Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, 16 March 2026 - Rwandan Security Forces deployed in Cabo Delgado Province have donated school supplies to students at Buji Primary School, in collaboration with local authorities, as part of ongoing efforts to support communities affected by conflict.
The donation, made on 16 March 2026, will benefit 525 students at the school, located in Mocímboa da Praia District.
School principal Lahaia Tomé expressed gratitude for the continued support, noting its positive impact on both the school and the wider community. The district’s Director of Education, Salmo Bacary, also praised the initiative, highlighting the role of Rwandan forces not only in restoring security but also in supporting the education sector.
This contribution follows a similar project earlier in March, when Rwandan forces handed over a newly renovated school building in Macomia District. The facility, which includes three classrooms and two offices, was completed in three months after construction had been halted due to terrorist attacks, and now serves 150 students.
Lt Col Frank Rwabugande, in charge of civil-military relations, said the initiative reflects a broader commitment to promoting education and strengthening ties with local communities. “This school is not just a building, but a symbol of unity and cooperation between the people of Rwanda and Mozambique,” he said.
Since July 2021, Rwandan and Mozambican security forces have worked together to combat insurgent groups in Cabo Delgado, restoring stability in areas previously affected by violence. The improved security situation has enabled displaced residents to return home and allowed the gradual restoration of basic services, including infrastructure and electricity.

title: Jamaica Praises Rwandan Forces for Post-Cyclone Relief Efforts

title_en: Jamaica Praises Rwandan Forces for Post-Cyclone Relief Efforts
excerpt_en: Kingston, 17 March 2026 - The Jamaican Armed Forces have expressed gratitude to the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) for their contribution to recovery efforts following the devastation caused by Cyclone Melissa. The storm, which struck in October 2025, killed 45 people and left more
body_en:
Kingston, 17 March 2026 - The Jamaican Armed Forces have expressed gratitude to the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) for their contribution to recovery efforts following the devastation caused by Cyclone Melissa.
The storm, which struck in October 2025, killed 45 people and left more than 15 missing, according to humanitarian data. It also damaged 450 schools and over 120,000 homes, affecting more than 626,000 people.
In response, Rwanda deployed 100 military engineers in January 2026 to assist with rebuilding homes and infrastructure in affected areas, including Trelawny and St. James.
In a message shared publicly, the Jamaican military praised the Rwandan troops for their commitment and sacrifice. “We will not forget the work you did during one of the greatest disasters in our recent history,” the statement read.
Officials noted that the presence of the Rwandan forces helped restore hope among affected communities, highlighting the impact of rebuilding efforts on families who had lost their homes.
After completing a two-month mission, the RDF contingent, led by Col Moses Kayigamba, returned to Rwanda on 16 March 2026, where they were received by military leadership in Kigali.
Beyond reconstruction work, the Rwandan team also carried out community service activities, including cleaning and supporting the Blessed Assurance Children’s Home, which cares for children with disabilities.
The mission has been widely seen as a sign of growing cooperation and solidarity between Rwanda and Jamaica in times of crisis.

title: Agathon Rwasa Questions Burundi’s Military Role in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 - Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people. Speaking in an interview with a lo
title_en: Agathon Rwasa Questions Burundi’s Military Role in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 - Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people. Speaking in an interview with a lo
body_en:
Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 - Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people.
Speaking in an interview with a local media outlet, Rwasa said the deployment of Burundian troops is driven by the interests of the ruling CNDD-FDD party, rather than national priorities.
“I believe Burundi’s involvement in the Congo war serves the interests of the authorities, not the people,” he said.
Rwasa also questioned the manner in which Burundian troops are reportedly operating in the DRC, claiming that if their mission were legitimate, they would act openly under their own identity.
He further warned that the conflict risks escalating and spreading closer to Burundi’s borders, particularly given the instability in eastern DRC.
The Burundian government maintains that its troops were deployed to combat armed groups opposed to it, including RED Tabara, FOREBU, and FNL, which are said to operate in South Kivu.
However, Rwasa dismissed this justification, arguing that such operations do not explain the presence of Burundian forces in other areas, including North Kivu.
The remarks highlight ongoing debate within Burundi over its military engagement abroad, as the conflict in eastern DRC continues to draw in regional actors.

title: Former U.S. Official Questions DRC’s Commitment to Neutralizing FDLR
excerpt: Washington, 20 March 2026 - Former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, Tibor Nagy, has expressed skepticism over the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s willingness to dismantle the FDLR armed group, a key condition in ongoing regional peace efforts. The remarks
title_en: Former U.S. Official Questions DRC’s Commitment to Neutralizing FDLR
excerpt_en: Washington, 20 March 2026 - Former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, Tibor Nagy, has expressed skepticism over the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s willingness to dismantle the FDLR armed group, a key condition in ongoing regional peace efforts. The remarks
body_en:
Washington, 20 March 2026 - Former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, Tibor Nagy, has expressed skepticism over the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s willingness to dismantle the FDLR armed group, a key condition in ongoing regional peace efforts.
The remarks come amid renewed diplomatic engagement between Rwanda and the DRC following a peace agreement signed in Washington on 27 June 2025, with U.S. support. The accord includes provisions for the neutralization of the FDLR and the eventual lifting of Rwanda’s security measures.
Although both countries ratified the agreement in December 2025 and recently recommitted to its implementation during talks held on 17-18 March 2026, progress remains limited.
Nagy argued that lasting peace in eastern DRC depends on concrete action against the FDLR, which Rwanda considers a major security threat. “It would be good to issue another joint peace declaration… but it all starts with Congo dismantling the FDLR,” he said, adding that he doubts Kinshasa’s willingness or ability to do so.
Rwanda has maintained that its security measures will remain in place until the group is effectively neutralized.
The ongoing stalemate highlights the challenges facing regional diplomacy, as both sides seek to balance security concerns and political commitments under the Washington peace framework.

excerpt_en: Uvira, 20 March 2026 - Fighting has resumed between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) and the AFC/M23 coalition in parts of the Ruzizi Valley, marking the end of a two-month lull in hostilities. The renewed clashes come shortly after Congolese force
body_en:
Uvira, 20 March 2026 - Fighting has resumed between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) and the AFC/M23 coalition in parts of the Ruzizi Valley, marking the end of a two-month lull in hostilities.
The renewed clashes come shortly after Congolese forces, supported by Wazalendo groups, closed the RN5 road linking Uvira and Bukavu, citing security concerns.
According to political analyst Tite Gatabazi, the AFC/M23 resumed combat following what it described as attacks on its positions. He added that the group also claims to be responding to violence targeting certain communities in the region.
Gatabazi suggested that the rebels retain significant operational capacity and could potentially attempt to advance toward Uvira town, particularly amid concerns over the current security situation.
The resurgence of fighting highlights ongoing instability in eastern DRC, despite recent diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions and advancing peace agreements.

title: 18 Migrants Killed in Boat Tragedy off Comoros Coast
excerpt: Mitsamiouli, Comoros, 20 March 2026 - At least 18 migrants have died after a boat capsized off the coast of the Comoros while attempting to reach the French-administered island of Mayotte. According to Comoros Security Minister Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani, the accident occurred durin
title_en: 18 Migrants Killed in Boat Tragedy off Comoros Coast
excerpt_en: Mitsamiouli, Comoros, 20 March 2026 - At least 18 migrants have died after a boat capsized off the coast of the Comoros while attempting to reach the French-administered island of Mayotte. According to Comoros Security Minister Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani, the accident occurred durin
body_en:
Mitsamiouli, Comoros, 20 March 2026 - At least 18 migrants have died after a boat capsized off the coast of the Comoros while attempting to reach the French-administered island of Mayotte.
According to Comoros Security Minister Mohamed Ahmed Assoumani, the accident occurred during the night of 18-19 March in the Mitsamiouli area. The victims included 16 nationals from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and two from Burundi.
The vessel was reportedly carrying 51 people, who had departed from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, on a week-long journey toward Mayotte.
Following the accident, local residents and fishermen launched rescue efforts, managing to save 33 survivors, who were transported to a nearby hospital.
Authorities praised the swift response of the community. “Their lives were saved thanks to collective action and rapid intervention,” Assoumani said.
The United Nations Resident Coordinator in the Comoros, James Bot, attributed such incidents to human trafficking networks that exploit migrants by promising safe passage but abandoning them at sea.
He called for stronger regional cooperation, particularly between Comoros and Tanzania, to address the root causes of irregular migration and prevent further tragedies.
The accident underscores the ongoing risks faced by migrants attempting dangerous sea crossings in search of better opportunities.

title: Former Armed Group Members Repatriated from DRC Confront Genocide History in Rwanda
excerpt: Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A group of 244 individuals, largely former members of armed groups operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo, have undergone a civic and historical re-education program in Rwanda aimed at countering long-held extremist narratives and facilitating rein
title_en: Former Armed Group Members Repatriated from DRC Confront Genocide History in Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A group of 244 individuals, largely former members of armed groups operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo, have undergone a civic and historical re-education program in Rwanda aimed at countering long-held extremist narratives and facilitating rein
body_en:
Kigali, March 21, 2026 - A group of 244 individuals, largely former members of armed groups operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo, have undergone a civic and historical re-education program in Rwanda aimed at countering long-held extremist narratives and facilitating reintegration into society.
The group, which includes ex-combatants linked to the FDLR as well as their families, recently returned to Rwanda and participated in guided visits to key historical sites. These included the Kigali Genocide Memorial and the Campaign Against Genocide Museum, where they were introduced to the history and consequences of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
According to Rwanda’s National Demobilization and Reintegration Commission (RDRC), 173 of the returnees are former fighters, while the remainder are their spouses and children. A significant proportion-173 individuals-were born in the DRC, while 71 were born in Rwanda. The group is predominantly male, with 216 men among them.
The visits, held on March 20, form part of a broader reintegration program conducted at the Mutobo Demobilization Center in Musanze District. The initiative is designed to prepare returnees for civilian life, with completion expected by the end of March.
RDRC Chairperson Valérie Nyirahabineza said the inclusion of historical education marks a shift in the commission’s approach. She emphasized that many of the younger returnees, particularly those born in the DRC, had been exposed to distorted narratives about Rwanda and its history.
“In the past, most returnees had firsthand knowledge of the Genocide against the Tutsi,” she noted. “Today, many of these young people were born outside Rwanda and have grown up hearing falsehoods. It is essential that they see and understand the truth for themselves.”
Nyirahabineza added that discussions with the group revealed a widespread lack of awareness about the planning, execution, and aftermath of the genocide. She said the visits aim not only to inform but also to foster a sense of responsibility and encourage participation in national unity and remembrance programs.
Among the returnees is Mbare Amoni, who fled Rwanda as a child in 1994 and later joined the FDLR at age 25. He described harsh living conditions in eastern DRC and recounted fighting alongside the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) before being pushed back by M23 rebels near Goma.
Amoni said his decision to return was influenced by contact with a former combatant who had already reintegrated. Reflecting on his visit to the memorial sites, he expressed shock at the historical realities presented, noting that they contradicted what he had long believed.
He also remarked on Rwanda’s development, saying it differed significantly from the image portrayed within armed groups. “What I saw here challenged everything we were told,” he said, adding that the experience, though difficult, was eye-opening.
Another participant, 25-year-old Ntakirutimana Faustin, born in the DRC, said he had never joined the FDLR but lived among its members and was influenced by their ideology. He explained that he grew up hearing that the group’s goal was to return to Rwanda and seize power.
Visiting Rwanda for the first time, Faustin described the country as “beautiful” and said learning about the Genocide against the Tutsi helped him reassess the beliefs he had held for years.
Authorities say such programs are critical in addressing the legacy of armed conflict and extremist indoctrination among returnees, particularly younger generations raised outside Rwanda.

According to Rwanda’s National Demobilization and Reintegration Commission (RDRC), 173 of the returnees are former fighters, while the remainder are their spouses and children. A significant proportion-173 individuals-were born in the DRC, while 71 were born in Rwanda. The group is predominantly male, with 216 men among them.
The visits, held on March 20, form part of a broader reintegration program conducted at the Mutobo Demobilization Center in Musanze District. The initiative is designed to prepare returnees for civilian life, with completion expected by the end of March.
RDRC Chairperson Valérie Nyirahabineza said the inclusion of historical education marks a shift in the commission’s approach. She emphasized that many of the younger returnees, particularly those born in the DRC, had been exposed to distorted narratives about Rwanda and its history.
“In the past, most returnees had firsthand knowledge of the Genocide against the Tutsi,” she noted. “Today, many of these young people were born outside Rwanda and have grown up hearing falsehoods. It is essential that they see and understand the truth for themselves.”
Nyirahabineza added that discussions with the group revealed a widespread lack of awareness about the planning, execution, and aftermath of the genocide. She said the visits aim not only to inform but also to foster a sense of responsibility and encourage participation in national unity and remembrance programs.
Among the returnees is Mbare Amoni, who fled Rwanda as a child in 1994 and later joined the FDLR at age 25. He described harsh living conditions in eastern DRC and recounted fighting alongside the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) before being pushed back by M23 rebels near Goma.
Amoni said his decision to return was influenced by contact with a former combatant who had already reintegrated. Reflecting on his visit to the memorial sites, he expressed shock at the historical realities presented, noting that they contradicted what he had long believed.
He also remarked on Rwanda’s development, saying it differed significantly from the image portrayed within armed groups. “What I saw here challenged everything we were told,” he said, adding that the experience, though difficult, was eye-opening.
Another participant, 25-year-old Ntakirutimana Faustin, born in the DRC, said he had never joined the FDLR but lived among its members and was influenced by their ideology. He explained that he grew up hearing that the group’s goal was to return to Rwanda and seize power.
Visiting Rwanda for the first time, Faustin described the country as “beautiful” and said learning about the Genocide against the Tutsi helped him reassess the beliefs he had held for years.
Authorities say such programs are critical in addressing the legacy of armed conflict and extremist indoctrination among returnees, particularly younger generations raised outside Rwanda.

title: Mob Killing in Kyankwanzi After Discovery of Human Remains Sparks Fear

title_en: Mob Killing in Kyankwanzi After Discovery of Human Remains Sparks Fear
excerpt_en: Kyankwanzi District Uganda, March 21, 2026 - Tensions are high in central Uganda’s Kyankwanzi District after two men suspected to be Rwandan nationals were killed by an angry mob following the discovery of human body parts in their home. The incident occurred on March 20 in Kirya
body_en:
Kyankwanzi District Uganda, March 21, 2026 - Tensions are high in central Uganda’s Kyankwanzi District after two men suspected to be Rwandan nationals were killed by an angry mob following the discovery of human body parts in their home.
The incident occurred on March 20 in Kiryanongo village, Bananywa, where residents reportedly forced their way into the house of the two men, identified as Semasaka and Hakiza Damascene, after noticing a strong, foul odor coming from the premises.
According to local accounts, villagers conducted a search of the house and discovered dismembered body parts believed to belong to a woman from Nakabugo village who had been reported missing several days earlier. Some of the remains were allegedly found in a bag inside the residence.
The discovery triggered outrage among residents, who then turned on the two men, beating them to death before authorities could intervene.
Local leaders alerted police shortly after the killings. Officers from Bananywa Police Station, along with district-level investigators, were deployed to the scene to begin inquiries into both the suspected murder and the mob violence.
Luke Kigozi, the police spokesperson for Wamala Region, condemned the incident, stressing that the law must take its course.
He confirmed that investigations are underway into the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death, as well as the mob action that led to the killing of the two suspects.
The bodies of the two men and the deceased woman have been transported to Ntwetwe Health Center for post-mortem examinations as part of the ongoing investigation.
Authorities have urged residents to refrain from taking justice into their own hands, warning that such actions undermine the rule of law and complicate criminal investigations.

excerpt: Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 - The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated. The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa,
title_en: AFC/M23 Denies Rumors of Withdrawal from Bukavu
excerpt_en: Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 - The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated. The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa,
body_en:
Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 - The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated.
The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa, the coalition’s Deputy Director for Political Affairs, suggesting that the group intended to withdraw from Bukavu to pave the way for lasting peace.
Responding on March 21, AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka described the statement as false, alleging it was circulated by the Democratic Republic of Congo government to divert attention from a recent attack in Goma.
Kanyuka emphasized that no false narrative could erase the memory of the March 11, 2026, attack in which French national Karine Buisset, employed by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), was killed.
AFC/M23 seized control of Bukavu in February 2025. Speculation about a potential withdrawal has grown since the coalition pulled out of Uvira in January 2026, but the group insists its position in Bukavu remains unchanged.

title: ADF Attacks in Ituri Kill 50 in One Week
excerpt: Mambasa, Ituri, March 21, 2026 - The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) terrorist group has killed 50 people in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo over the course of a single week, local sources report. According to a civil society organization
title_en: ADF Attacks in Ituri Kill 50 in One Week
excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri, March 21, 2026 - The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) terrorist group has killed 50 people in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo over the course of a single week, local sources report. According to a civil society organization
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri, March 21, 2026 - The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) terrorist group has killed 50 people in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo over the course of a single week, local sources report.
According to a civil society organization operating in Ituri, 35 people were killed in Muchacha and 15 in Babesua between March 9 and 15. The attacks also involved the burning of multiple homes and widespread looting of property.
The violence has forced residents of several villages along the main RN4 road to flee to Mambasa and Niania centers, where they now live in precarious conditions, with agriculture and mining-the primary livelihoods in the region-disrupted.
The organization called on the DRC government to prioritize security in Ituri and mount stronger operations against the ADF, similar to efforts targeting the AFC/M23 coalition in North and South Kivu.
“The DRC government should urgently address the security situation in Ituri, which undermines governance, and undertake extensive operations against the ADF while assisting the people of Mambasa who are in immediate danger,” a spokesperson said.
Reports, including those from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), confirm that the ADF remains the deadliest armed group in the country, responsible for the highest number of killings in the DRC.
